We consider the global Morrey-type spaces {GM}_{p(.),\theta(.),w(.

title: Thermal WIMPs and the Scale of New Physics: Global Fits of Dirac Dark Matter Effective Field Theories Journal: Eur. Phys. J. C
creator: The GAMBIT Collaboration: Peter Athron monash,nanjing, Neal Avis Kozar mcdonald,queens, Csaba Balázs monash, Ankit Beniwal louvain,a, Sanjay Bloor imperial,uq,b, Torsten Bringmann oslo, Joachim Brod cincy, Christopher Chang uq, Jonathan M. Cornell wsu, Ben Farmer bom, Andrew Fowlie nanjing, Tomás E.
description: Abstract We assess the status of a wide class of WIMP dark matter (DM) models in light of the latest experimental results using the global fitting framework GAMBIT . We perform a global analysis of effective field theory (EFT) operators describing the interactions between a gauge-singlet Dirac fermion and the Standard Model quarks, the gluons and the photon.

title: Factorials and powers, a minimality result, revisited
creator: David E. Radford
description: Abstract Let a > 1 a>1 . Then a n < n ! a^{n}<n! for some positive integer n n . There are several numerical sequences associated with the study of the smallest such integer which are studied in [ 2 ] and [ 3 ] . Here we continue the examination of one of them.

title: Rotor Thermal Monitoring Scheme for Direct-Torque-Controlled Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machines via High-Frequency Rotating Flux or Torque Injection Thanks: S. Zhang, S. Li, and T. G. Habetler are with the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Georgia Institute of Technology
creator: Shen Zhang, Sufei Li, Lijun He
description: Abstract Interior permanent magnet synchronous machine drives are widely employed in electric traction systems and various industrial processes. However, prolonged exposure to high temperatures while operating can demagnetize the permanent magnets to the point of irreversible demagnetization. In addition, direct measurements with infrared sensors or contact-type sensors with wireless communication can be expensive and intrusive to the motor drive systems.

title: Online test administration results in students selecting more responses to multiple-choice-multiple-response items
creator: Alexis Olsho, Trevor I. Smith, Philip Eaton, Charlotte Zimmerman, Andrew Boudreaux, Suzanne White Brahmia
description: Abstract Multiple-choice multiple-response (MCMR) items (i.e., multiple-choice questions for which more than one response may be selected) can be a valuable tool for assessment. Like traditional multiple-choice single-response questions, they are easy to score, but MCMR items can provide more information about student thinking by probing multiple reasoning facets in a single problem context.

title: Probabilistic Discriminative Models Address the Tactile Perceptual Aliasing Problem
creator: John Lloyd, Yijiong Lin and Nathan F. Lepora Department of Engineering Mathematics and Bristol Robotics Laboratory, University of Bristol, U.K. Email: {jl15313, yijiong.lin, n.lepora}@bristol.ac.uk
description: Abstract In this paper, our aim is to highlight Tactile Perceptual Aliasing as a problem when using deep neural networks and other discriminative models. Perceptual aliasing will arise wherever a physical variable extracted from tactile data is subject to ambiguity between stimuli that are physically distinct.

title: The Weyl problem for unbounded convex domains in ℍ 3 {\mathbb{H}}^{3} Thanks: Partially supported by FNR project O20/14766753.
creator: Jean-Marc Schlenker
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jean-Marc Schlenker. Let K ⊂ ℍ 3 K\subset{\mathbb{H}}^{3} be a convex subset in ℍ 3 {\mathbb{H}}^{3} with smooth, strictly convex boundary. The induced metric on ∂ K \partial K then has curvature K > − 1 K>-1 . It was proved by Alexandrov that if K K is bounded, then it is uniquely determined by the induced metric on the boundary, and any smooth metric with curvature K > − 1 K>-1 can be obtained.

title: The Power Spectrum of Cosmological Number Densities
creator: Amanda R. Lopes, Marcelo B. Ribeiro, William R. Stoeger
description: Abstract This paper studies the cosmological power spectrum (PS) of the differential and integral galaxy volume number densities, respectively \gamma_{i} and \gamma_{i}^{*} , constructed with the cosmological distances d_{i} (i={\scriptstyle A},{\scriptstyle G},{\scriptstyle L},{\scriptstyle Z}) , where d_{\scriptscriptstyle A} is the angular diameter distance, d_{\scriptscriptstyle G} is the galaxy area distance, d_{\scriptscriptstyle L} is the luminosity distance and d_{z} is the

title: More Counterexamples to the Unit Conjecture for Group Rings
creator: Alan G. Murray
description: Abstract . Extending the discovery by Giles Gardam of a concrete counterexample to Kaplansky’s unit conjecture in characteristic 2, a family of counterexamples for every prime characteristic is presented. 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification 20C07 (16S34, 16U60) 1. Background Consider the group ring K[G] , where K is a field and G is a torsion-free group.

title: Demystifying Quantum Mechanics
creator: Ana Elisa D. Barioni, Felipe B. Mazzi, Elsa Bifano Pimenta, Willian Vieira dos Santos, Marco A. P. Lima
description: Abstract Why does such a successful theory like Quantum Mechanics have so many mysteries? The history of this theory is replete with dubious interpretations and controversies, and yet a knowledge of its predictions, however, contributed to the amazing technological revolution of the last hundred years.

title: Gradient Boosted Binary Histogram Ensemble for Large-scale Regression
creator: Hanyuan Hang h.hang@utwente.nl
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Hanyuan Hang h.hang@utwente.nl. In this paper, we propose a gradient boosting algorithm for large-scale regression problems called Gradient Boosted Binary Histogram Ensemble (GBBHE) based on binary histogram partition and ensemble learning. From the theoretical perspective, by assuming the Hölder continuity of the target function, we establish the statistical convergence rate of GBBHE in the space C 0 , α C^{0,\alpha} and C 1 , 0 C^{1,0} , where a lower bound of the convergence rate for the base learner demonstrates the advantage of boosting.

title: Approximation Algorithms for Min-Distance Problems in DAGs Corrected version.
creator: Mina Dalirrooyfard, Jenny Kaufmann
description: Abstract Graph parameters such as the diameter, radius, and vertex eccentricities are not defined in a useful way in Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs) using the standard measure of distance, since for any two nodes, there is no path between them in one of the two directions.

title: Time-dependent relations between gaps and returns in a Bitcoin order book
creator: Roberto Mota Navarro, Paulino Monroy Castillero, Francois Leyvraz
description: Abstract Several studies have shown that large changes in the returns of an asset are associated with the sized of the gaps present in the order book In general, these associations have been studied without explicitly considering the dynamics of either gaps or returns. Here we present a study of these relationships.

title: Gravitational Decoupling algorithm modifies the value of the conserved charges and thermodynamics properties in Lovelock Unique Vacuum theory.
creator: Milko Estrada
description: Abstract We provide an extension of the Gravitational Decoupling (algorithm) for the Lovelock theory with Unique Vacuum (LUV), which represents a simple way to solve the equations of motion. Due to the application of this algorithm, the energy of the system splits in the energy of the seed solution and the energy of each quasi-LUV sector .

title: Black String Thermal Equilibrium
creator: João Chakrian, Antônio de Pádua Santos
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by João Chakrian, Antônio de Pádua Santos. The black string solution is a model of black holes in (3+1) dimensions that can be related to the BTZ (2+1) dimensions black hole solution. This object can be seen as a cylindrical black hole. In this work it is considered the black string Hawking temperature obtained by the Hamilton-Jacobi method and a description of a system composed by a black string and a thermal reservoir, considering the thermal equilibrium state.

title: PRIMALITY OF WEAKLY CONNECTED COLLECTIONS OF CELLS AND WEAKLY CLOSED PATH POLYOMINOES
creator: CARMELO CISTO, FRANCESCO NAVARRA, ROSANNA UTANO
description: Abstract . In this paper we study the primality of weakly connected collections of cells, showing that the ideal generated by inner 2-minors attached to a weakly connected and simple collection of cells is the toric ideal of the edge ring of a weakly chordal bipartite graph.

title: A physical study of the LLL algorithm
creator: Jintai Ding, Seungki Kim, Tsuyoshi Takagi, Yuntao Wang, Bo-yin Yang
description: Abstract . This paper presents a study of the LLL algorithm from the perspective of statistical physics. Based on our experimental and theoretical results, we suggest that interpreting LLL as a sandpile model may help understand much of its mysterious behavior.

title: Distributed Symbolic Execution using Test-Depth Partitioning
creator: Shikhar Singh, Sarfraz Khurshid
description: Abstract Symbolic execution is a classic technique for systematic bug finding, which has seen many applications in recent years but remains hard to scale. Recent work introduced ranged symbolic execution to distribute the symbolic execution task among different workers with minimal communication overhead using test inputs. However, each worker was restricted to perform only a depth-first search.

title: A Continuous Paradoxical Colouring Rule Using Group Action
creator: Tuğkan Batu, Robert Simon, Grzegorz Tomkowicz
description: Abstract Given a probability space ( X , ℬ , m ) (X,{\cal B},m) , measure preserving transformations g 1 , … , g k g_{1},\dots,g_{k} of X X , and a colour set C C , a colouring rule is a way to colour the space with C C such that the colours allowed for a point x x

title: Learning from Counterfactual Links for Link Prediction
creator: Tong Zhao, Gang Liu, Daheng Wang, Wenhao Yu, Meng Jiang
description: Abstract Learning to predict missing links is important for many graph-based applications. Existing methods were designed to learn the association between observed graph structure and existence of link between a pair of nodes. However, the causal relationship between the two variables was largely ignored for learning to predict links on a graph.

title: Canonical Polynomial Sequences: Inverse Pairs
creator: Philip Feinsilver
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Philip Feinsilver. For V ⁡ ( z ) V(z) , analytic in a neighborhood of 0 ∈ ℂ 0\in\mathbb{C} , V ⁡ ( 0 ) = 0 V(0)=0 , V ′ ​ ( 0 ) ≠ 0 V^{\prime}(0)\neq 0 , there is an associated sequence of polynomials, canonical polynomials , that is a generalized Appell sequence with lowering operator V ⁡ ( d / d ​ x ) V(d/dx) .

title: Braids of the N N -body problem II: carousel solutions by cabling central configurations
creator: M. Fontaine, C. García-Azpeitia
description: Abstract Abstract. We prove the existence of relative periodic solutions of the planar N=\sum_{j=1}^{n}k_{j} -body problem starting with n bodies moving close to a non-degenerate central configuration and replacing each of them with clusters of k_{j} bodies that move close to a small central configuration. We name these solutions carousel solutions.

title: Detecting and Adapting to Novelty in Games
creator: Xiangyu Peng, Jonathan C. Balloch, Mark O. Riedl
description: Abstract Open-world novelty occurs when the rules of an environment can change abruptly, such as when a game player encounters “house rules”. To address open-world novelty, game playing agents must be able to detect when novelty is injected, and to quickly adapt to the new rules.

title: Finite Prime Distance Graphs and 2-Odd Graphs
creator: Joshua D. Laison, Colin Starr, Andrea Walker
description: Abstract A graph G G is a prime distance graph (respectively, a 2-odd graph) if its vertices can be labeled with distinct integers such that for any two adjacent vertices, the difference of their labels is prime (either 2 or odd).

title: Enabling Lightweight Fine-tuning for Pre-trained Language Model Compression based on Matrix Product Operators
creator: Peiyu Liu, Ze-Feng Gao, Wayne Xin Zhao, Z.Y. Xie, Zhong-Yi Lu, Ji-Rong Wen
description: Abstract This paper presents a novel pre-trained language models (PLM) compression approach based on the matrix product operator (short as MPO) from quantum many-body physics. It can decompose an original matrix into central tensors (containing the core information) and auxiliary tensors (with only a small proportion of parameters).

title: Influence of Roles in Decision-Making during OSS Development — A Study of Python Conference: Evaluation and Assessment in Software Engineering; June 21–23, 2021; Trondheim, Norway Evaluation and Assessment in Software Engineering (EASE 2021), June 21–23, 2021, Trondheim, Norway Price: 15.00 DOI: 10.
creator: Pankajeshwara Nand Sharma, Bastin Tony Roy Savarimuthu, Nigel Stanger
description: Abstract . Governance has been highlighted as a key factor in the success of an Open Source Software (OSS) project. It is generally seen that in a mixed meritocracy and autocracy governance model, the decision-making (DM) responsibility regarding what features are included in the OSS is shared among members from select roles; prominently the project leader.

title: Materials representation and transfer learning for multi-property prediction
creator: Shufeng Kong, Dan Guevarra, Carla P. Gomes, John M. Gregoire
description: Abstract The adoption of machine learning in materials science has rapidly transformed materials property prediction. Hurdles limiting full capitalization of recent advancements in machine learning include the limited development of methods to learn the underlying interactions of multiple elements, as well as the relationships among multiple properties, to facilitate property prediction in new composition spaces.

title: Language Scaling for Universal Suggested Replies Model
creator: Qianlan Ying, Payal Bajaj, Budhaditya Deb, Yu Yang, Wei Wang, Bojia Lin, Milad Shokouhi, Xia Song, Yang Yang, Daxin Jiang
description: Abstract We consider the problem of scaling automated suggested replies for Outlook email system to multiple languages. Faced with increased compute requirements and low resources for language expansion, we build a single universal model for improving the quality and reducing run-time costs of our production system. However, restricted data movement across regional centers prevents joint training across languages.

title: A unified view on symmetry, anomalous symmetry, and non-invertible gravitational anomaly
creator: Wenjie Ji, Xiao-Gang Wen
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Wenjie Ji, Xiao-Gang Wen. In this paper, using 1+1D models as examples, we study symmetries and anomalous symmetries via multi-component partition functions obtained through symmetry twists, and their transformations under the mapping class group of spacetime. This point of view allows us to treat symmetries and anomalous symmetries as non-invertible gravitational anomalies (which are also described by multi-component partition functions, transforming covariantly under the mapping group transformations).

title: Analysis of the robustness of NMF algorithms
description: Abstract We examine three non-negative matrix factorization techniques; L 2 L_{2} -norm, L 1 L_{1} -norm, and L 2 , 1 L_{2,1} -norm. Our aim is to establish the performance of these different approaches, and their robustness in real-world applications such as feature selection while managing computational complexity, sensitivity to noise and more.

title: Fluctuation-dissipation Type Theorem in Stochastic Linear Learning
creator: Manhyung Han, Jeonghyeok Park, Taewoong Lee, Jung Hoon Han
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Manhyung Han, Jeonghyeok Park, Taewoong Lee, Jung Hoon Han. The fluctuation-dissipation theorem (FDT) is a simple yet powerful consequence of the first-order differential equation governing the dynamics of systems subject simultaneously to dissipative and stochastic forces. The linear learning dynamics, in which the input vector maps to the output vector by a linear matrix whose elements are the subject of learning, has a stochastic version closely mimicking the Langevin dynamics when a full-batch gradient descent scheme is replaced by that of stochastic gradient descent.

title: Stochastic Iterative Graph Matching
creator: Linfeng Liu, Michael C. Hughes, Soha Hassoun, Li-Ping Liu
description: Abstract Recent works apply Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to graph matching tasks and show promising results. Considering that model outputs are complex matchings, we devise several techniques to improve the learning of GNNs and obtain a new model, Stochastic Iterative Graph MAtching (SIGMA).

title: Privately Learning Mixtures of Axis-Aligned Gaussians
creator: Ishaq Aden-Ali, Hassan Ashtiani, Christopher Liaw
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Ishaq Aden-Ali, Hassan Ashtiani, Christopher Liaw. We consider the problem of learning mixtures of Gaussians under the constraint of approximate differential privacy. We prove that O ~ ​ ( k 2 ​ d ​ log 3 / 2 ⁡ ( 1 / δ ) / α 2 ​ ε ) \widetilde{O}(k^{2}d\log^{3/2}(1/\delta)/\alpha^{2}\varepsilon) samples are sufficient to learn a mixture of k k axis-aligned Gaussians in ℝ d \mathbb{R}^{d} to within total variation distance α \alpha while satisfying ( ε , δ ) (\varepsilon,\delta) -differential privacy.

title: Towards offensive language detection and reduction in four Software Engineering communities Conference: Evaluation and Assessment in Software Engineering; June 21–23, 2021; Trondheim, Norway Evaluation and Assessment in Software Engineering (EASE 2021), June 21–23, 2021, Trondheim, Norway Price: 15.
creator: Jithin Cheriyan, Bastin Tony Roy Savarimuthu, Stephen Cranefield
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jithin Cheriyan, Bastin Tony Roy Savarimuthu, Stephen Cranefield. Software Engineering (SE) communities such as Stack Overflow have become unwelcoming, particularly through members’ use of offensive language. Research has shown that offensive language drives users away from active engagement within these platforms. This work aims to explore this issue more broadly by investigating the nature of offensive language in comments posted by users in four prominent SE platforms – GitHub, Gitter, Slack and Stack Overflow (SO).

title: Diagnosing Turbulence in the Neutral and Molecular Interstellar Medium of Galaxies
creator: Blakesley Burkhart
description: Abstract Magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) turbulence is a crucial component of the current paradigms of star formation, dynamo theory, particle transport, magnetic reconnection and evolution of structure in the interstellar medium (ISM) of galaxies. Despite the importance of turbulence to astrophysical fluids, a full theoretical framework based on solutions to the Navier-Stokes equations remains intractable.

title: The first non-static inhomogeneous exact solution in f ⁡ ( T , B ) f(T,B) gravity
creator: Sebastián Nájera, Aram Aguilar, Celia Escamilla-Rivera, Roberto A. Sussman
description: Abstract We examine in this paper the possibility of finding exact solutions for Teleparallel Gravity (TG) of the type of spherically symmetric Lemaître-Tolman-Bondi (LTB) dust models. We apply to the LTB metric, as obtained from the Schwarzschild solution in General Relativity, the formalism of Teleparallel Gravity in its extension to f ⁡ ( T , B ) f(T,B) models.

title: Repeat a physics course more than once: A diagnosis of the most frequent misconceptions in newtonian mechanics of first and second-year engineering students
creator: F. Escalante 1
description: Abstract In this work, we study a sample of 600 engineering students in three consecutive physics courses of different levels, according to their curriculum. We focus on the most frequent students’ misconceptions in newtonian mechanics. It was administered the FCI test at the beginning of the academic semester in each course.

title: Incremental formation of scale-free fitness networks
creator: Fabio Vanni
description: Abstract In the paper, we present an incremental approach in the construction of scale free networks with hidden variables. The work arises from the necessity to generate that type of networks with a given number of links instead of obtaining a random configurations for a given set of parameters as in the usual literature.

title: Over-the-Air Computation via Broadband Channels
creator: Tianrui Qin, Wanchun Liu, Branka Vucetic, Yonghui Li
description: Abstract † † The authors are with School of Electrical and Information Engineering, the University of Sydney, Australia. Emails: {tianrui.qin, wanchun.liu, branka.vucetic, yonghui.li}@sydney.edu.au. ( Wanchun Liu is the corresponding author. ) Over-the-air computation (AirComp) has been recognized as a low-latency solution for wireless sensor data fusion, where multiple sensors send their measurement signals to a receiver simultaneously for computation.

title: Deep Contextual Learners for Protein Networks
creator: Michelle M. Li, Marinka Zitnik
description: Abstract Spatial context is central to understanding health and disease. Yet reference protein interaction networks lack such contextualization, thereby limiting the study of where protein interactions likely occur in the human body and how they may be altered in disease. Contextualized protein interactions could better characterize genes with disease-specific interactions and elucidate diseases’ manifestation in specific cell types.

title: Discovery of Causal Additive Models in the Presence of Unobserved Variables
creator: Takashi Nicholas Maeda, Shohei Shimizu
description: Abstract Causal discovery from data affected by unobserved variables is an important but difficult problem to solve. The effects that unobserved variables have on the relationships between observed variables are more complex in nonlinear cases than in linear cases. In this study, we focus on causal additive models in the presence of unobserved variables.

title: Visual Question Rewriting for Increasing Response Rate Conference: Proceedings of the 44th International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval; July 11–15, 2021; Virtual Event, Canada. Proceedings of the 44th International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Deve
creator: Jiayi Wei, Xilian Li, Yi Zhang, Xin Eric Wang
description: Abstract . When a human asks questions online, or when a conversational virtual agent asks a human questions, questions triggering emotions or with details might more likely to get responses or answers. we explore how to automatically rewrite natural language questions to improve the response rate form people.

title: A General Method for Event Detection on Social Media
creator: Yihong Zhang, Masumi Shirakawa, Takahiro Hara
description: Abstract Event detection on social media has attracted a number of researches, given the recent availability of large volumes of social media discussions. Previous works on social media event detection either assume a specific type of event, or assume certain behavior of observed variables.

title: Using Social Media Background to Improve Cold-start Recommendation Deep Models
creator: Yihong Zhang, Takuya Maekawa, and Takahiro Hara
description: Abstract In recommender systems, a cold-start problem occurs when there is no past interaction record associated with the user or item. Typical solutions to the cold-start problem make use of contextual information, such as user demographic attributes or product descriptions.

title: Human-Adversarial Visual Question Answering
creator: Sasha Sheng, Amanpreet Singh, Vedanuj GoswamiJose Alberto Lopez Magana, Wojciech Galuba, Devi Parikh, Douwe Kiela
description: Abstract Performance on the most commonly used Visual Question Answering dataset (VQA v2) is starting to approach human accuracy. However, in interacting with state-of-the-art VQA models, it is clear that the problem is far from being solved. In order to stress test VQA models, we benchmark them against human-adversarial examples.

title: Gravitational waves from the remnants of the first stars in nuclear star clusters 2021 Gravitational waves from the remnants of the first stars in nuclear star clusters – References
creator: Boyuan Liu, Volker Bromm
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Boyuan Liu, Volker Bromm. We study Population III (Pop III) binary remnant mergers in nuclear star clusters (NSCs) with a semi-analytical approach for early structure formation. Within this framework, we keep track of the dynamics of Pop III binary (compact object) remnants during cosmic structure formation, and construct the population of Pop III binary remnants that fall into NSCs by dynamical friction of field stars. The subsequent evolution within NSCs is then derived from three-body encounters and gravitational-wave (GW) emission.

title: Bayesian inference on high-dimensional multivariate binary responses
creator: Antik Chakraborty, Rihui Ou, David B. Dunson
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Antik Chakraborty, Rihui Ou, David B. Dunson. It has become increasingly common to collect high-dimensional binary response data; for example, with the emergence of new sampling techniques in ecology. In smaller dimensions, multivariate probit (MVP) models are routinely used for inferences. However, algorithms for fitting such models face issues in scaling up to high dimensions due to the intractability of the likelihood, involving an integral over a multivariate normal distribution having no analytic form.

title: Tackling the Background Bias in Sparse Object Detection via Cropped Windows
creator: Leon Amadeus Varga, Andreas Zell
description: Abstract Object detection on Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) is still a challenging task. The recordings are mostly sparse and contain only small objects. In this work, we propose a simple tiling method that improves the detection capability in the remote sensing case. We identified one core component of many tiling approaches and extracted an easy to implement preprocessing step.

title: Many-body excitations in trapped Bose gas: A non-Hermitian view Thanks: The work of the second and third authors (DM and SS) was partially supported by Grant No. 1517162 of the Division of Mathematical Sciences (DMS) of the National Science Foundation (NSF).
creator: Manoussos G. Grillakis, Dionisios Margetis, Stephen Sorokanich
description: Abstract We provide the analysis of a physically motivated model for a trapped dilute Bose gas with repulsive pairwise atomic interactions at zero temperature. Our goal is to describe aspects of the excited many-body quantum states by accounting for the scattering of atoms in pairs from the macroscopic state (condensate).

title: Subdivision-Based Mesh Convolution Networks Journal: TOG CCS: Computing methodologies Neural networks CCS: Computing methodologies Shape analysis
creator: Shi-Min Hu, Zheng-Ning Liu, Meng-Hao Guo, Jun-Xiong Cai, Jiahui Huang, Tai-Jiang Mu, Ralph R. Martin
description: Abstract . Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have made great breakthroughs in 2D computer vision. However, their irregular structure makes it hard to harness the potential of CNNs directly on meshes. A subdivision surface provides a hierarchical multi-resolution structure, in which each face in a closed 2-manifold triangle mesh is exactly adjacent to three faces.

title: Thermodynamic uncertainty relation for underdamped dynamics driven by time-dependent protocols
creator: Chulan Kwon, Youngchae Kwon, Hyun Keun Lee
description: Abstract The thermodynamic uncertainty relation (TUR) for underdamped dynamics has intriguing problems while its counterpart for overdamped dynamics has recently been derived. Even for the case of steady states, a proper way to match underdamped and overdamped TURs has not been found.

title: The structure of the unit group of the group algebra F ⁡ ( C 3 × D 10 ) F(C_{3}\times D_{10})
creator: Meena Sahai, Sheere Farhat Ansari
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Meena Sahai, Sheere Farhat Ansari. Let D n D_{n} be the dihedral group of order n n . The structure of the unit group U ⁡ ( F ⁡ ( C 3 × D 10 ) ) U(F(C_{3}\times D_{10})) of the group algebra F ⁡ ( C 3 × D 10 ) F(C_{3}\times D_{10}) over a finite field F F of characteristic 3 3 is given in [ 11 ] .

title: Correlated insulators, semimetals, and superconductivity in twisted trilayer graphene
creator: Maine Christos, Subir Sachdev, Mathias S. Scheurer
description: Abstract Motivated by recent experiments indicating strong superconductivity and intricate correlated insulating and flavor-polarized physics in mirror-symmetric twisted trilayer graphene, we study the effects of interactions in this system close to the magic angle, using a combination of analytical and numerical methods.

title: Discrete time crystals in Bose-Einstein Condensates and symmetry-breaking edge in a simple two-mode theory
creator: Jia Wang, Krzysztof Sacha, Peter Hannaford, Bryan J. Dalton
description: Abstract Discrete time crystals (DTCs) refer to a novel many-body steady state that spontaneously breaks the discrete time-translational symmetry in a periodically-driven quantum system. Here, we study DTCs in a Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) bouncing resonantly on an oscillating mirror, using a two-mode model derived from a standard quantum field theory.

title: A Nearly Optimal All-Pairs Min-Cuts Algorithm in Simple Graphs
creator: Jason Li, Debmalya Panigrahi, Thatchaphol Saranurak
description: Abstract We give an n 2 + o ⁡ ( 1 ) n^{2+o(1)} -time algorithm for finding s s - t t min-cuts for all pairs of vertices s s and t t in a simple, undirected graph on n n vertices.

title: Adam in Private: Secure and Fast Training of Deep Neural Networks with Adaptive Moment Estimation
creator: Nuttapong Attrapadung 1 , Koki Hamada 2 , Dai Ikarashi 2 , Ryo Kikuchi 2 , Takahiro Matsuda 1 , Ibuki Mishina 2 , Hiraku Morita 3 and Jacob C. N. Schuldt 1
description: Abstract Machine Learning (ML) algorithms, especially deep neural networks (DNN), have proven themselves to be extremely useful tools for data analysis, and are increasingly being deployed in systems operating on sensitive data, such as recommendation systems, banking fraud detection, and healthcare systems.

title: Intelligent Transportation Systems to Mitigate Road Traffic Congestion
creator: Nizar Hamadeh, Ali Karouni, Zeinab Farhat, Hussein El Ghor, Mohamad El Ghor, Israa Katea
description: Abstract Intelligent transport systems have efficiently and effectively proved themselves in settling up the problem of traffic congestion around the world. The multi-agent based transportation system is one of the most important intelligent transport systems, which represents an interaction among the neighbouring vehicles, drivers, roads, infrastructure and vehicles.

title: ON L ∞ L^{\infty} ESTIMATES FOR COMPLEX MONGE-AMPÈRE EQUATIONS 1 1 1 Work supported in part by the National Science Foundation under grant DMS-1855947.
description: Abstract A PDE proof is provided for the sharp L ∞ L^{\infty} estimates for the complex Monge-Ampère equation which had required pluripotential theory before. The proof covers both cases of fixed background as well as degenerating background metrics. It extends to more general fully non-linear equations satisfying a structural condition, and it also gives estimates of Trudinger type.

title: Torricelli’s Curtain: Morphology of Horizontal Laminar Jets Under Gravity
creator: O. Tramis, E. Merlin-Anglade, G. Paternoster, M. Rabaud, N. M. Ribe
description: Abstract Viscous fluid exiting a long horizontal circular pipe develops a complex structure comprising a primary jet above and a smaller secondary jet below with a thin fluid curtain connecting them. We present here a combined experimental, theoretical and numerical study of this ‘Torricelli’s curtain’ phenomenon, focusing on the factors that control its morphology.

title: Low-bandwidth Modular Mathematical Modeling of DC Microgrid Systems for Control Development with Application to Shipboard Power Systems
creator: M. M. Bijaieh, Member, IEEE, S. Vedula, O. M. Anubi, Member, IEEE
description: Abstract In recent years, DC and AC microgrid (MG) systems have attracted a major attention due to various potential for integration of future technology into conventional systems and control. The integration of such technology requires appropriate tools for complex design, analysis and optimization.

title: Differentiable Dynamic Quantization with Mixed Precision and Adaptive Resolution
creator: Zhaoyang Zhang, Wenqi Shao, Jinwei Gu, Xiaogang Wang, Ping Luo
description: Abstract Model quantization is challenging due to many tedious hyper-parameters such as precision (bitwidth), dynamic range (minimum and maximum discrete values) and stepsize (interval between discrete values). Unlike prior arts that carefully tune these values, we present a fully differentiable approach to learn all of them, named Differentiable Dynamic Quantization (DDQ), which has several benefits.

title: Units in F ⁡ ( C n × Q 12 ) F(C_{n}\times Q_{12}) and F ⁡ ( C n × D 12 ) F(C_{n}\times D_{12})
creator: Meena Sahai* and Sheere Farhat Ansari** Department of Mathematics and Astronomy Lucknow University Lucknow 226007, India. E-mail: *meena_sahai@hotmail.com **sheere_farhat@rediffmail.com
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Meena Sahai* and Sheere Farhat Ansari** Department of Mathematics and Astronomy Lucknow University Lucknow 226007, India. E-mail: *meena_sahai@hotmail.com **sheere_farhat@rediffmail.com. Let C n C_{n} , Q n Q_{n} and D n D_{n} be the cyclic group, the quaternion group and the dihedral group of order n n , respectively.

title: SAND-mask: An Enhanced Gradient Masking Strategy for the Discovery of Invariances in Domain Generalization
creator: Soroosh Shahtalebi, Jean-Christophe Gagnon-Audet, Touraj Laleh, Mojtaba Faramarzi, Kartik Ahuja, Irina Rish
description: Abstract A major bottleneck in the real-world applications of machine learning models is their failure in generalizing to unseen domains whose data distribution is not i.i.d to the training domains. This failure often stems from learning non-generalizable features in the training domains that are spuriously correlated with the label of data.

title: Isomers in 203 Tl and core excitations built on a five-nucleon-hole structure
creator: V. Bothe, S.K. Tandel, S.G. Wahid, P.C. Srivastava, Bharti Bhoy, P. Chowdhury, R.V.F. Janssens, F.G. Kondev, M.P. Carpenter, T. Lauritsen, D. Seweryniak, S. Zhu
description: Abstract Isomers with three- and five-nucleon-hole configurations have been established in 203 Tl. These include newly identified levels with a three-nucleon structure: I π = (15/2 - ) with T 1/2 = 7.9(5) ns, and I π = (35/2 - ) with T 1/2 = 4.0(5) ns.

title: Temporally coherent video anonymization through GAN inpainting
creator: Thangapavithraa Balaji, Patrick Blies, Georg Göri, Raphael Mitsch, Marcel Wasserer and Torsten Schön Audi AG, thangapavithraa.balaji@audi.de, Enlite.ai Technische Hochschule Ingolstadt, torsten.schoen@thi.de
description: Abstract This work tackles the problem of temporally coherent face anonymization in natural video streams. We propose JaGAN , a two-stage system starting with detecting and masking out faces with black image patches in all individual frames of the video.

title: Test of a small prototype of the COMET cylindrical drift chamber Journal: Nuclear Instruments and Methods in Physics Research A
creator: C. Wu 1,, T.S. Wong, Y. Kuno 1,, M. Moritsu, Y. Nakazawa 2,, A. Sato, H. Sakamoto 3,, N.H. Tran 4,, M.L. Wong 5,, H. Yoshida 1,, T. Yamane, J. Zhang
description: Abstract The performance of a small prototype of a cylindrical drift chamber (CDC) used in the COMET Phase-I experiment was studied by using an electron beam. The prototype chamber was constructed with alternating all-stereo wire configuration and operated with the He − - iC 4 H 10 (90/10) gas mixture without a magnetic field.

title: Refined clock-jitter reduction in the Sagnac-type time-delay interferometry combinations
creator: Pan-Pan Wang 1, Yu-Jie Tan 1, Wei-Liang Qian 1,2,3, Cheng-Gang Shao 1
description: Abstract The ongoing development of the space-based laser interferometer missions is aiming at unprecedented gravitational wave detections in the millihertz frequency band. The spaceborne nature of the experimental setups leads to a degree of subtlety regarding the otherwise overwhelming laser frequency noise. The cancellation of the latter is accomplished through the time-delay interferometry technique.

title: Efficient ℤ 2 \mathbb{Z}_{2} synchronization on ℤ d \mathbb{Z}^{d} under symmetry-preserving side information
creator: Ahmed El Alaoui
description: Abstract We consider ℤ 2 \mathbb{Z}_{2} -synchronization on the Euclidean lattice. Every vertex of ℤ d \mathbb{Z}^{d} is assigned an independent symmetric random sign θ u \theta_{u} , and for every edge ( u , v ) (u,v) of the lattice, one observes the product θ u ​ θ v \theta_{u}\theta_{v} flipped independently with probability p p .

title: Phase-locking of lasers with Gaussian coupling Journal: osajournal Publication type: Research Article
creator: Andra Naresh Kumar Reddy, \authormark 1, † Simon Mahler, \authormark 1, † Alon Goldring, \authormark 1 Vishwa Pal, \authormark 2 Asher A. Friesem, \authormark 1 and Nir Davidson \authormark 1,*
description: Abstract Abstract A unique approach for steady in-phase locking of lasers in an array, regardless of the array geometry, position, orientation, period or size, is presented. The approach relies on the insertion of an intra-cavity Gaussian aperture in the far-field plane of the laser array.

title: ASCNet: Self-supervised Video Representation Learning with Appearance-Speed Consistency
creator: Deng Huang, Wenhao Wu, Weiwen Hu, Xu Liu, Dongliang He, Zhihua Wu, Xiangmiao Wu, Mingkui Tan, Errui Ding
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Deng Huang, Wenhao Wu, Weiwen Hu, Xu Liu, Dongliang He, Zhihua Wu, Xiangmiao Wu, Mingkui Tan, Errui Ding. We study self-supervised video representation learning, which is a challenging task due to 1) lack of labels for explicit supervision; 2) unstructured and noisy visual information.

title: Out-of-Distribution Generalization in Kernel Regression
creator: Abdulkadir Canatar, Blake Bordelon, Cengiz Pehlevan
description: Abstract In real word applications, the data generating process for training a machine learning model often differs from what the model encounters in the test stage. Understanding how and whether machine learning models generalize under such distributional shifts remains a theoretical challenge.

title: Inferring couplings in networks across order-disorder phase transitions
creator: Vudtiwat Ngampruetikorn, Vedant Sachdeva, Johanna Torrence, Jan Humplik, David J. Schwab, Stephanie E. Palmer
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Vudtiwat Ngampruetikorn, Vedant Sachdeva, Johanna Torrence, Jan Humplik, David J. Schwab, Stephanie E. Palmer. Statistical inference is central to many scientific endeavours, yet how it works remains unresolved. Answering this requires a quantitative understanding of the intrinsic interplay between statistical models, inference methods and data structure. To this end, we characterise the efficacy of direct coupling analysis (DCA)—a highly successful method for analysing amino acid sequence data—in inferring pairwise interactions from samples of ferromagnetic Ising models on random graphs.

title: How Good Is NLP? A Sober Look at NLP Tasks through the Lens of Social Impact
creator: Zhijing Jin, Geeticka Chauhan, Brian Tse, Mrinmaya Sachan, Rada Mihalcea
description: Abstract Recent years have seen many breakthroughs in natural language processing (NLP), transitioning it from a mostly theoretical field to one with many real-world applications. Noting the rising number of applications of other machine learning and AI techniques with pervasive societal impact, we anticipate the rising importance of developing NLP technologies for social good.

title: ToyADMOS2: Another dataset of miniature-machine operating sounds for anomalous sound detection under domain shift conditions
description: Abstract This paper proposes a new large-scale dataset called ”ToyADMOS2” for anomaly detection in machine operating sounds (ADMOS). As did for our previous ToyADMOS dataset, we collected a large number of operating sounds of miniature machines (toys) under normal and anomaly conditions by deliberately damaging them but extended with providing controlled depth of damages in anomaly samples.

title: Learning Slice-Aware Representations with Mixture of Attentions
creator: Cheng Wang, Sungjin Lee, Sunghyun Park, Han Li, Young-Bum Kim, Ruhi Sarikaya
description: Abstract Real-world machine learning systems are achieving remarkable performance in terms of coarse-grained metrics like overall accuracy and F-1 score. However, model improvement and development often require fine-grained modeling on individual data subsets or slices, for instance, the data slices where the models have unsatisfactory results.

title: Eliminating uncertainty of thermal emittance measurement in solenoid scans due to rf and solenoid fields overlap
creator: Lianmin Zheng, Yingchao Du, Pengwei Huang
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Lianmin Zheng, Yingchao Du, Pengwei Huang. The solenoid scan is one of the most common methods for the in-situ measurement of the thermal emittance of a photocathode in an rf photoinjector. The fringe field of the solenoid overlaps with the gun rf field in quite a number of photoinjectors, which makes accurate knowledge of the transfer matrix challenging, thus increases the measurement uncertainty of the thermal emittance.

title: Algebraic structure underlying spherical, parabolic and prolate spheroidal bases of the nine-dimensional MICZ-Kepler problem
creator: Dai-Nam Le, Van-Hoang Le
description: Abstract The nonrelativistic motion of a charged particle around a dyon in ( 9 + 1 ) (9+1) spacetime is known as the nine-dimensional MICZ-Kepler problem. This problem has been solved exactly by the variables-separation method in three different coordinate systems, spherical, parabolic, and prolate spheroidal.

title: Efficient Predictive Monitoring of Linear Time-Invariant Systems Under Stealthy Attacks
creator: Mazen Azzam, Liliana Pasquale, Gregory Provan, Bashar Nuseibeh
description: Abstract Attacks on Industrial Control Systems (ICS) can lead to significant physical damage. While offline safety and security assessments can provide insight into vulnerable system components, they may not account for stealthy attacks designed to evade anomaly detectors during long operational transients.

title: Local Adaptivity in Federated Learning: Convergence and Consistency
creator: Jianyu Wang, Zheng Xu, Zachary Garrett, Zachary Charles, Luyang Liu, Gauri Joshi
description: Abstract The federated learning (FL) framework trains a machine learning model using decentralized data stored at edge client devices by periodically aggregating locally trained models. Popular optimization algorithms of FL use vanilla (stochastic) gradient descent for both local updates at clients and global updates at the aggregating server.

title: Parallel and External-Memory Construction of Minimal Perfect Hash Functions with PTHash
creator: Giulio Ermanno Pibiri – Roberto Trani
description: Abstract A function f : U → { 0 , … , n − 1 } f:U\to\{0,\ldots,n-1\} is a minimal perfect hash function for a set S ⊆ U S\subseteq U of size n n , if f f bijectively maps S S into the first n n natural numbers.

title: Online reinforcement learning with sparse rewards through an active inference capsule
creator: Alejandro Daniel Noel, Charel van Hoof, Beren Millidge
description: Abstract Intelligent agents must pursue their goals in complex environments with partial information and often limited computational capacity. Reinforcement learning methods have achieved great success by creating agents that optimize engineered reward functions, but which often struggle to learn in sparse-reward environments, generally require many environmental interactions to perform well, and are typically computationally very expensive.

title: Gravitational collapse from cold uniform asymmetric initial conditions
creator: Francesco Sylos Labini and Michael Joyce
description: Abstract Using controlled numerical N-body experiments, we show how, in the collapse dynamics of an initially cold and uniform distribution of particles with a generic asymmetric shape, finite N N fluctuations and perturbations induced by the anisotropic gravitational field compete to determine the physical properties of the asymptotic quasi-stationary state.

title: Covering Polygons is Even Harder
creator: Mikkel Abrahamsen
description: Abstract In the Minimum Convex Cover ( MCC ) problem, we are given a simple polygon 𝒫 \mathcal{P} and an integer k k , and the question is if there exist k k convex polygons whose union is 𝒫 \mathcal{P} .

title: Facade-X: an opinionated approach to SPARQL anything Submitted to https://2021-eu.semantics.cc (Accepted, May 2021)
creator: Enrico Daga, Luigi Asprino, Paul Mulholland, Aldo Gangemi
description: Abstract The Semantic Web research community understood since its beginning how crucial it is to equip practitioners with methods to transform non-RDF resources into RDF. Proposals focus on either engineering content transformations or accessing non-RDF resources with SPARQL. Existing solutions require users to learn specific mapping languages (e.g.

title: Controlling False Positive/Negative Rates for Deep-Learning-Based Prostate Cancer Detection on Multiparametric MR images
creator: Zhe Min 1, Fernando J. Bianco 2, Qianye Yang 1, Rachael Rodell 1,3, Wen Yan 1,4, Dean Barratt 1, Yipeng Hu 1
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Zhe Min 1, Fernando J. Bianco 2, Qianye Yang 1, Rachael Rodell 1,3, Wen Yan 1,4, Dean Barratt 1, Yipeng Hu 1. Prostate cancer (PCa) is one of the leading causes of death for men worldwide. Multi-parametric magnetic resonance (mpMR) imaging has emerged as a non-invasive diagnostic tool for detecting and localising prostate tumours by specialised radiologists.

title: Provably Strict Generalisation Benefit for Invariance in Kernel Methods
creator: Bryn Elesedy
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Bryn Elesedy. It is a commonly held belief that enforcing invariance improves generalisation. Although this approach enjoys widespread popularity, it is only very recently that a rigorous theoretical demonstration of this benefit has been established. In this work we build on the function space perspective of [ 8 ] to derive a strictly non-zero generalisation benefit of incorporating invariance in kernel ridge regression when the target is invariant to the action of a compact group.

title: A Learning-based Optimal Market Bidding Strategy for Price-Maker Energy Storage
creator: Mathilde D. Badoual, Scott J. Moura
description: Abstract Load serving entities with storage units reach sizes and performances that can significantly impact clearing prices in electricity markets. Nevertheless, price endogeneity is rarely considered in storage bidding strategies and modeling the electricity market is a challenging task. Meanwhile, model-free reinforcement learning such as the Actor-Critic are becoming increasingly popular for designing energy system controllers.

title: Resource Allocation in Disaggregated Data Centre Systems with Reinforcement Learning
creator: Zacharaya Shabka, Georgios Zervas
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Zacharaya Shabka, Georgios Zervas. Resource-disaggregated data centres (RDDC) propose a resource-centric, and high-utilisation architecture for data centres (DC), avoiding resource fragmentation and enabling arbitrarily sized resource pools to be allocated to tasks, rather than server-sized ones.

title: Fast Extra Gradient Methods for Smooth Structured Nonconvex-Nonconcave Minimax Problems
creator: Sucheol Lee, Donghwan Kim
description: Abstract Modern minimax problems, such as generative adversarial network and adversarial training, are often under a nonconvex-nonconcave setting, and developing an efficient method for such setting is of interest. Recently, two variants of the extragradient (EG) method are studied in that direction.

title: \pkg varycoef: An \proglang R Package for Gaussian Process-based Spatially Varying Coefficient Models
creator: Jakob A. Dambon Lucerne University of Applied Sciences and Arts, Fabio Sigrist Lucerne University of Applied Sciences and Arts, Reinhard Furrer University of Zurich
description: Abstract \Plainauthor Jakob A. Dambon, Fabio Sigrist, Reinhard Furrer \Plaintitle varycoef: An R Package for Gaussian Process-based Spatially Varying Coefficient Models \Shorttitle \pkg varycoef: GP-based SVC Models \Abstract Gaussian processes (GPs) are well-known tools for modeling dependent data with applications in spatial statistics, time series analysis, or econometrics.

title: Solid/Liquid Phase Transition and Heat Engine in Asymptotically Flat Schwarzschild Black Hole via the Rényi Extended Phase Space Approach
creator: Chatchai Promsiri, Ekapong Hirunsirisawat, and Watchara Liewrian
description: Abstract Recently, it has been found that, with the Rényi statistics, the asymptotically flat Schwarzschild black hole can be in thermal equilibrium with infinite heat reservior at a fixed temperature when its event horizon radius is larger than the characteristic length scale L λ = 1 / π ​ λ L_{\lambda}=1/\sqrt{\pi\lambda} , where λ \lambda is the nonextensivity parameter.

title: Distortion measure of spectrograms for classification of respiratory diseases
creator: Jeremy Levy, Alexander Naitsat and Yehoshua Y. Zeevi
description: Abstract A new method for classification of respiratory diseases is presented. The method is based on a novel class of features, extracted from pulmonary sounds, by parameterizing their spectrograms that are represented as surfaces, and by utilizing geometrical distortions defined with reference to these surfaces. This method yields a set of highly descriptive features for analysis of pulmonary sound recordings.

title: Anti-symmetric Compton scattering in LiNiPO 4 : Towards a direct probe of the magneto-electric multipole moment
creator: Sayantika Bhowal ∗, Daniel O’Neill ∗, Michael Fechner ∗, Nicola A. Spaldin, Urs Staub, Jon Duffy, Stephen P. Collins
description: Abstract We present a combined theoretical and experimental investigation of the anti-symmetric Compton profile in LiNiPO 4 as a possible probe for magneto-electric toroidal moments. Understanding as well as detecting such magneto-electric multipoles is an active area of research in condensed matter physics.

title: You Only Compress Once: Towards Effective and Elastic BERT Compression via Exploit-Explore Stochastic Nature Gradient
creator: Shaokun Zhang, Xiawu Zheng, Chenyi Yang, Yuchao Li, Yan Wang Fei Chao Mengdi Wang Shen Li Yang Jun Rongrong Ji, School of Informatics, Xiamen University Alibaba Group
description: Abstract Despite superior performance on various natural language processing tasks, pre-trained models such as BERT are challenged by deploying on resource-constraint devices. Most existing model compression approaches require re-compression or fine-tuning across diverse constraints to accommodate various hardware deployments. This practically limits the further application of model compression.

title: Contour Moments Based Manipulation of Composite Rigid-Deformable Objects with Finite Time Model Estimation and Shape/Position Control Thanks: This work is supported in part by: the Key-Area Research and Development Program of Guangdong Province 2020 under project 76, the Hong Kong Research Grants Co
creator: Jiaming Qi, Guangfu Ma, Jihong Zhu, Peng Zhou, Yueyong Lyu
description: Abstract The robotic manipulation of composite rigid-deformable objects (i.e. those with mixed non-homogeneous stiffness properties) is a challenging problem with clear practical applications that, despite the recent progress in the field, it has not been sufficiently studied in the literature.

title: An Intelligent Resource Reservation for Crowdsourced Live Video Streaming Applications in Geo-Distributed Cloud Environment
creator: E. Baccour, F. Haouari, A. Erbad, A. Mohamed, K. Bilal, M. Guizani, M. Hamdi
description: Abstract Crowdsourced live video streaming (livecast) services such as Facebook Live, YouNow, Douyu and Twitch are gaining more momentum recently. Allocating the limited resources in a cost-effective manner while maximizing the Quality of Service (QoS) through real-time delivery and the provision of the appropriate representations for all viewers is a challenging problem.

title: On an inverse scattering transform for the nonlinear Schödinger equation on the half-line This project is support by NSFC No. 11601312, 11875040.
creator: Cheng Zhang
description: Abstract In this paper, we develop an inverse scattering transform for the integrable focusing nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equation on the half-line subject to a class of boundary conditions. The method is based on the notions of integrable boundary conditions and double-row monodromy matrix, developed by Sklyanin, which characterize initial-boundary value problems for NLS on an interval.

title: Modeling premiums of non-life insurance companies in India
creator: Kartik Sethi, Siddhartha P. Chakrabarty
description: Abstract We undertake an empirical analysis for the premium data of non-life insurance companies operating in India, in the paradigm of fitting the data for the parametric distribution of Lognormal and the extreme value based distributions of Generalized Extreme Value and Generalized Pareto.

title: On (co-lex) Ordering Automata
creator: Nicola Cotumaccio, Giovanna D’Agostino, Alberto Policriti, Nicola Prezza
description: Abstract The states of a deterministic finite automaton 𝒜 \mathcal{A} can be identified with collections of words in Pref ​ ( ℒ ​ ( 𝒜 ) ) \text{Pref}(\mathcal{L}(\mathcal{A})) —the set of prefixes of words belonging to the regular language accepted by 𝒜 \mathcal{A} .

title: A Two Component Model of the Vela Pulsars with Large Fractional Moment of Inertia of the Crust
creator: P S Negi
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by P S Negi. We construct a two-component analytic model of the Vela pulsar which can reproduce the fractional crustal moment of inertia, I crust / I total ≥ 0.074 I_{\rm crust}/I_{\rm total}\geq 0.074 ( where I crust I_{\rm crust} represents the moment of inertia of the crust and I total I_{\rm total} is the total moment of inertia of the star) for the mass range M / M ⊙ ≥ 1.0 − 1.96 M/M_{\odot}\geq 1.0-1.96 .

title: Over-optimism in benchmark studies and the multiplicity of design and analysis options when interpreting their results
creator: Christina Nießl, Moritz Herrmann, Chiara Wiedemann, Giuseppe Casalicchio, Anne-Laure Boulesteix
description: Abstract In recent years, the need for neutral benchmark studies that focus on the comparison of methods from computational sciences has been increasingly recognised by the scientific community. While general advice on the design and analysis of neutral benchmark studies can be found in recent literature, certain amounts of flexibility always exist.

creator: Avijit Chowdhury
description: Abstract \thesistitle On the effect of scalar fields on Hawking radiation and quasinormal modes of black holes \supervisor Prof. Narayan Banerjee \examiner Doctor of Philosophy \addresses \subject Physical Sciences \university IISER Kolkata \department Department of Physical Sciences Doctoral Thesis \HRule \ttitle \HRule By Avijit Chowdhury Roll No.

title: Comparison of Graphcore IPUs and Nvidia GPUs for cosmology applications
creator: Bastien Arcelin 1 1 Université de Paris, CNRS, Astroparticule et Cosmologie, F-75013 Paris, France
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Bastien Arcelin 1 1 Université de Paris, CNRS, Astroparticule et Cosmologie, F-75013 Paris, France. This paper represents the first investigation of the suitability and performance of Graphcore Intelligence Processing Units (IPUs) for deep learning applications in cosmology. It presents the benchmark between a Nvidia V100 GPU and a Graphcore MK1 (GC2) IPU on three cosmological use cases: a classical deep neural network and a Bayesian neural network (BNN) for galaxy shape estimation, and a generative network for galaxy images simulation.

title: Braid group and q q -Racah polynomials
creator: Nicolas Crampé †, Luc Vinet ∗, Meri Zaimi ∗
description: Abstract . The irreducible representations of two intermediate Casimir elements associated to the recoupling of three identical irreducible representations of U q ​ ( 𝔰 ​ 𝔩 2 ) U_{q}(\mathfrak{sl}_{2}) are considered. It is shown that these intermediate Casimirs are related by a conjugation involving braid group representations.

title: A Robust and Accurate Deep Learning based Pattern Recognition Framework for Upper Limb Prosthesis using sEMG
creator: Sidharth Pancholi, Amit M. Joshi, Deepak Joshi
description: Abstract In EMG based pattern recognition (EMG-PR), deep learning-based techniques have become more prominent for their self-regulating capability to extract discriminant features from large data-sets. Moreover, the performance of traditional machine learning-based methods show limitation to categorize over a certain number of classes and degrades over a period of time.
