title: Image of the thin accretion disk around compact objects in the Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity
creator: Galin Gyulchev, Petya Nedkova, Tsvetan Vetsov, Stoytcho Yazadjiev
description: Abstract We study the optical appearance of a thin accretion disk around compact objects within the Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity. Considering static spherically symmetric black holes and naked singularities we search for characteristic signatures which can arise in the observable images due to the modification of general relativity.

title: Electric-field-driven conductance switching in encapsulated graphene nanogaps
creator: Eugenia Pyurbeeva, Jacob L. Swett, Qingyu Ye, Oscar W. Kennedy, Jan A. Mol
description: Abstract Feedback-controlled electric breakdown of graphene in air or vacuum is a well-established way of fabricating tunnel junctions, nanogaps, and quantum dots. We show that the method is equally applicable to encapsulated graphene constrictions fabricated using hydrogen silsesquioxane. The silica-like layer left by hydrogen silsesquioxane resist after electron-beam exposure remains intact after electric breakdown of the graphene.

title: Stabilization of a nonlinear bullet coexisting with a Bose-Einstein condensate in a rapidly cooled magnonic system driven by a spin-orbit torque
creator: Michael Schneider, David Breitbach, Rostyslav O. Serha, Qi Wang, Morteza Mohseni, Alexander A. Serga, Andrei N. Slavin, Vasyl S. Tiberkevich, Björn Heinz, Thomas Brächer, Bert Lägel, Carsten Dubs, Sebastian Knauer, Oleksandr V. Dobrovolskiy, Philipp Pirro, Burkard Hillebrands, Andrii V. Chumak
description: Abstract We have recently shown that injection of magnons into a magnetic dielectric via the spin-orbit torque (SOT) effect in the adjacent layer of a heavy metal subjected to the action of short ( 0.1 µ ​ s 0.1\text{\,}\mathrm{\SIUnitSymbolMicro s} ) current pulses allows for control of a magnon Bose-Einstein Condensate (BEC).

title: Strain-induced topological charge control in multifold fermion systems
creator: Anumita Bose, Awadhesh Narayan
description: Abstract Multifold fermion systems feature free fermionic excitations, which have no counterparts in high-energy physics, and exhibit several unconventional properties. Using first-principles calculations, we predict that strain engineering can be used to control the distribution of topological charges in transition metal silicide candidate CoSi, hosting multifold fermions.

title: Deep inelastic (anti)neutrino-nucleus scattering
creator: V. Ansari 1, M. Sajjad Athar 1, H. Haider 1, I. Ruiz Simo 2, S. K. Singh 1, F. Zaidi 1
description: Abstract The present status of the field theoretical model studies of the deep inelastic scattering induced by (anti)neutrino on the nuclear targets in a wide range of Bjorken variable x x and four momentum transfer square Q 2 Q^{2} , has been reviewed Haider:2011qs ; Haider:2012nf ; Haider:2016zrk ; Zaidi:2019mfd ; Zaidi:2019asc ; Ansari:2020xne .

title: String breaking in a cold wind as seen by string models
creator: Oleg Andreev
description: Abstract Using the gauge/string duality, we model a heavy quark-antiquark pair in a color singlet state moving through a cold medium and explore the consequences of temperature and velocity on string breaking. In doing so, we restrict to the case of two dynamical flavors.

title: Realtime Robust Malicious Traffic Detection via Frequency Domain Analysis Conference: Proceedings of the 2021 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security; November 15–19, 2021; Virtual Event, Republic of Korea Proceedings of the 2021 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communicat
creator: Chuanpu Fu 1 , Qi Li 2,3 , Meng Shen 4 , and Ke Xu 1,3,5
description: Abstract . Machine learning (ML) based malicious traffic detection is an emerging security paradigm, particularly for zero-day attack detection, which is complementary to existing rule based detection. However, the existing ML based detection achieves low detection accuracy and low throughput incurred by inefficient traffic features extraction. Thus, they cannot detect attacks in realtime, especially in high throughput networks.

title: On the Garden of Eden theorem for ℬ \mathscr{B} -free subshifts
creator: G. Keller, M. Lemańczyk, C. Richard, D. Sell
description: Abstract We prove that on ℬ \mathscr{B} -free subshifts, with ℬ \mathscr{B} satisfying the Erdös condition, all cellular automata are determined by monotone sliding block codes. In particular, this implies the validity of the Garden of Eden theorem for such systems. 1 Introduction 1.

title: Keyphrase Generation for Scientific Document Retrieval
creator: Florian Boudin, Ygor Gallina, Akiko Aizawa
description: Abstract Sequence-to-sequence models have lead to significant progress in keyphrase generation, but it remains unknown whether they are reliable enough to be beneficial for document retrieval. This study provides empirical evidence that such models can significantly improve retrieval performance, and introduces a new extrinsic evaluation framework that allows for a better understanding of the limitations of keyphrase generation models.

description:
A 2021 arXiv research paper by Conrad Gstöttner a , Bernd Kolar b and Markus Schöberl a. We propose easily verifiable necessary and sufficient conditions for the linearizability of two-input systems by an endogenous dynamic feedback with a dimension of at most two. keywords

title: Tiled sparse coding in eigenspaces for the COVID-19 diagnosis in chest X-ray images
description: Abstract Zusammenfassung The ongoing crisis of the COVID-19 (Coronavirus disease 2019) pandemic has changed the world. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), 4 million people have died due to this disease, whereas there have been more than 180 million confirmed cases of COVID-19.

title: Adding Interactivity to Education of Complex Wireless Networks Using Digital Game-Based Learning
creator: Seungmo Kim, Senior Member, IEEE
description: Abstract Can we make undergraduate engineering education easier and more fun? This research aims to see if we can answer the ambitious question! The digital game-based learning (DGBL) has been found to increase the efficacy of learning when applied in engineering classes thanks to its ability to make students feel easy and fun.

title: Permanent variational wave functions for bosons
creator: J. M. Zhang, H. F. Song, Y. Liu
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by J. M. Zhang, H. F. Song, Y. Liu. We study the performance of permanent states (the bosonic counterpart of the Slater determinant state) as approximating functions for bosons, with the intention to develop variational methods based upon them. For a system of N N identical bosons, a permanent state is constructed by taking a set of N N arbitrary (not necessarily orthonormal) single-particle orbitals, forming their product and then symmetrizing it.

title: The DELICES project: Indexing scientific literature through semantic expansion DOI: 10.1145/1122445.1122456 Conference: Woodstock ’18: ACM Symposium on Neural Gaze Detection; June 03–05, 2018; Woodstock, NY Woodstock ’18: ACM Symposium on Neural Gaze Detection, June 03–05, 2018, Woodstock, NY Price:
creator: Florian Boudin, Béatrice Daille, Evelyne Jacquey, Jian-Yun Nie
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Florian Boudin, Béatrice Daille, Evelyne Jacquey, Jian-Yun Nie. Scientific digital libraries play a critical role in the development and dissemination of scientific literature. Despite dedicated search engines, retrieving relevant publications from the ever-growing body of scientific literature remains challenging and time-consuming. Indexing scientific articles is indeed a difficult matter, and current models solely rely on a small portion of the articles (title and abstract) and on author-assigned keyphrases when available. This results in a frustratingly limited access to scientific knowledge.

title: The Kazdan–Warner problem with (and via) symmetries
creator: Leonardo F. Cavenaghi, João Marcos do Ó, Llohann D. Sperança
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Leonardo F. Cavenaghi, João Marcos do Ó, Llohann D. Sperança. Schoen completed the solution to the Yamabe problem, compact manifolds could be categorized into three classes, depending on whether they admit a metric with positive, non-negative, or only negative scalar curvature. Here we follow Yamabe’s first attempt to solve his problem through variational methods and provide an analogous equivalent classification for manifolds equipped with actions by compact connected Lie groups. Moreover, we approach the Kazdan–Warner problem for manifolds with isometric actions.

title: Privacy-Utility Trade-Offs Against Limited Adversaries
creator: Xiaoming Duan, Zhe Xu, Rui Yan, Ufuk Topcu
description: Abstract We study privacy-utility trade-offs where users share privacy-correlated useful information with a service provider to obtain some utility. The service provider is adversarial in the sense that it can infer the users’ private information based on the shared useful information.

title: Strong quantum computational advantage using a superconducting quantum processor
creator: Yulin Wu, Wan-Su Bao, Sirui Cao, Fusheng Chen, Ming-Cheng Chen, Xiawei Chen, Tung-Hsun Chung, Hui Deng, Yajie Du, Daojin Fan, Ming Gong, Cheng Guo, Chu Guo, Shaojun Guo, Lianchen Han, Linyin Hong, He-Liang Huang, Yong-Heng Huo, Liping Li, Na Li, Shaowei Li, Yuan Li, Futian Liang, Chun Lin, Jin Lin,
description: Abstract Scaling up to a large number of qubits with high-precision control is essential in the demonstrations of quantum computational advantage to exponentially outpace the classical hardware and algorithmic improvements. Here, we develop a two-dimensional programmable superconducting quantum processor, Zuchongzhi , which is composed of 66 functional qubits in a tunable coupling architecture.

title: Final size and partial distance estimate for a two-group SEIRD model Thanks: Submitted on August 8, 2026
creator: Alison M.V.D.L. Melo, Matheus C. Santos
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Alison M.V.D.L. Melo, Matheus C. Santos. In this paper we consider a SEIRD epidemic model for a population composed by two groups of individuals with asymmetric interaction. Given an approximate solution for the two-group model, we estimate the error of this approximation to the unknown solution to the second group based on the known error that the approximation has with respect to the solution to the first group. We also study the final size of the epidemic for each group.

title: BMS Algebra, Double Soft Theorems, and All That
creator: Miguel Campiglia, Alok Laddha
description: Abstract The Lie algebra generated by supertranslation and superrotation vector fields at null infinity, known as the extended Bondi–van der Burg–Metzner–Sachs (eBMS) algebra is expected to be a symmetry algebra of the quantum gravity S-matrix. However, the algebra of commutators of the quantized eBMS charges has been a thorny issue in the literature.

title: A Wick rotation for EPRL spin foam models
creator: Pietro Donà, Francesco Gozzini, Alessandro Nicotra a CPT, Aix-Marseille Université, Université de Toulon, CNRS, 13288 Marseille, Franceb DIFA, Alma Mater Studiorum, Università di Bologna, Italy
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Pietro Donà, Francesco Gozzini, Alessandro Nicotra a CPT, Aix-Marseille Université, Université de Toulon, CNRS, 13288 Marseille, Franceb DIFA, Alma Mater Studiorum, Università di Bologna, Italy. We show that the Euclidean and Lorentzian EPRL vertex amplitudes of covariant Loop Quantum Gravity are related through a “Wick rotation” of the real Immirzi parameter to purely imaginary values.

title: HIGHER-DIMENSIONAL POWER DIAGRAMS FOR SEMI-DISCRETE OPTIMAL TRANSPORT
creator: Philip Claude Caplan
description: Abstract Efficient algorithms for solving optimal transport problems are important for measuring and optimizing distances between functions. In the L 2 L^{2} semi-discrete context, this problem consists of finding a map from a continuous density function to a discrete set of points so as to minimize the transport cost, using the squared Euclidean distance as the cost function.

title: TENT: Tensorized Encoder Transformer for temperature forecasting Journal: arXiv
creator: Onur Bilgin, Paweł Mąka, Thomas Vergutz, Siamak Mehrkanoon
description: Abstract Reliable weather forecasting is of great importance in science, business, and society. The best performing data-driven models for weather prediction tasks rely on recurrent or convolutional neural networks, where some of which incorporate attention mechanisms. In this work, we introduce a novel model based on Transformer architecture for weather forecasting.

title: Unitarity and Page curve for evaporation of 2D AdS black holes
creator: M. Cadoni, A. P. Sanna
description: Abstract We explore the Hawking evaporation of two-dimensional anti-de Sitter (AdS 2 ), dilatonic black hole coupled with conformal matter, and derive the Page curve for the entanglement entropy of radiation. We first work in a semiclassical approximation with backreaction. We show that the end-point of the evaporation process is AdS 2 with a vanishing dilaton, i.e.

title: Improved Prediction and Network Estimation Using the Monotone Single Index Multi-variate Autoregressive Model
creator: Yue Gao ygao266@wisc.edu, Garvesh Raskutti garvesh@gmail.com
description: Abstract Network estimation from multi-variate point process or time series data is a problem of fundamental importance. Prior work has focused on parametric approaches that require a known parametric model, which makes estimation procedures less robust to model mis-specification, non-linearities and heterogeneities.

title: One-Shot Affordance Detection
creator: Hongchen Luo, Wei Zhai, Jing Zhang, Yang Cao, Dacheng Tao
description: Abstract Affordance detection refers to identifying the potential action possibilities of objects in an image, which is an important ability for robot perception and manipulation. To empower robots with this ability in unseen scenarios, we consider the challenging one-shot affordance detection problem in this paper, i.e.

title: Counting Divisions of a 2 × n 2\times n Rectangular Grid
creator: Jacob Brown
description: Abstract What is the number of ways to divide a 2 × n 2\times n rectangular grid, cutting along the grid lines, into k k pieces? Are there formulas that calculate these number of divisions? If so, what do they look like?

title: Designing color symmetry in stigmergic art
creator: Hendrik Richter
description: Abstract Color symmetry is an extension of symmetry imposed by isometric transformations and means that the colors of geometrical objects are assigned according to the symmetry properties of the objects. A color symmetry permutes the coloring of the objects consistently with their symmetry group. We apply this concept to bio-inspired generative art.

title: A New Approach to Bell and poly-Bell Numbers and Polynomials
creator: DAE SAN KIM, D. V. Dolgy, Hye Kyoung Kim, Hyunseok Lee, Taekyun Kim
description: Abstract . The aim of this paper is to introduce Bell polynomials and numbers of the second kind and poly-Bell polynomials and numbers of the second kind, and to derive their explicit expressions, recurrence relations and some identities involving those polynomials and numbers.

title: Measurement of Topological Order based on Metric-Curvature Correspondence
creator: Gero von Gersdorff, Wei Chen
description: Abstract A unified expression for topological invariants has been proposed recently to describe the topological order in Dirac models belonging to any dimension and symmetry class. We uncover a correspondence between the curvature function that integrates to this unified topological invariant and the quantum metric that measures the distance between properly defined many-body Bloch states in momentum space.

title: Clarifying How Degree Entropies and Degree-Degree Correlations Relate to Network Robustness
creator: Chris Jones 1 and Karoline Wiesner 2
description: Abstract It is often claimed that the entropy of a network’s degree distribution is a proxy for its robustness. Here, we clarify the link between degree distribution entropy and giant component robustness to node removal by showing that the former merely sets a lower bound to the latter for randomly configured networks when no other network characteristics are specified.

title: The Runsort Permuton
creator: Noga Alon, Colin Defant, Noah Kravitz
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Noga Alon, Colin Defant, Noah Kravitz. Suppose we choose a permutation π \pi uniformly at random from S n S_{n} . Let 𝗋𝗎𝗇𝗌𝗈𝗋𝗍 ⁡ ( π ) \mathsf{runsort}(\pi) be the permutation obtained by sorting the ascending runs of π \pi into lexicographic order. Alexandersson and Nabawanda recently asked if the plot of 𝗋𝗎𝗇𝗌𝗈𝗋𝗍 ⁡ ( π ) \mathsf{runsort}(\pi) , when scaled to the unit square [ 0 , 1 ] 2 [0,1]^{2} , converges to a limit shape as n → ∞ n\to\infty .

title: Ricci flow starting from an embedded closed convex surface in ℝ 3 \mathbb{R}^{3} Thanks: AMS Mathematics Subject Classification.
creator: Jiuzhou Huang and Jiawei Liu
description: Abstract . In this paper, we establish the existence and uniqueness of Ricci flow that admits an embedded closed convex surface in ℝ 3 \mathbb{R}^{3} as metric initial condition. The main point is a family of smooth Ricci flows starting from smooth convex surfaces whose metrics converge uniformly to the metric of the initial surface in intrinsic sense. 1.

title: Continuous data assimilation and long-time accuracy in a C 0 C^{0} interior penalty method for the Cahn-Hilliard equation
creator: Amanda E. Diegel, Leo G. Rebholz
description: Abstract We propose a numerical approximation method for the Cahn-Hilliard equations that incorporates continuous data assimilation in order to achieve long time accuracy. The method uses a C 0 interior penalty spatial discretization of the fourth order Cahn-Hilliard equations, together with a backward Euler temporal discretization.

title: Additive Sparsification of CSPs Thanks: An extended abstract of this work appeared in the Proceedings of the 29th European Symposium on Algorithms (ESA’21) [ 29 ] . Stanislav Živný was supported by a Royal Society University Research Fellowship. This project has received funding from the European Re
creator: Eden Pelleg, Stanislav Živný
description: Abstract Multiplicative cut sparsifiers, introduced by Benczúr and Karger [STOC’96], have proved extremely influential and found various applications. Precise characterisations were established for sparsifiability of graphs with other 2-variable predicates on Boolean domains by Filtser and Krauthgamer [SIDMA’17] and non-Boolean domains by Butti and Živný [SIDMA’20].

title: On the mechanism of ionization oscillations in Hall thrusters
creator: O. Chapurin, A. I. Smolyakov, G. Hagelaar, Y. Raitses
description: Abstract Low frequency ionization oscillations involving plasma and neutral density (breathing modes) are the most violent perturbations in Hall thrusters for electric propulsion. Because of its simplicity, the zero-dimensional (0-D) predator-prey model of two nonlinearly coupled ordinary differential equations for plasma and neutral density has been often used for the characterization of such oscillations and scaling estimates.

title: Exact description of quantum stochastic models as quantum resistors
creator: Tony Jin 1 , João S. Ferreira 1 , Michele Filippone 1,2 and Thierry Giamarchi 1
description: Abstract We study the transport properties of generic out-of-equilibrium quantum systems connected to fermionic reservoirs. We develop a new perturbation scheme in the inverse system size, named 1 / N 1/N expansion, to study a large class of out of equilibrium diffusive/ohmic systems.

title: Low temperature thermodynamics of the antiferromagnetic J 1 − J 2 J_{1}-J_{2} model: Entropy, critical points and spin gap
creator: Sudip Kumar Saha, Manodip Routh, Manoranjan Kumar, Zoltán G. Soos
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Sudip Kumar Saha, Manodip Routh, Manoranjan Kumar, Zoltán G. Soos. The antiferromagnetic J 1 − J 2 J_{1}-J_{2} model is a spin-1/2 chain with isotropic exchange J 1 > 0 J_{1}>0 between first neighbors and J 2 = α ​ J 1 J_{2}=\alpha J_{1} between second neighbors. The model supports both gapless quantum phases with nondegenerate ground states and gapped phases with Δ ⁡ ( α ) > 0 \Delta(\alpha)>0 and doubly degenerate ground states.

title: Weighted unary-binary trees, Hex-trees, marked ordered trees, and related structures Thanks: Results from https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.03350 are now included in the present version (August 16, 2021).
creator: Helmut Prodinger
description: Abstract . Hex-trees are identified as a particular instance of weighted unary-binary trees. The Horton-Strahler numbers of these objects are revisited, and, thanks to a substitution that is not immediately intuitive, explicit results are possible. They are augmented by asymptotic evaluations as well.

title: Implementation of a time-dependent multiconfiguration self-consistent-field method for coupled electron-nuclear dynamics in diatomic molecules driven by intense laser pulses
creator: Yang Li, Takeshi Sato, Kenichi L. Ishikawa
description: Abstract We present an implementation of a time-dependent multiconfiguration self-consistent-field method [R. Anzaki, T. Sato and K. L. Ishikawa, Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys. 19 , 22008 (2017) ] with the full configuration-interaction expansion for coupled electron-nuclear dynamics in diatomic molecules subject to a strong laser field.

title: Experimental Comparison of PC-Trees and PQ-Trees
creator: Simon D. Fink, Matthias Pfretzschner, Ignaz Rutter
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Simon D. Fink, Matthias Pfretzschner, Ignaz Rutter. PQ-trees and PC-trees are data structures that represent sets of linear and circular orders, respectively, subject to constraints that specific subsets of elements have to be consecutive.

title: The curvature of convex sum of metrics and applications
creator: Leonardo F. Cavenaghi, Llohann D. Sperança
description: Abstract In this paper we explore the curvature of convex sums of Riemannian metrics g ⁡ ( t ) = ( 1 − t ) ​ g 0 + t ​ g 1 g(t)=(1-t)g_{0}+tg_{1} , and study whether such a deformation can increase the curvature of an immersed totally geodesic flat tori.

title: An effective theory for higher-dimensional black holes and applications to metastable antibranes
creator: Nam Huy Hoai Nguyen
description: Abstract Despite their consequential applications across the subfields of high energy physics, metastable states of antibranes in warped throats are not yet fully understood. In this thesis, we provide new information on various aspects of these metastable antibranes through applications of the blackfold effective theory for higher-dimensional black holes.

title: Channel Estimation for RIS-Aided Multiuser Millimeter-Wave Systems
creator: Gui Zhou, Cunhua Pan, Hong Ren, Petar Popovski, IEEE Fellow , A. Lee Swindlehurst, IEEE Fellow
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Gui Zhou, Cunhua Pan, Hong Ren, Petar Popovski, IEEE Fellow , A. Lee Swindlehurst, IEEE Fellow. A reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) is a promising device that can reconfigure the electromagnetic propagation environment through adjustment of the phase shifts of its multiple reflecting elements. However, channel estimation in RIS-aided multiuser multiple-input single-output (MU-MISO) wireless communication systems is challenging due to the passive nature of the RIS and the large number of reflecting elements that can lead to high channel estimation overhead.

title: Feature Importance Guided Attack, a Model Agnostic Adversarial Attack for Tabular Datasets
creator: Gilad Gressel, Kalyani Harikumar, Niranjan Hegde, Anjali S, Archana Sreekumar, Krishnashree Achuthan, Rishikumar Radhakrishnan
description: Abstract Research in adversarial learning has primarily focused on homogeneous unstructured datasets, which often map into the problem space naturally. Inverting a feature space attack on heterogeneous datasets into the problem space is much more challenging, particularly the task of finding the perturbation to perform.

title: Differentially Private Algorithms for Graphs Under Continual Observation
creator: Hendrik Fichtenberger, Monika Henzinger, Lara Ost
description: Abstract Differentially private algorithms protect individuals in data analysis scenarios by ensuring that there is only a weak correlation between the existence of the user in the data and the result of the analysis. Dynamic graph algorithms maintain the solution to a problem (e.g., a matching) on an evolving input, i.e.

title: Nash Social Welfare for 2-value Instances
creator: Hannaneh Akrami, Bhaskar Ray Chaudhury, Kurt Mehlhorn, Golnoosh Shahkarami, Quentin Vermande
description: Abstract This paper is merged with [ 1 ] . We refer the reader to the full and updated version. We study the problem of allocating a set of indivisible goods among agents with 2-value additive valuations. Our goal is to find an allocation with maximum Nash social welfare, i.e., the geometric mean of the valuations of the agents.

title: A Theory-Driven Self-Labeling Refinement Method for Contrastive Representation Learning
creator: Pan Zhou, Caiming Xiong, Xiao-Tong Yuan, Steven Hoi
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Pan Zhou, Caiming Xiong, Xiao-Tong Yuan, Steven Hoi. For an image query, unsupervised contrastive learning labels crops of the same image as positives, and other image crops as negatives. Although intuitive, such a native label assignment strategy cannot reveal the underlying semantic similarity between a query and its positives and negatives, and impairs performance, since some negatives are semantically similar to the query or even share the same semantic class as the query.

title: Effect of plasmonic Aluminum nanoparticles shapes on optical absorption enhancement in silicon thin-film solar cells
creator: Maedeh Rassekh 1, Reza Shirmohammadi 2, Roghayeh Ghasempour 2, Fatemeh Razi Astaraei 2, Saber Farjami Shayesteh 1
description: Abstract Scattering from metal nanoparticles near their localized plasmon resonance; especially, the resonances of noble metals which are mostly in the visible or infrared part of the electromagnetic spectrum; is a way of improving light absorption in thin-film solar cells.

title: Gaussian Process Regression for Active Sensing Probabilistic Structural Health Monitoring: Experimental Assessment Across Multiple Damage and Loading Scenarios
creator: Ahmad Amer, Fotis Kopsaftopoulos
description: Abstract In the near future, Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) technologies for aircraft will be capable of overcoming the drawbacks in the current maintenance and life-cycle management paradigms, namely: cost, increased downtime, less-than-optimal safety management paradigm and the limited applicability of fully-autonomous operations. In the context of SHM for aircraft structures, one of the most challenging tasks is structural damage quantification.

title: The Temporal Onset of Habitability For Earth-Like Planets
creator: Johnny Seales, Adrian Lenardic
description: Abstract The ability of a planet to maintain surface water, key to life as we know it, depends on solar and planetary energy. As a star ages, it delivers more energy to a planet. As a planet ages it produces less internal heat, which leads to cooling.

title: Doing good by fighting fraud: Ethical anti-fraud systems for mobile payments
creator: Zainul Abi Din 1 , Hari Venugopalan 1 , Henry Lin 2 , Adam Wushensky 2 , Steven Liu 2 , Samuel T. King 1 2
description: Abstract App builders commonly use security challenges, a form of step-up authentication, to add security to their apps. However, the ethical implications of this type of architecture has not been studied previously. In this paper, we present a large-scale measurement study of running an existing anti-fraud security challenge, Boxer, in real apps running on mobile devices.

title: A comprehensive first-principle study of borophene-based nano gas sensor with gold electrodes
creator: Yueyue Tian, Houping Yang, Junjun Li, Shunbo Hu, Shixun Cao, Wei Ren, Yin Wang
description: Abstract Using density functional theory combined with nonequilibrium Green’s function method, the transport properties of borophene-based nano gas sensors with gold electrodes are calculated, and comprehensive understandings regarding the effects of gas molecules, MoS 2 substrate and gold electrodes to the transport properties of borophene are made.

title: The earliest diamond of finite type in Nottingham algebras
creator: Marina Avitabile, Sandro Mattarei
description: Abstract . We prove several structural results on Nottingham algebras, a class of infinite-dimensional, modular, graded Lie algebras, which includes the graded Lie algebra associated to the Nottingham group with respect to its lower central series. Homogeneous components of a Nottingham algebra have dimension one or two, and in the latter case they are called diamonds .

title: Hybrid zonotopes: a new set representation for reachability analysis of mixed logical dynamical systems footnoteinfo
creator: Trevor J. Bird, Herschel C. Pangborn, Neera Jain, Justin P. Koeln
description: Abstract This article presents a new set representation named the hybrid zonotope that is equivalent to the union of 2 N 2^{N} constrained zonotopes—convex polytopes—through the addition of N N binary zonotope factors. The major contribution of this manuscript is a closed-form solution for exact forward reachable sets of discrete-time, linear hybrid systems modeled as mixed logical dynamical systems.

title: A Criterion for the Onset of Chaos in Compact, Eccentric Multiplanet Systems
creator: Daniel Tamayo, Norman Murray, Scott Tremaine, Joshua Winn
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Daniel Tamayo, Norman Murray, Scott Tremaine, Joshua Winn. We derive a semi-analytic criterion for the presence of chaos in compact, eccentric multiplanet systems. Beyond a minimum semimajor-axis separation, below which the dynamics are chaotic at all eccentricities, we show that (i) the onset of chaos is determined by the overlap of two-body mean motion resonances (MMRs), like it is in two-planet systems; (ii) secular evolution causes the MMR widths to expand and contract adiabatically, so that the chaotic boundary is established where MMRs overlap

title: Nonunique Stationary States and Broken Universality in Birth Death Diffusion Processes
creator: Kartik Chhajed 1 and P. K. Mohanty 2
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Kartik Chhajed 1 and P. K. Mohanty 2. Systems with absorbing configurations usually lead to a unique stationary probability measure called quasi stationary state (QSS) defined with respect to the survived samples. We show that the birth death diffusion (BBD) processes exhibit universal phases and phase transitions when the birth and death rates depend on the instantaneous particle density and their time scales are exponentially separated from the diffusion rates.

title: A product-CLT and its application in invariance principle of random projection
creator: Juntao Duan, Ionel Popescu, Fan Zhou
description: Abstract Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma states random projections can be used as a topology preserving embedding technique for fixed vectors. In this paper, we try to understand how random projections affect probabilistic properties of random vectors. In particular we prove the distribution of inner product of two independent random vectors X , Z ∈ ℝ n X,Z\in\mathbb{R}^{n} with i.i.d.

title: Multi-task curriculum learning in a complex, visual, hard-exploration domain: Minecraft
creator: Ingmar Kanitscheider, Joost Huizinga, David Farhi, William Hebgen Guss Brandon Houghton , Raul Sampedro , Peter Zhokhov , Bowen Baker , Adrien Ecoffet , Jie Tang , Oleg Klimov , Jeff Clune OpenAI
description: Abstract An important challenge in reinforcement learning is training agents that can solve a wide variety of tasks. If tasks depend on each other (e.g. needing to learn to walk before learning to run), curriculum learning can speed up learning by focusing on the next best task to learn.

title: Bootstrapping the error of Oja’s algorithm
creator: Robert Lunde, Purnamrita Sarkar
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Robert Lunde, Purnamrita Sarkar. We consider the problem of quantifying uncertainty for the estimation error of the leading eigenvector from Oja’s algorithm for streaming principal component analysis, where the data are generated IID from some unknown distribution.

title: Modeling Clothing as a Separate Layer for an Animatable Human Avatar 334 Journal: TOG Volume: 40 6 1 12 DOI: 10.1145/3478513.3480545 CCS: Computing methodologies Image-based rendering CCS: Computing methodologies Animation
creator: Donglai Xiang, Fabian Prada, Timur Bagautdinov, Weipeng Xu, Yuan Dong, He Wen, Jessica Hodgins, Chenglei Wu
description: Abstract . We have recently seen great progress in building photorealistic animatable full-body codec avatars, but generating high-fidelity animation of clothing is still difficult. To address these difficulties, we propose a method to build an animatable clothed body avatar with an explicit representation of the clothing on the upper body from multi-view captured videos.

title: Gram quadrature: Numerical integration with Gram polynomials
creator: Irfan Muhammad
description: Abstract The numerical integration of an analytical function f ⁡ ( x ) f(x) using a finite set of equidistant points can be performed by quadrature formulas like the Newton-Cotes. Unlike Gaussian quadrature formulas however, higher-order Newton-Cotes formulas are not stable, limiting the usable order of such formulas.

title: A geometric way to find the measures of uncertainty from statistical divergences for discrete and finite probability distributions
creator: Gautam Sharma, Sk Sazim
description: Abstract Exploiting the geometric nature of statistical divergences, we devise a way to define associated induced uncertainty measures for discrete and finite probability distributions. We also report new uncertainty measures and discuss their properties. Further, we apply a similar technique to measure the uncertainty in the preparation of a quantum state.

title: Distance- k k locating-dominating sets in graphs
creator: Cong X. Kang, Eunjeong Yi Texas A&M University at Galveston, Galveston, TX 77553, USA, kangc@tamug.edu ; yie@tamug.edu
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Cong X. Kang, Eunjeong Yi Texas A&M University at Galveston, Galveston, TX 77553, USA, kangc@tamug.edu ; yie@tamug.edu. Let G G be a graph with vertex set V V , and let k k be a positive integer.

title: Rethinking Token-Mixing MLP for MLP-based Vision Backbone
creator: Tan Yu, Xu Li, Yunfeng Cai, Mingming Sun, Ping Li
description: Abstract In the past decade, we have witnessed rapid progress in the machine vision backbone. By introducing the inductive bias from the image processing, convolution neural network (CNN) has achieved excellent performance in numerous computer vision tasks and has been established as de facto backbone.

title: On estimating the cosmic molecular gas density from CO Line Intensity Mapping observations
creator: Patrick C. Breysse, Shengqi Yang, Rachel S. Somerville, Anthony R. Pullen, Gergö Popping, Abhishek S. Maniyar
description: Abstract The Millimeter-wave Intensity Mapping Experiment (mmIME) recently reported a detection of excess spatial fluctuations at a wavelength of 3 mm, which can be attributed to unresolved emission of several CO rotational transitions between z ∼ 1 − 5 z\sim 1-5 .

title: Signatures of inflowing gas in red geyser galaxies hosting radio-AGN
creator: Namrata Roy†, Kevin Bundy, Kate H. R. Rubin, Kate Rowlands , Kyle Westfall , Rogerio Riffel, Dmitry Bizyaev , David V. Stark , Rogemar A. Riffel, Ivan Lacerna , Preethi Nair , Xuanyi Wu , Niv Drory
description: Abstract We study cool neutral gas traced by NaD absorption in 140 local ( OPEN z < 0.1 ) \rm z<0.1) early-type “red geyser” galaxies. These galaxies show unique signatures in spatially-resolved strong-line emission maps that have been interpreted as large-scale active galactic nuclei driven ionized winds.

title: Neutrino-electron magnetohydrodynamics in an expanding Universe
creator: L. M. Perrone, G. Gregori, B. Reville, L. O. Silva, R. Bingham
description: Abstract We derive a new model for neutrino-plasma interactions in an expanding universe that incorporates the collective effects of the neutrinos on the plasma constituents. We start from the kinetic description of a multi-species plasma in the flat Friedmann-Robertson-Walker metric, where the particles are coupled to neutrinos through the charged- and neutral-current forms of the weak interaction.

title: From random point processes to hierarchical Cavity Master Equations for stochastic dynamics of disordered systems in Random Graphs: Ising models and epidemics
creator: D. Machado, R. Mulet
description: Abstract We start from the Theory of Random Point Processes to derive n-point coupled master equations describing the continuous dynamics of discrete variables in random graphs. These equations constitute a hierarchical set of approximations that generalize and improve the Cavity Master Equation (CME) previously obtained in CME-PRE .

title: Higher-order van Hove singularity in magic-angle twisted trilayer graphene
creator: Daniele Guerci, Pascal Simon, Christophe Mora
description: Abstract Twisted trilayer graphene (TTG) has recently emerged experimentally as a fascinating playground for studying correlated and exotic superconducting phases. We have found that TTG hosts a zero-energy higher-order van Hove singularity with an exponent − 1 / 3 -1/3 that is stronger than the one predicted in twisted bilayer graphene.

title: Toward a Better Understanding of Cosmic Chronometers: Stellar Population Properties of Passive Galaxies at Intermediate Redshift Astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2018 ) ; ChainConsumer ( Hinton 2016 ) ; emcee ( Foreman-Mackey et al. 2013 ) ; LOESS ( Cappellari et al. 2013a ) ; LtsFit ( Cappell
creator: Nicola Borghi, Michele Moresco, Andrea Cimatti, Alexandre Huchet, Salvatore Quai, Lucia Pozzetti
description: Abstract We take advantage of the publicly available LEGA-C spectroscopic survey to measure the stellar population properties of 140 individual massive and passive galaxies at z ∼ 0.7 z\sim 0.7 . We develop and publicly release PyLick , a flexible Python code to measure UV to near-IR spectral indices.

title: Curve graphs of surfaces with finite-invariance index 1 Thanks: The first author acknowledges support from NSF Grants DGE-1650044 and DMS-2002187. creator: Justin Lanier, Marissa Loving
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Justin Lanier, Marissa Loving. In this note we make progress toward a conjecture of Durham–Fanoni–Vlamis, showing that every infinite-type surface with finite-invariance index 1 1 and no nondisplaceable compact subsurfaces fails to have a good curve graph, that is, a connected graph where vertices represent homotopy classes of essential simple closed curves and where the natural mapping class group action has infinite diameter orbits. Our arguments use tools developed by Mann–Rafi in their study of the coarse geometry of big mapping class groups.

title: Striking the Right Balance: Recall Loss for Semantic Segmentation
creator: Junjiao Tian*, Niluthpol Mithun † \dagger, Zachary Seymour † \dagger, Han-Pang Chiu † \dagger, Zsolt Kira*
description: Abstract Class imbalance is a fundamental problem in computer vision applications such as semantic segmentation. Specifically, uneven class distributions in a training dataset often result in unsatisfactory performance on under-represented classes. Many works have proposed to weight the standard cross entropy loss function with pre-computed weights based on class statistics, such as the number of samples and class margins.

title: Constraining the Milky Way’s Ultraviolet to Infrared SED with Gaussian Process Regression 2021 Constraining the Milky Way’s Ultraviolet to Infrared SED with Gaussian Process Regression – D
creator: Catherine E. Fielder, Jeffrey A. Newman, Brett H. Andrews, Gail Zasowski, Nicholas F. Boardman, Tim Licquia, Karen L. Masters, Samir Salim
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Catherine E. Fielder, Jeffrey A. Newman, Brett H. Andrews, Gail Zasowski, Nicholas F. Boardman, Tim Licquia, Karen L. Masters, Samir Salim. Improving our knowledge of global Milky Way (MW) properties is critical for connecting the detailed measurements only possible from within our Galaxy to our understanding of the broader galaxy population.

title: Risk contributions of lambda quantiles History: Earlier versions have been presented at Birkbeck, University of London PhD Jamboree, the Mathematical and Statistical Methods for Actuarial Sciences and Finance 2020 Conference (eMAF) (virtual), and the 10th General Advanced Mathematical Methods for Fi
creator: A. INCE ∗,∤, I. PERI ∗,† and S. PESENTI ‡
description: Abstract Risk contributions of portfolios form an indispensable part of risk adjusted performance measurement. The risk contribution of a portfolio, e.g., in the Euler or Aumann-Shapley framework, is given by the partial derivatives of a risk measure applied to the portfolio profit and loss in direction of the asset units.

title: Extremal behavior of large cells in the Poisson hyperplane mosaic
creator: Moritz Otto
description: Abstract We study the asymptotic behavior of a size-marked point process of centers of large cells in a stationary and isotropic Poisson hyperplane mosaic in dimension d ≥ 2 d\geq 2 . The sizes of the cells are measured by their inradius or their k k th intrinsic volume ( k ≥ 2 k\geq 2 ), for example.

title: Multiphase Powerful Outflows Detected in High-z Quasars Journal: ApJ glafic ( Oguri 2010 , v1.1.6;) , SAS ( Gabriel et al. 2004 , v18;) , CIAO ( Fruscione et al. 2006 , v4.12;) , XSPEC ( Arnaud 1996 , v12;) , XSTAR photoionization model warmabs ( Kallman & Bautista 2001 ; Kallman et al. 1996 ) , Ast
creator: G. Chartas, M. Cappi, C. Vignali, M. Dadina, V. James, G. Lanzuisi, M. Giustini, M. Gaspari, S. Strickland, E. Bertola
description: Abstract We present results from a comprehensive study of ultrafast outflows (UFOs) detected in a sample of fourteen quasars, twelve of which are gravitationally lensed, in a redshift range of 1.41 – 3.91, near the peak of the AGN and star formation activity.

title: Minimal model for Hilbert space fragmentation with local constraints
creator: Bhaskar Mukherjee, Debasish Banerjee, K. Sengupta, Arnab Sen
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Bhaskar Mukherjee, Debasish Banerjee, K. Sengupta, Arnab Sen. Motivated by previous works on a Floquet version of the PXP model [Mukherjee et al. B 102, 075123 (2020), Mukherjee et al. B 101, 245107 (2020)], we study a one-dimensional spin- 1 / 2 1/2 lattice model with three-spin interactions in the same constrained Hilbert space (where all configurations with two adjacent S z = ↑ S^{z}=\uparrow spins are excluded).

title: Two-Hole Ground State: Dichotomy in Pairing Symmetry
creator: Jing-Yu Zhao, Shuai A. Chen, Hao-Kai Zhang, Zheng-Yu Weng
description: Abstract A single-hole ground state Ansatz for the two-dimensional t t - J J model has been recently studied by the variational Monte Carlo (VMC) method. Such a doped hole behaves like a “twisted” non-Landau quasiparticle characterized by an emergent quantum number in agreement with exact numerics.

title: Theoretical and computational analysis of the thermal quasi-geostrophic model
creator: D Crisan, DD Holm, E Luesink, PR Mensah, W Pan
description: Abstract . This work involves theoretical and numerical analysis of the Thermal Quasi-Geostrophic (TQG) model of submesoscale geophysical fluid dynamics (GFD). Physically, the TQG model involves thermal geostrophic balance, in which the Rossby number, the Froude number and the stratification parameter are all of the same asymptotic order.

title: Interaction driven Metal-Insulator Transition with Charge Fractionalization
creator: Yichen Xu, Xiao-Chuan Wu, Mengxing Ye, Zhu-Xi Luo, Chao-Ming Jian, Cenke Xu
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Yichen Xu, Xiao-Chuan Wu, Mengxing Ye, Zhu-Xi Luo, Chao-Ming Jian, Cenke Xu. It has been proposed that an extended version of the Hubbard model which potentially hosts rich correlated physics may be well simulated by the transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) moiré heterostructures. Motivated by recent reports of continuous metal-insulator transition (MIT) at half filling, as well as correlated insulators at various fractional fillings in TMD moiré heterostructures, we propose a theory for the potentially continuous MIT with fractionalized electric charges.

title: Achieving Real-Time Object Detection on Mobile Devices with Neural Pruning Search
creator: 1 Pu Zhao, 2 Wei Niu, 1 Geng Yuan, 1 Yuxuan Cai, 2 Bin Ren, 1 Yanzhi Wang, 1 Xue Lin
description: Abstract Object detection plays an important role in self-driving cars for security development. However, mobile systems on self-driving cars with limited computation resources lead to difficulties for object detection. To facilitate this, we propose a compiler-aware neural pruning search framework to achieve high-speed inference on autonomous vehicles for 2D and 3D object detection.

title: H H -theorem and boundary conditions for the linear R26 equations: application to flow past an evaporating droplet
creator: Anirudh S. Rana 1 , Vinay Kumar Gupta 2, James E. Sprittles 3, Manuel Torrilhon 4
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Anirudh S. Rana 1 , Vinay Kumar Gupta 2, James E. Sprittles 3, Manuel Torrilhon 4. Determining physically admissible boundary conditions for higher moments in an extended continuum model is recognised as a major obstacle.

title: On the proof of Taylor’s conjecture in multiply connected domains Journal: Applied Mathematics Letters
creator: Daniel Faraco, Sauli Lindberg, David MacTaggart, Alberto Valli
description: Abstract In this Letter we extend the proof, by Faraco and Lindberg [ 1 ] , of Taylor’s conjecture in multiply connected domains to cover arbitrary vector potentials and remove the need to impose conditions on the magnetic field due to gauge invariance.

title: An XMM–Newton Early-type Galaxy Atlas Journal: ApJS CIAO (v4.10; Fruscione et al. 2006 ), SAS (16.1.0; Gabriel et al. 2004 ), Sherpa ( Freeman et al. 2001 )
creator: Nazma Islam, Dong-Woo Kim, Kenneth Lin, Ewan O’Sullivan, Craig Anderson, Giuseppina Fabbiano, Jennifer Lauer, Douglas Morgan, Amy Mossman, Alessandro Paggi, Ginevra Trinchieri, Saeqa Vrtilek
description: Abstract The distribution of hot interstellar medium in early-type galaxies bears the imprint of the various astrophysical processes it underwent during its evolution. The X-ray observations of these galaxies have identified various structural features related to AGN and stellar feedback and environmental effects such as merging and sloshing.

title: Random groups at density d < 3 / 14 d<3/14 act non-trivially on a CAT(0) cube complex
creator: MurphyKate Montee
description: Abstract . For random groups in the Gromov density model at d < 3 / 14 d<3/14 , we construct walls in the Cayley complex X X which give rise to a non-trivial action by isometries on a CAT(0) cube complex.

title: Robust Control for a Class of Nonlinearly Coupled Hierarchical Systems with Actuator Faults Sponsor and financial support acknowledgment goes here. Paper titles should be written in uppercase and lowercase letters, not all uppercase.
creator: Sina Ameli, Olugbenga Moses Anubi
description: Abstract This paper proposes an approach to addresses the control challenges posed by a fault-induced uncertainty in both the dynamics and control input effectiveness of a class of hierarchical nonlinear systems in which the high-level dynamics is nonlinearly coupled with a multi-agent low-level dynamics.

title: Equations and improved coefficients for parallel transport in multicomponent collisional plasmas: method and application for tokamak modelling
creator: S. Makarov, D. Coster, V. Rozhansky, A. Stepanenko, E. Kaveeva, I. Senichenkov, V. Zhdanov, X. Bonnin
description: Abstract New analytical expressions for parallel transport coefficients in multicomponent collisional plasmas are presented in this paper. They are improved versions of the expressions written in [V. M. Zhdanov. Transport Processes in Multicomponent Plasma, vol. 44. 10 2002.], based on Grad’s 21N-moment method. Both explicit and approximate approaches for transport coefficients calculation are considered.

title: Data augmentation for deep learning based accelerated MRI reconstruction with limited data
creator: Zalan Fabian, Reinhard Heckel, Mahdi Soltanolkotabi
description: Abstract Deep neural networks have emerged as very successful tools for image restoration and reconstruction tasks. These networks are often trained end-to-end to directly reconstruct an image from a noisy or corrupted measurement of that image. To achieve state-of-the-art performance, training on large and diverse sets of images is considered critical.

title: A note on the modular representation on the ℤ / 2 \mathbb{Z}/2 -homology groups of the fourth power of real projective space and its application
creator: D - ặng Võ Phúc
description: Abstract We write B ​ V h BV_{h} for the classifying space of the elementary Abelian 2-group V h V_{h} of rank h , h, which is homotopy equivalent to the cartesian product of h h copies of ℝ ​ P ∞ . \mathbb{R}P^{\infty}.

title: Signature of topological non-trivial band structure in Ta 3 SiTe 6
creator: Shubhankar Roy, Ratnadwip Singha, Arup Ghosh, Prabhat Mandal
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Shubhankar Roy, Ratnadwip Singha, Arup Ghosh, Prabhat Mandal. The study of topology protected electronic properties is a fascinating topic in present day condensed matter physics research. New topological materials are frequently being proposed and explored through various experimental techniques. Ta 3 SiTe 6 is a newly predicted topological semimetal with fourfold degenerate nodal-line crossing in absence of spin-orbit coupling (SOC) and an hourglass Dirac loop, when SOC is included.

title: Interaction of the Galactic-Centre Super Bubbles with the Gaseous Disc
creator: Yoshiaki Sofue, Jun Kataoka 1. Institute of Astronomy, The University of Tokyo, Mitaka, Tokyo 181-0015, Japan2. Faculty of Science and Engineering, Waseda University, Shinjyuku, Tokyo, 169-8555, Japan
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Yoshiaki Sofue, Jun Kataoka 1. Institute of Astronomy, The University of Tokyo, Mitaka, Tokyo 181-0015, Japan2. Faculty of Science and Engineering, Waseda University, Shinjyuku, Tokyo, 169-8555, Japan. The interaction of Galactic-Centre (GC) super bubbles (GSB) with the gaseous disc and halo of the Milky Way is investigated using radio continuum, X-ray, HI and CO line surveys.

title: Phase Transition for a Family of Complex-driven Loewner Hulls
creator: Joan Lind, Jeffrey Utley
description: Abstract Building on H. Tran’s study of Loewner hulls generated by complex-valued driving functions, which showed the existence of a phase transition [ T ] , we answer the question of whether the phase transition for complex-driven hulls matches the phase transition for real-driven hulls.

title: Avis: In-Situ Model Checking for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
creator: Max Taylor, Haicheng Chen, Feng Qin, Christopher Stewart
description: Abstract Control firmware in unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) uses sensors to model and manage flight operations, from takeoff to landing to flying between waypoints. However, sensors can fail at any time during a flight. If control firmware mishandles sensor failures, UAVs can crash, fly away, or suffer other unsafe conditions.

title: Design Considerations for Data Daemons: Co-creating Design Futures to Explore Ethical Personal Data Management CCS: Human-centered computing Participatory design CCS: Human-centered computing Ambient intelligence
creator: Wiebke Toussaint, Olya Kudina, Aaron Yi Ding, Alejandra Gomez Ortega, Jered Vroon, Jacky Bourgeois, Julian Harty, Gürkan Solmaz, Ella Peltonen
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Wiebke Toussaint, Olya Kudina, Aaron Yi Ding, Alejandra Gomez Ortega, Jered Vroon, Jacky Bourgeois, Julian Harty, Gürkan Solmaz, Ella Peltonen. Mobile applications and online service providers track our virtual and physical behaviour more actively and with a broader scope than ever before. This has given rise to growing concerns about ethical personal data management. Even though regulation and awareness around data ethics are increasing, end-users are seldom engaged when defining and designing what a future with ethical personal data management should look like.

title: Discovery of two TNO-like bodies in the asteroid belt Journal: ApJ
creator: Sunao Hasegawa, Michaël Marsset, Francesca E. DeMeo, Schelte J. Bus, Jooyeon Geem, Masateru Ishiguro, Myungshin Im, Daisuke Kuroda, Pierre Vernazza
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Sunao Hasegawa, Michaël Marsset, Francesca E. DeMeo, Schelte J. Bus, Jooyeon Geem, Masateru Ishiguro, Myungshin Im, Daisuke Kuroda, Pierre Vernazza. Two extremely red main-belt asteroids: 203 Pompeja and 269 Justitia, were identified from combined visible and near-infrared spectroscopic observations collected at the IRTF and SAO observatories.

creator: Michael J. Chapman, Faizan G. Mohammad, Zhongxu Zhai, Will J. Percival, Jeremy L. Tinker, Julian E. Bautista, Joel R. Brownstein, Etienne Burtin, Kyle S. Dawson, Héctor Gil-Marín, Axel de la Macorra, Ashley J. Ross, Graziano Rossi, Donald P. Schneider, Gong-Bo Zhao
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Michael J. Chapman, Faizan G. Mohammad, Zhongxu Zhai, Will J. Percival, Jeremy L. Tinker, Julian E. Bautista, Joel R. Brownstein, Etienne Burtin, Kyle S. Dawson, Héctor Gil-Marín, Axel de la Macorra, Ashley J. Ross, Graziano Rossi, Donald P. Schneider, Gong-Bo Zhao. We measure the small-scale clustering of the Data Release 16 extended Baryon Oscillation Spectroscopic Survey Luminous Red Galaxy sample, corrected for fibre-collisions using Pairwise Inverse Probability weights, which give unbiased clustering measurements on all scales.

description: Abstract Robustness against adversarial attacks has recently been at the forefront of algorithmic design for machine learning tasks. In the adversarial streaming model, an adversary gives an algorithm a sequence of adaptively chosen updates u 1 , … , u n u_{1},\ldots,u_{n} as a data stream.

title: TOI-942b: A Prograde Neptune in a ∼ ​ 60 \mathord{\sim}60 Myr old Multi-transiting System Journal: ApJL This paper includes data gathered with the 6.5 meter Magellan Telescopes located at Las Campanas Observatory, Chile. emcee ( Foreman-Mackey et al. 2013 ) , batman ( Kreidberg 2015 )
creator: Christopher P. Wirth, George Zhou, Samuel N. Quinn, Andrew W. Mann, Luke G. Bouma, David W. Latham, Johanna K. Teske, Sharon X. Wang, Stephen A. Shectman, R.P. Butler, Jeffrey D. Crane
description: Abstract Mapping the orbital obliquity distribution of young planets is one avenue towards understanding mechanisms that sculpt the architectures of planetary systems. TOI-942 is a young field star, with an age of ∼ ​ 60 \mathord{\sim}60 Myr, hosting a planetary system consisting of two transiting Neptune-sized planets in 4.3- and 10.1-day period orbits.

title: Dynamic Connectivity in Disk Graphs
creator: Alexander Baumann, Haim Kaplan, Katharina Klost, Kristin Knorr, Wolfgang Mulzer, Liam Roditty, Paul Seiferth
description: Abstract Let S ⊆ ℝ 2 S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{2} be a set of n n sites in the plane, so that every site s ∈ S s\in S has an associated radius r s > 0 r_{s}>0 . Let 𝒟 ⁡ ( S ) \mathcal{D}(S) be the disk intersection graph defined by S S , i.e.

title: Solving the puzzle of nuclear stopping power
creator: Marek Jeżabek 1 and Andrzej Rybicki 1
description: Abstract This paper reviews our recent findings on the dynamics of transport of baryon number in proton-induced reactions at the CERN SPS. These are put in a more general context of the present understanding of baryon stopping phenomena up to LHC and cosmic ray energies.

title: On closures for reduced order models – A spectrum of first-principle to machine-learned avenues
creator: Shady E. Ahmed, Suraj Pawar, Omer San, Adil Rasheed, Traian Iliescu, Bernd R. Noack
description: Abstract For over a century, reduced order models (ROMs) have been a fundamental discipline of theoretical fluid mechanics. Early examples include Galerkin models inspired by the Orr-Sommerfeld stability equation and numerous vortex models, of which the von Kármán vortex street is one of the most prominent.

title: From Seiberg-Witten to Gromov: MCE and Singular Symplectic Forms
creator: Yi-Jen Lee
description: Abstract Motivated by various possible generalizations of Taubes’s S ​ W = G ​ r SW=Gr theorem [ T ] to Floer-theoretic setting, we prove certain variants of Taubes’s convergence theorem in [ T ] (the first part of his proof of S ​ W = G ​ r SW=Gr ).

title: LYCEN 2021-01 Epidemiological theory of virus variants
creator: Giacomo Cacciapaglia, Corentin Cot, Adele de Hoffer, Stefan Hohenegger, Francesco Sannino, Shahram Vatani
