creator: Haifeng Tian, Xiankun Du, Hongyu Jia
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Haifeng Tian, Xiankun Du, Hongyu Jia. Let K K be a field of characteristic zero. We prove that images of a linear K K -derivation and a linear K K - ℰ \mathcal{E} -derivation of the ring K ⁡ [ x 1 , x 2 , x 3 ] K[x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}] of polynomial in three variables over K K are Mathieu-Zhao subspaces, which affirms the LFED conjecture for linear K K -derivations and linear K K - ℰ \mathcal{E} -derivations of K ⁡ [ x

title: On fractional semidiscrete Dirac operators of Lévy-Leblond type Journal: arXiv.org
creator: N. Faustino, Center for R&D in Mathematics and Applications (CIDMA)
description: Abstract In this paper we introduce a wide class of space-fractional and time-fractional semidiscrete Dirac operators of Lévy-Leblond type on the semidiscrete space-time lattice h ​ ℤ n × [ 0 , ∞ ) h{\mathbb{Z}}^{n}\times[0,\infty) ( h > 0 h>0 ), resembling to fractional semidiscrete counterparts of the so-called parabolic Dirac operators.

title: PAN++: Towards Efficient and Accurate End-to-End Spotting of Arbitrarily-Shaped Text
creator: Wenhai Wang, Enze Xie, Xiang Li, Xuebo Liu, Ding Liang, Zhibo Yang, Tong Lu, Chunhua Shen
description: Abstract Scene text detection and recognition have been well explored in the past few years. Despite the progress, efficient and accurate end-to-end spotting of arbitrarily-shaped text remains challenging. In this work, we propose an end-to-end text spotting framework, termed PAN++, which can efficiently detect and recognize text of arbitrary shapes in natural scenes.

title: TE-ESN: Time Encoding Echo State Network for Prediction Based on Irregularly Sampled Time Series Data
creator: Chenxi Sun, Shenda Hong, Moxian Song, Yanxiu Zhou, Yongyue Sun, Derun Cai, Hongyan Li
description: Abstract Prediction based on Irregularly Sampled Time Series (ISTS) is of wide concern in the real-world applications. For more accurate prediction, the methods had better grasp more data characteristics. Different from ordinary time series, ISTS is characterised with irregular time intervals of intra-series and different sampling rates of inter-series.

title: Non-asymptotic Excess Risk Bounds for Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
creator: Guohao Shen ghshen@link.cuhk.edu.hkDepartment of StatisticsThe Chinese University of Hong KongHong Kong, China, Yuling Jiao yulingjiaomath@whu.edu.cnSchool of Mathematics and StatisticsWuhan UniversityWuhan, Hubei, China 430072Yuanyuan Lin ylin@sta.cuhk.edu.hkDepartment of StatisticsThe Chinese Univ
description: Abstract In this paper, we consider the problem of binary classification with a class of general deep convolutional neural networks, which includes fully-connected neural networks and fully convolutional neural networks as special cases. We establish non-asymptotic excess risk bounds for a class of convex surrogate losses and target functions with different modulus of continuity.

title: Deeply virtual Compton scattering off Helium nuclei with positron beams
creator: Sara Fucini, Mohammad Hattawy, Matteo Rinaldi, Sergio Scopetta
description: Abstract Positron initiated deeply virtual Compton scattering (DVCS) off 4 He and 3 He nuclei is described. The way the so-called d − d- term could be obtained from the real part of the relevant Compton form factor is summarized, and the importance and novelty of this measurement is discussed.

title: Many-body molecule formation at a domain wall in a one-dimensional strongly interacting ultracold Fermi gas
creator: Andrzej Syrwid, Maciej Łebek, Piotr T. Grochowski, Kazimierz Rzążewski
description: Abstract We analyze how the presence of the bound state on top of strong intercomponent contact repulsion affects the dynamics of a two-component ultracold Fermi gas confined in a one-dimensional harmonic trap. By performing full many-body numerical calculations, we retrieve dynamics of an initially phase separated state that has been utilized to excite the spin-dipole mode in experimental settings.

title: Cost vector analysis & multi-path entanglement routing in quantum networks
creator: Hudson Leone, Ashe Miller, Deepesh Singh, Nathan K. Langford, Peter P. Rohde
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Hudson Leone, Ashe Miller, Deepesh Singh, Nathan K. Langford, Peter P. Rohde. We present a static framework for analysing quantum routing protocols that we call the cost-vector formalism . Here, quantum networks are recast as multi-graphs where edges represent two-qubit entanglement resources that could exist under some sequence of operations. Each edge is weighted with a transmission probability that represents the likelihood of the pair existing and a coherence probability which is the likelihood that the pair is suitable for teleportation.

title: Divergence Scaling for Distribution Matching
creator: Gerhard Kramer
description: Abstract Distribution matchers for finite alphabets are shown to have informational divergences that grow logarithmically with the block length, generalizing a basic result for binary strings. I Introduction Distribution matchers (DMs) are random number generators with a one-to-one mapping [ 1 ] . An important application of DMs is probabilistic amplitude shaping for energy-efficient communication [ 2 ] .

title: Formalizing Stack Safety as a Security Property
creator: Sean Noble Anderson, Roberto Blanco, Leonidas Lampropoulos, Benjamin C. Pierce, Andrew Tolmach
description: Abstract The term stack safety is used to describe a variety of compiler, run-time, and hardware mechanisms for protecting stack memory. Unlike “the heap,” the ISA-level stack does not correspond to a single high-level language concept: different compilers use it in different ways to support procedural and functional abstraction mechanisms from a wide range of languages.

title: Rational and p p -adic analogs of J.H.C. Whitehead’s conjecture
creator: A. M. Mikhovich
description: Abstract We show that subpresentations of aspherical prounipotent presentations over fields of zero characteristics and subpresentations of aspherical pro- p p -presentations are aspherical; an application to subpresentations of aspherical discrete presentations is also included. Following Bousfield-Kan, Quillen and Sullivan the results are regarded as affirmative answers to rational and p p -adic analogs of J.H.C. Whitehead’s conjecture.

title: DRIVE: Machine Learning to Identify Drivers of Cancer with High-Dimensional Genomic Data & Imputed Labels
creator: Adnan Akbar, Andrey Solovyev, John W Cassidy, Nirmesh Patel, Harry W Clifford
description: Abstract Identifying the mutations that drive cancer growth is key in clinical decision making and precision oncology. As driver mutations confer selective advantage and thus have an increased likelihood of occurrence, frequency-based statistical models are currently favoured. These methods are not suited to rare, low frequency, driver mutations.

title: Fixed Point Constructions in Tilings and Cellular Automata
creator: Ilkka Törmä
description: Abstract The fixed point construction is a method for designing tile sets and cellular automata with highly nontrivial dynamical and computational properties. It produces an infinite hierarchy of systems where each layer simulates the next one. The simulations are implemented entirely by computations of Turing machines embedded in the tilings or spacetime diagrams.

title: Weighted completion time minimization for capacitated parallel machines
creator: Ilan Reuven Cohen, Izack Cohen, Iyar Zaks
description: Abstract We consider the weighted completion time minimization problem for capacitated parallel machines, which is a fundamental problem in modern cloud computing environments. We study settings in which the processed jobs may have varying duration, resource requirements and importance (weight). Each server (machine) can process multiple concurrent jobs up to its capacity.

title: Event Argument Extraction using Causal Knowledge Structures
creator: Debanjana Kar, Sudeshna Sarkar, Pawan Goyal
description: Abstract Event Argument extraction refers to the task of extracting structured information from unstructured text for a particular event of interest. The existing works exhibit poor capabilities to extract causal event arguments like Reason and After Effects. Furthermore, most of the existing works model this task at a sentence level, restricting the context to a local scope.

title: Charged Anisotropic Finch-Skea-Bardeen Spheres
creator: M. Farasat Shamir, G. Mustafa, Mushtaq Ahmad
description: Abstract This manuscript explores the compact geometries by employing Karmarkar condition with the charged anisotropic source of matter distribution. For this purpose, we consider an explicit model by indulging g r ​ r \mathrm{g}_{rr} metric potential obeying the Karmarkar condition. Moreover, we ansatz the time metric co-efficient following the approach by Adler Adler .

title: Magnetic Relaxation in Two Dimensional Assembly of Dipolar Interacting Nanoparticles
creator: Manish Anand
description: Abstract Using the two-level approximation of the energy barrier, we perform extensive kinetic Monte Carlo simulations to probe the relaxation characteristics in a two-dimensional ( L x × L y L_{x}\times L_{y} ) array of magnetic nanoparticle as a function of dipolar interaction strength h d h_{d} , aspect ratio A r = L y / L x A_{r}=L_{y}/L_{x} ,

title: Forming pressure-traps at the snow-line to isolate isotopic reservoirs in the absence of a planet.
creator: S. Charnoz, G. Avice, R. Hyodo, F. C. Pignatale, M. Chaussidon
description: Abstract Context. Pressure maxima are regions in protoplanetary disks where pebbles can be trapped because of the local absence of pressure gradient. These regions could be ideal places to form planetesimals or to isolate isotopic reservoirs. Observations of protoplanetary disks show that dusty rings structures are common, and pressure maxima are sometime invoked as a possible explanation.

title: The use of astronomy VLBA campaign MOJAVE for geodesy Journal: Journal of Geodesy
creator: Hana Krásná, Leonid Petrov
description: Abstract We investigated the suitability of the astronomical 15 GHz VLBA observing program MOJAVE-5 for estimation of geodetic parameters, such as station coordinates and Earth orientation parameters. We processed contemporary geodetic dual-band RV and CN experiments observed at 2.3 GHz and 8.6 GHz starting on September 2016 through July 2020 as reference dataset.

title: Unconventional anomalous Hall effect from magnetization parallel to the electric field
creator: Hengxin Tan, Yizhou Liu, Binghai Yan
description: Abstract In the anomalous Hall effect (AHE), the magnetization, electric field and the Hall current are presumed to be mutually vertical to each other. In this work, we propose an unconventional AHE where the magnetization, the electric field and Hall current stay inside the same plane.

title: Stability of energy landscape for Ising models
creator: Bruno Hideki Fukushima-Kimura Akira Sakai Hisayoshi Toyokawa Yuki Ueda
description: Abstract In this paper, we explore the stability of the energy landscape of an Ising Hamiltonian when subjected to two kinds of perturbations: a perturbation on the coupling coefficients and external fields, and a perturbation on the underlying graph structure.

title: Curious Exploration and Return-based Memory Restoration for Deep Reinforcement Learning
creator: Saeed Tafazzol, Erfan Fathi, Mahdi Rezaei, Ehsan Asali
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Saeed Tafazzol, Erfan Fathi, Mahdi Rezaei, Ehsan Asali. Reward engineering and designing an incentive reward function are non-trivial tasks to train agents in complex environments. Furthermore, an inaccurate reward function may lead to a biased behaviour which is far from an efficient and optimised behaviour. In this paper, we focus on training a single agent to score goals with binary success/failure reward function in Half Field Offense domain.

title: Ab-initio calculations for electronic and optical properties of Er W defects in tungsten disulfide
creator: M. A. Khan, Michael N. Leuenberger
description: Abstract Ab-initio calculations for the electronic and optical properties of single-layer (SL) tungsten disulfide (WS 2 ) in the presence of substitutional Erbium defects (Er W ) are presented, where the W atom is replaced by an Er atom. Defects usually play an important role in tailoring electronic and optical properties of semiconductors.

title: A model of inter-organizational network formation
creator: Shweta Gaonkar, Angelo Mele
description: Abstract How do inter-organizational networks emerge? Accounting for interdependence among ties while studying tie formation is one of the key challenges in this area of research. We address this challenge using an equilibrium framework where firms’ decisions to form links with other firms are modeled as a strategic game.

title: In-cell Discontinuous Reconstruction path-conservative methods for non conservative hyperbolic systems - Second-order extension Journal: Journal of Computational Physics
creator: Ernesto Pimentel-García, Manuel J. Castro, Christophe Chalons, Tomás Morales de Luna, Carlos Parés
description: Abstract We are interested in the numerical approximation of discontinuous solutions in non conservative hyperbolic systems. An extension to second-order of a new strategy based on in-cell discontinuous reconstructions to deal with this challenging topic is presented. This extension is based on the combination of the first-order in-cell reconstruction and the MUSCL-Hancock reconstruction.

title: A tight compact quadratically constrained convex relaxation of the Optimal Power Flow problem
creator: Amélie Lambert
description: Abstract In this paper, we consider the optimal power flow (OPF) problem which consists in determining the power production at each bus of an electric network by minimizing the production cost. Our contribution is an exact solution algorithm for the OPF problem. It consits in a spatial branch-and-bound algorithm based on a compact quadratically constrained convex relaxation.

title: Selective Inference in Propensity Score Analysis
creator: Yoshiyuki Ninomiya, Yuta Umezu, Ichiro Takeuchi
description: Abstract Selective inference (post-selection inference) is a methodology that has attracted much attention in recent years in the fields of statistics and machine learning. Naive inference based on data that are also used for model selection tends to show an overestimation, and so the selective inference conditions the event that the model was selected.

title: Augmenting Sequential Recommendation with Pseudo-Prior Items via Reversely Pre-training Transformer Conference: Proceedings of the 44th International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval; July 11–15, 2021; Virtual Event, Canada Proceedings of the 44th Internation
creator: Zhiwei Liu*, Ziwei Fan*, Yu Wang, Philip S. Yu
description: Abstract . Sequential Recommendation characterizes the evolving patterns by modeling item sequences chronologically. The essential target of it is to capture the item transition correlations. The recent developments of transformer inspire the community to design effective sequence encoders, e.g., SASRec and BERT4Rec. However, we observe that these transformer-based models suffer from the cold-start issue, i.e., performing poorly for short sequences.

title: CDR Based Trajectories: Tentative for Filtering Ping-pong Handover
creator: Joonas Lõmps, Artjom Lind, Amnir Hadachi
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Joonas Lõmps, Artjom Lind, Amnir Hadachi. Call Detail Records (CDRs) coupled with the coverage area locations provide the operator with an incredible amount of information on its customers’ whereabouts and movement. Due to the non-static and overlapping nature of the antenna coverage area there commonly exist situations where cellphones geographically close to each other can be connected to different antennas due to handover rule - the operator hands over a certain cellphone to another antenna to spread the load between antennas.

title: Flow-induced flapping of an inverted flag with non-uniform stiffness distribution
creator: Andres Goza 1
description: Abstract We perform high-fidelity, two-dimensional (2D), fluid-structure interaction (FSI) simulations at a Reynolds number of R ​ e = 200 Re=200 of uniform flow past an inverted flag (i.e., clamped at its trailing edge). The inverted flag system can exhibit large-amplitude flapping motions (on the order of the flag length) that can be converted to electricity via, e.g., piezoelectric materials.
