title: Higher-dimensional minimal theory of mass-varying massive gravity and its cosmological consequences
creator: Ahmad Khoirul Falah, Andy Octavian Latief, Husin Alatas, Bobby Eka Gunara
description: Abstract In this paper we construct higher-dimensional minimal theory of mass-varying massive gravity (MTMVMG) where the masslike scalar potential is coupled to a vielbein potential, unlike in the previous literature where it is coupled to metric, such that the number of graviton degrees of freedom in the theory is the same as in general relativity.

title: gComm: An environment for investigating generalization in Grounded Language Acquisition
creator: Rishi Hazra, Sonu Dixit
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Rishi Hazra, Sonu Dixit. gComm 1 1 1 codes & baselines: https//github.com/SonuDixit/gComm is a step towards developing a robust platform to foster research in grounded language acquisition in a more challenging and realistic setting. It comprises a 2-d grid environment with a set of agents (a stationary speaker and a mobile listener connected via a communication channel) exposed to a continuous array of tasks in a partially observable setting.

title: Computationally Efficient Dynamic Traffic Optimization Of Railway Systems
creator: Robin Vujanic, and Andrew J. Hill
description: Abstract In this paper, we investigate dynamic traffic optimization in railway systems, i.e., the behavior of these systems through time when their movements are dictated by solutions to optimization models with finite horizons. As interactions between trains are not considered beyond the limits of finite horizons, the danger of leading the system into a deadlock arises.

title: The extremal length systole of the Bolza surface
creator: Maxime Fortier Bourque, Dídac Martínez-Granado, Franco Vargas Pallete
description: Abstract . We prove that the extremal length systole of genus two surfaces attains a strict local maximum at the Bolza surface, where it takes the value 2 \sqrt{2} . 1. Introduction Extremal length is a conformal invariant that plays an important role in complex analysis, complex dynamics, and Teichmüller theory [ Ahl06 , Ahl10 , Jen58 ] .

title: Differentiable Neural Architecture Search for Extremely Lightweight Image Super-Resolution PubID: pubid: Copyright © 2022 IEEE. Personal use of this material is permitted. However, permission to use this material for any other purposes must be obtained from the IEEE by sending an email to pubs-permi
creator: Han Huang, Li Shen, Chaoyang He, Weisheng Dong, Wei Liu
description: Abstract Single Image Super-Resolution (SISR) tasks have achieved significant performance with deep neural networks. However, the large number of parameters in CNN-based met-hods for SISR tasks require heavy computations. Although several efficient SISR models have been recently proposed, most are handcrafted and thus lack flexibility.

title: A short note on relative entropy for a pair of intermediate subfactors Thanks: The first named author was supported through a DST INSPIRE Faculty grant (reference no. DST/INSPIRE/04/2019/002754).
creator: Keshab Chandra Bakshi
description: Abstract . Given a quadruple of finite index subfactors we explicitly compute the Pimsner-Popa probabilistic constant for the pair of intermediate subfactors and relate it with the corresponding Connes-Størmer relative entropy between them. This generalizes an old result of Pimsner and Popa. 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification 46L37 1.

title: Block designs and prime values of polynomials
creator: Gareth A. Jones and Alexander K. Zvonkin
description: Abstract . A recent construction by Amarra, Devillers and Praeger of block designs with specific parameters depends on certain quadratic polynomials, with integer coefficients, taking prime power values. The Bunyakovsky Conjecture, if true, would imply that each of them takes infinitely many prime values, giving an infinite family of block designs with the required parameters.

title: Quantum Machine Learning For Classical Data
creator: Leonard P. Wossnig
description: Abstract In this dissertation, we study the intersection of quantum computing and supervised machine learning algorithms, which means that we investigate quantum algorithms for supervised machine learning that operate on classical data. This area of research falls under the umbrella of quantum machine learning , a research area of computer science which has recently received wide attention.

title: Quantum Back Flow Across a Black Hole Horizon in a Toy Model Approach
creator: Dripto Biswas, Subir Ghosh
description: Abstract Quantum Back Flow (QBF), discovered quite a few years back, is a generic purely quantum phenomenon, in which the probability of finding a particle in a direction is non-zero (and increasing for a certain period of time) even when the particle has with certainty a velocity in the opposite direction.

title: Coexistence of hourglass Weyl and Dirac nodal line phonons in orthorhombic-type KCuS
creator: Jianhua Wang, Hongkuan Yuan, Ying Liu, Feng Zhou, Juntao Ma, Minquan Kuang, Tie Yang, Xiaotian Wang, Gang Zhang
description: Abstract In parallel to electronic systems, the concept of topology has been extended to phonons, which has led to the birth of topological phonons. Very recently, nodal point phonons, nodal line phonons, and nodal surface phonons have been proposed, and a handful of candidate materials have been predicted in solid-state materials.

title: Mutually Unbiased Balanced Functions & Generalized Random Access Codes
creator: Vaisakh M, Ram krishna Patra, Mukta Janpandit, Samrat Sen, Anubhav Chaturvedi, Manik Banik
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Vaisakh M, Ram krishna Patra, Mukta Janpandit, Samrat Sen, Anubhav Chaturvedi, Manik Banik. Quantum resources and protocols are known to outperform their classical counterparts in variety of communication and information processing tasks. Random Access Codes (RACs) are one such cryptographically significant family of bipartite communication tasks, wherein, the sender encodes a data set (typically a string of input bits) onto a physical system of bounded dimension and transmits it to the receiver, who then attempts to guess a randomly chosen part of the sender’s

title: Heron triangles and a family of elliptic curves with rank zero
creator: Vinodkumar Ghale, Shamik Das, Debopam Chakraborty
description: Abstract 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification Primary 11D25, 51M04, 11G05; Secondary 11R11, 11R27, 11R29 Abstract Given any positive integer n , it is well-known that there always exists a triangle with rational sides a,b and c such that the area of the triangle is n .

title: Mirror-extended standard model with spontaneously broken left-right symmetry and its implementation in the course of cosmological evolution
creator: Alexander B. Kaganovich
description: Abstract A mirror-extended standard model (MESM) is offered, where in the left-right symmetric underlying action the sector of the standard model (SM) and its mirror copy have the same S ​ U ​ ( 2 ) × U ⁡ ( 1 ) SU(2)\times U(1) gauge structure and parameters; the mirror fermion counter-partners have opposite chiralities.

title: On the Kato square root problem
creator: Yury Arlinskiĭ
description: Abstract . In the infinite-dimensional separable complex Hilbert space we construct new abstract examples of unbounded maximal accretive and maximal sectorial operators B B for which dom ​ B 1 2 ≠ dom ​ B ∗ 1 2 {\rm dom\,}B^{\frac{1}{2}}\neq{\rm dom\,}B^{*{\frac{1}{2}}} . New criterions for the equality are established. 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification Primary 47B12, 47B44; Secondary 47A05 1.

title: Understanding the Role of Affect Dimensions in Detecting Emotions from Tweets: A Multi-task Approach Conference: Proceedings of the 44th International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval; July 11–15, 2021; Virtual Event, Canada Proceedings of the 44th Internatio
creator: Rajdeep Mukherjee, Atharva Naik, Sriyash Poddar, Soham Dasgupta, Niloy Ganguly
description: Abstract . We propose VADEC , a multi-task framework that exploits the correlation between the categorical and dimensional models of emotion representation for better subjectivity analysis. Focusing primarily on the effective detection of emotions from tweets, we jointly train multi-label emotion classification and multi-dimensional emotion regression , thereby utilizing the inter-relatedness between the tasks.

title: Convergence to the thermodynamic limit for random-field random surfaces
creator: Paul Dario
description: Abstract . We study random surfaces with a uniformly convex gradient interaction in the presence of quenched disorder taking the form of a random independent external field. Previous work on the model has focused on proving existence and uniqueness of infinite-volume gradient Gibbs measures with a given tilt and on studying the fluctuations of the surface and its discrete gradient.

title: Advising Agent for Service-Providing Live-Chat Operators
creator: Aviram Aviv, Yaniv Oshrat, Samuel A. Assefa, Tobi Mustapha, Daniel Borrajo, Manuela Veloso, Sarit Kraus
description: Abstract Call centers, in which human operators attend clients using textual chat, are very common in modern e-commerce. Training enough skilled operators who are able to provide good service is a challenge. We suggest an algorithm and a method to train and implement an assisting agent that provides on-line advice to operators while they attend clients.

title: Parametric binomial sums involving harmonic numbers
creator: necdet batır
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by necdet batır. We present explicit formulas for the following family of parametric binomial sums involving harmonic numbers for p = 0 , 1 , 2 p=0,1,2 and | t | ≤ 1 |t|\leq 1 . ∑ k = 1 ∞ H k − 1 ​ t k k p ​ ( n + k k ) and ∑ k = 1 ∞ t k k p ​ ( n + k k ) . \sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{H_{k-1}t^{k}}{k^{p}\binom{n+k}{k}}\quad\mbox{and}\quad\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{t^{k}}{k^{p}\binom{n+k}{k}}.

title: Unit Ball Model for Embedding Hierarchical Structures in the Complex Hyperbolic Space DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: Make sure to enter the correct conference title from your rights confirmation emai; June 03–05, 2018; Woodstock, NY Price: 15.00 ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/18/06
creator: Huiru Xiao, Caigao Jiang, Yangqiu Song, James Zhang, Junwu Xiong
description: Abstract . Learning the representation of data with hierarchical structures in the hyperbolic space attracts increasing attention in recent years. Due to the constant negative curvature, the hyperbolic space resembles tree metrics and captures the tree-like properties naturally, which enables the hyperbolic embeddings to improve over traditional Euclidean models.

title: Coercive Inequalities on Carnot Groups: Taming Singularities
creator: E. Bou Dagher, B. Zegarliński
description: Abstract In the setting of Carnot groups, we propose an approach of taming singularities to get coercive inequalities. To this end, we develop a technique to introduce natural singularities in the energy function U U in order to force one of the coercivity conditions.

title: Improving Patent Mining and Relevance Classification using Transformers Thanks: 6th National Conference on Practical Applications of Artificial Intelligence, 2021, Bordeaux, France
creator: Théo Ding, Walter Vermeiren, Sylvie Ranwez, Binbin Xu
description: Abstract Patent analysis and mining are time-consuming and costly processes for companies, but nevertheless essential if they are willing to remain competitive. To face the overload induced by numerous patents, the idea is to automatically filter them, bringing only few to read to experts.

title: CHARACTERIZING ALTERNATING SIGN TRIANGLES Thanks: This project was supported by the University of Minnesota’s Office of Undergraduate Research.
creator: SON NGUYEN
description: Abstract \justify Alternating sign triangles were introduced by Carroll and Speyer in relation to cube recurrence, by analogy to alternating sign matrices for octahedron recurrence. Permutation triangles are the alternating sign triangles whose entries are either 0 0 or 1 1 , by analogy with permutation matrices.

title: Dispatcher: A Message-Passing Approach To Language Modelling.
creator: Alberto Cetoli
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Alberto Cetoli. This paper proposes a message-passing mechanism to address language modelling. A new layer type is introduced that aims to substitute self-attention for unidirectional sequence generation tasks. The system is shown to be competitive with existing methods: Given N N tokens, the computational complexity is 𝒪 ⁡ ( N ​ log ​ N ) \mathcal{O}(N\,\mathrm{log}N) and the memory complexity is 𝒪 ⁡ ( N ) \mathcal{O}(N) under reasonable assumptions.

title: Stochastic Multi-Armed Bandits with Control Variates
creator: Arun Verma, Manjesh K. Hanawal
description: Abstract This paper studies a new variant of the stochastic multi-armed bandits problem where auxiliary information about the arm rewards is available in the form of control variates. In many applications like queuing and wireless networks, the arm rewards are functions of some exogenous variables.

title: Strong anomaly and phases of chiral gauge theories
creator: Stefano Bolognesi, Kenichi Konishi, Andrea Luzio, [13pt] Department of Physics “E. Fermi”, University of Pisa, [-5pt] Largo Pontecorvo, 3, Ed. C, 56127 Pisa, Italy, [2pt] INFN, Sezione di Pisa, Largo Pontecorvo, 3, Ed. C, 56127 Pisa, Italy, [2pt] Scuola Normale Superiore, Piazza dei Cavalieri, 7, 56
description: Abstract We present a simple argument which seems to favor, when applied to a large class of strongly-coupled chiral gauge theories, a dynamical-Higgs-phase scenario, characterized by certain bifermion condensates. Flavor symmetric confining vacua described in the infrared by a set of baryonlike massless composite fermions saturating the conventional ’t Hooft anomaly matching equations, appear instead disfavored.

title: Fast n n -fold Boolean Convolution via Additive Combinatorics This work is part of the project TIPEA that has received funding from the European Research Council (ERC) under the European Unions Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme (grant agreement No. 850979).
creator: Karl Bringmann Vasileios Nakos
description: Abstract We consider the problem of computing the Boolean convolution (with wraparound) of n n vectors of dimension m m , or, equivalently, the problem of computing the sumset A 1 + A 2 + … + A n A_{1}+A_{2}+\ldots+A_{n} for A 1 , … , A n ⊆ ℤ m A_{1},\ldots,A_{n}\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_{m} .

title: Quantum phase transition in overdoped La 2-x Sr x CuO 4 evinced by the superfluid density
creator: T. Schneider
description: Abstract The superfluid density ρ ∥ s f ( T ) = λ ∥ − 2 ( T ) \rho_{\|sf}\left(T\right)=\lambda_{\|}^{-2}\left(T\right) of overdoped La 2-x Sr x CuO 4 thin films of high quality have been measured with T c T_{c} (defined by the onset of the Meissner effect ) from 5.1 5.1 to 41.6 41.6 K by Božović et al.

title: Higgs boson tagging with the Lund jet plane
creator: Charanjit K. Khosa, Simone Marzani
description: Abstract We construct a procedure to separate boosted Higgs bosons decaying into hadrons, from the background due to strong interactions. We employ the Lund jet plane to obtain a theoretically well-motivated representation of the jets of interest and we use the resulting images as the input to a convolutional neural network classifier.

title: Persistent plasma waves in interstellar space detected by Voyager 1
creator: Stella Koch Ocker, James M. Cordes, Shami Chatterjee, Donald A. Gurnett, William S. Kurth, Steven R. Spangler
description: Abstract In 2012, Voyager 1 became the first in situ probe of the very local interstellar medium 1 . The Voyager 1 Plasma Wave System has given point estimates of the plasma density spanning about 30 au of interstellar space, revealing a large-scale density gradient 2 , 3 and turbulence 4 outside the heliopause.

title: Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia Detection from Microscopic Images Using Weighted Ensemble of Convolutional Neural Networks Journal: Informatics in Medicine Unlocked
creator: Chayan Mondal, Md. Kamrul Hasan, Md. Tasnim Jawad, Aishwariya Dutta, Md. Rabiul Islam, Md. Abdul Awal, Mohiuddin Ahmad
description: Abstract Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL) is a blood cell cancer characterized by numerous immature lymphocytes. Even though automation in ALL prognosis is an essential aspect of cancer diagnosis, it is challenging due to the morphological correlation between malignant and normal cells.

title: Manipulating single photon emitter radiative lifetime in transition-metal dichalcogenides through Förster resonance energy transfer to graphene
creator: R.Eddhib 1, S.Ayari 1, A.Hichri 1, S.Jaziri 1 , 2
description: Abstract Structural defects can crucially impact the optical response of monolayer (ML) thick materials as they enable trapping sites for excitons. These trapped excitons appear in photoluminescence spectra as new emissions below the free bright exciton and it can be exploited for single photon emissions (SPE).

title: Ultra-Heavy Dark Matter Search with Electron Microscopy of Geological Quartz
creator: Reza Ebadi †, Anubhav Mathur, Erwin H. Tanin, Nicholas D. Tailby, Mason C. Marshall, Aakash Ravi, Raisa Trubko, Roger R. Fu, David F. Phillips, Surjeet Rajendran, Ronald L. Walsworth
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Reza Ebadi †, Anubhav Mathur, Erwin H. Tanin, Nicholas D. Tailby, Mason C. Marshall, Aakash Ravi, Raisa Trubko, Roger R. Fu, David F. Phillips, Surjeet Rajendran, Ronald L. Walsworth. Self-interactions within the dark sector could clump dark matter into heavy composite states with low number density, leading to a highly suppressed event rate in existing direct detection experiments.

title: DocSCAN: Unsupervised Text Classification via Learning from Neighbors
creator: Dominik Stammbach, Elliott Ash
description: Abstract We introduce DocSCAN, a completely unsupervised text classification approach built on the Semantic Clustering by Adopting Nearest-Neighbors algorithm. For each document, we obtain semantically informative vectors from a large pre-trained language model. We find that similar documents have proximate vectors, so neighbors in the representation space tend to share topic labels.

title: Large k k topological quantum computer
creator: Nikita Kolganov, Sergey Mironov, Andrey Morozov
description: Abstract Chern-Simons topological quantum computer is a device that can be effectively described by the Chern-Simons topological quantum field theory and used for quantum computations. Quantum qudit gates of this quantum computer are represented by sequences of quantum ℛ \mathcal{R} -matrices.

title: Analyzing Online Political Advertisements
creator: Danae Sánchez Villegas, Saeid Mokaram, Nikolaos Aletras
description: Abstract Online political advertising is a central aspect of modern election campaigning for influencing public opinion. Computational analysis of political ads is of utmost importance in political science to understand the characteristics of digital campaigning. It is also important in computational linguistics to study features of political discourse and communication on a large scale.

title: On measurement of photon polarization in radiative penguin 𝑩 B decays to baryons
creator: P. Pakhlov, T. Uglov
description: Abstract A measurement of the photon polarization in radiative penguin B B decays provides a test of the Standard Model and a probe for New Physics, that can lead to a deviation from the Standard Model prediction of left-handed photons in b → s ​ γ b\to s\gamma .

title: Anomalous dimensions of twist 2 operators and 𝒩 = 4 \mathcal{N}=4 SYM quantum spectral curve
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by . We present algorithmic perturbative solution of 𝒩 = 4 \mathcal{N}=4 SYM quantum spectral curve in the case of twist 2 operators, valid to in principle arbitrary order in coupling constant. The latter treats operator spins as arbitrary integer values and is written in terms of special class of functions – products of rational functions in spectral parameter with sums of Baxter polynomials and Hurwitz functions.

title: Swarm Differential Privacy for Purpose Driven Data-Information-Knowledge-Wisdom Architecture
creator: Yingbo Li, Yucong Duan*, Zakaria Maamar, Haoyang Che, Anamaria-Beatrice Spulber, Stelios Fuentes
description: Abstract Privacy protection has recently been in the spotlight of attention to both academia and industry. Society protects individual data privacy through complex legal frameworks. The increasing number of applications of data science and artificial intelligence has resulted in a higher demand for the ubiquitous application of the data.

title: Measuring neutron skin by grazing isobaric collisions
creator: Hao-jie Xu, Hanlin Li, Ying Zhou, Xiaobao Wang, Jie Zhao, Lie-Wen Chen, Fuqiang Wang
description: Abstract Neutron skin thickness ( Δ ​ r np \Delta r_{\rm np} ) of nuclei and the inferred nuclear symmetry energy are of critical importance to nuclear physics and astrophysics. It is traditionally measured by nuclear processes with significant theoretical uncertainties.

title: Fast and Error-Adaptive Influence Maximization based on Count-Distinct Sketches
creator: Gökhan Göktürk and Kamer Kaya
description: Abstract Influence maximization (IM) is the problem of finding a seed vertex set that maximizes the expected number of vertices influenced under a given diffusion model. Due to the NP-Hardness of finding an optimal seed set, approximation algorithms are frequently used for IM. In this work, we describe a fast, error-adaptive approach that leverages Count-Distinct sketches and hash-based fused sampling.

title: A Bit More Bayesian: Domain-Invariant Learning with Uncertainty
creator: Zehao Xiao, Jiayi Shen, Xiantong Zhen, Ling Shao, Cees G. M. Snoek
description: Abstract Domain generalization is challenging due to the domain shift and the uncertainty caused by the inaccessibility of target domain data. In this paper, we address both challenges with a probabilistic framework based on variational Bayesian inference, by incorporating uncertainty into neural network weights. We couple domain invariance in a probabilistic formula with the variational Bayesian inference.

title: Lyapunov–Krasovskii functionals for some classes of nonlinear time delay systems
creator: Gerson Portilla, Irina V. Alexandrova, Sabine Mondié
description: Abstract In this contribution, we study an homogeneous class of nonlinear time delay systems with time-varying perturbations. Using the Lyapunov-Krasovskii approach, we introduce a functional that leads to perturbation conditions matching those obtained previously in the Razumikhin framework. The functionals are applied to the estimation of the domain of attraction and of the system solutions. An illustrative example is given.

title: Probabilistic Forecast of Multiphase Transport under Viscous and Buoyancy Forces in Heterogeneous Porous Media
creator: Farzaneh Rajabi, Hamdi A. Tchelepi
description: Abstract In this study, we develop a probabilistic approach to map the parametric uncertainty to the output state uncertainty in first-order hyperbolic conservation laws. We analyze this problem for nonlinear immiscible two-phase transport in heterogeneous porous media in the presence of a stochastic velocity field.

title: Adversarial Training with Natural Transformation
creator: Shuo Wang, Surya Nepal, Marthie Grobler, Kristen Moore, Lingjuan Lyu
description: Abstract Previous robustness approaches for deep learning models such as data augmentation techniques via data transformation or adversarial training cannot capture real-world variations that preserve the semantics of the input, such as a change in lighting conditions. To bridge this gap, we present NaTra, an adversarial training scheme that is designed to improve the robustness of image classification algorithms.

title: Active XY model on a substrate: Density fluctuations and phase ordering
creator: Astik Haldar, Apurba Sarkar, Swarnajit Chatterjee, Abhik Basu
description: Abstract We explore the generic long wavelength properties of an active XY model on a substrate, consisting of collection of nearly phase-ordered active XY spins in contact with a diffusing, conserved species, as a representative system of active spinners with a conservation law .

title: Sampling-Frequency-Independent Audio Source Separation Using Convolution Layer Based on Impulse Invariant Method Thanks: This work was supported by JSPS KAKENHI Grant Number JP20K19818.
creator: Koichi Saito, Tomohiko Nakamura, Kohei Yatabe, Yuma Koizumi, Hiroshi Saruwatari
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Koichi Saito, Tomohiko Nakamura, Kohei Yatabe, Yuma Koizumi, Hiroshi Saruwatari. Audio source separation is often used as preprocessing of various applications, and one of its ultimate goals is to construct a single versatile model capable of dealing with the varieties of audio signals. Since sampling frequency, one of the audio signal varieties, is usually application specific, the preceding audio source separation model should be able to deal with audio signals of all sampling frequencies specified in the target applications.

title: Towards a functorial description of quantum relative entropy
creator: Arthur J. Parzygnat
description: Abstract A Bayesian functorial characterization of the classical relative entropy (KL divergence) of finite probabilities was recently obtained by Baez and Fritz. This was then generalized to standard Borel spaces by Gagné and Panangaden. Here, we provide preliminary calculations suggesting that the finite-dimensional quantum (Umegaki) relative entropy might be characterized in a similar way.

title: The Behavior of Internet Traffic for Internet Services during COVID-19 Pandemic Scenario
creator: Carlos Alexandre Gouvea da Silva, Allan Christian Krainski Ferrari, Cristiano Osinski and Douglas Antonio Firmino Pelacini
description: Abstract Resumo Since the end of 2019, the SARS-CoV-2 virus known as COVID-19 has spread rapidly around the world, forcing many governments to impose restrictive blocking or lockdown to combat the pandemic. With locomotion restriction of people in almost of countries of the world, workers and students needed to keep their activities at home.

title: Markov processes related to the stationary measure for the open KPZ equation
creator: Włodek Bryc, Alexey Kuznetsov, Yizao Wang, Jacek Wesołowski
description: Abstract . We provide a probabilistic description of the stationary measures for the open KPZ on the spatial interval [ 0 , 1 ] [0,1] in terms of a Markov process Y Y , which is a Doob’s h h transform of the Brownian motion killed at an exponential rate.

title: Bond-length distributions classified by coordination environments
creator: Motonari Sawada, Ryoga Iwamoto, Takao Kotani, Hirofumi Sakakibara
description: Abstract We have analyzed bond-length distributions between cations and anions for crystal structures in the crystallographic open database (www.crystallography.net/cod/). The distributions are classified by the coordination environments of cations, which are determined by a tool named as Chemenv (Acta Cryst. (2020). B76, 683-695). pacs 61.50.-f,61.50.Ah,61.66.

title: A Coupled Random Projection Approach to Large-Scale Canonical Polyadic Decomposition
creator: Lu-Ming Wang, Ya-Nan Wang, Xiao-Feng Gong, Qiu-Hua Lin, Fei Xiang
description: Abstract We propose a novel algorithm for the computation of canonical polyadic decomposition (CPD) of large-scale tensors. The proposed algorithm generalizes the random projection (RAP) technique, which is often used to compute large-scale decompositions, from one single projection to multiple but coupled random projections (CoRAP).

title: Latency Analysis of Consortium Blockchained Federated Learning
creator: Pengcheng Ren, Tongjiang Yan
description: Abstract A decentralized federated learning architecture is proposed to apply to the Businesses-to-Businesses scenarios by introducing the consortium blockchain in this paper. We introduce a model verification mechanism to ensure the quality of local models trained by participators. To analyze the latency of the system, a latency model is constructed by considering the work flow of the architecture.

title: Filtered simplicial homology, graph dissimilarity and überhomology
creator: Daniele Celoria
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Daniele Celoria. We introduce a filtration on the simplicial homology of a finite simplicial complex X X using bi-colourings of its vertices. This yields two dual homology theories closely related to discrete Morse matchings on X X . We give an explicit expression for the associated graded object of these homologies when X X is the matching complex of the Tait graph of a plane graph G G , in terms of subgraphs determined by certain matchings on the dual of G G .

title: Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC): Nuts and Bolts
creator: Abhishek Aich
description: Abstract In this report, we present a theoretical support of the continual learning method Elastic Weight Consolidation , introduced in paper titled ‘Overcoming catastrophic forgetting in neural networks’ [ 4 ] . Being one of the most cited paper in regularized methods for continual learning, this report disentangles the underlying concept of the proposed objective function.

title: SRLF: A Stance-aware Reinforcement Learning Framework for Content-based Rumor Detection on Social Media
creator: Chunyuan Yuan, Wanhui Qian, Qianwen Ma, Wei Zhou, Songlin Hu
description: Abstract The † † footnotetext: * Corresponding author. rapid development of social media changes the lifestyle of people and simultaneously provides an ideal place for publishing and disseminating rumors, which severely exacerbates social panic and triggers a crisis of social trust. Early content-based methods focused on finding clues from the text and user profiles for rumor detection.

title: Validation of image systems simulation technology using a Cornell Box
creator: Zheng Lyu, Krithin Kripakaran, Max Furth, Eric Tang, Brian Wandell, Joyce Farrell
description: Abstract We describe and experimentally validate an end-to-end simulation of a digital camera. The simulation models the spectral radiance of 3D-scenes, formation of the spectral irradiance by multi-element optics, and conversion of the irradiance to digital values by the image sensor.

title: Approximate Fréchet Mean for Data Sets of Sparse Graphs
creator: Daniel Ferguson, François G. Meyer
description: Abstract To characterize the location (mean, median) of a set of graphs, one needs a notion of centrality that is adapted to metric spaces, since graph sets are not Euclidean spaces. A standard approach is to consider the Fréchet mean.

title: Contacts, equilibration, and interactions in fractional quantum Hall edge transport
creator: C. Spånslätt, Yuval Gefen, I. V. Gornyi, D. G. Polyakov
description: Abstract We study electron transport through a multichannel fractional quantum Hall edge in the presence of both interchannel interaction and random tunneling between channels, with emphasis on the role of contacts. The prime example in our discussion is the edge at filling factor 2/3 with two counterpropagating channels.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning-based Methods for Resource Scheduling in Cloud Computing: A Review and Future Directions
creator: Guangyao Zhou, Wenhong Tian, Rajkumar Buyya, Ruini Xue, Liang Song
description: Abstract . With the acceleration of the Internet in Web 2.0, Cloud computing is a new paradigm to offer dynamic, reliable and elastic computing services. Efficient scheduling of resources or optimal allocation of requests is one of the prominent issues in emerging Cloud computing.

title: Integrable structure of BCD conformal field theory and boundary Bethe ansatz for affine Yangian
creator: Alexey Litvinov, Ilya Vilkoviskiy[] 1. Landau Institute for Theoretical Physics, 142432 Chernogolovka, Russia 2. Center for Advanced Studies, Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology, 143026 Moscow, Russia 3. National Research University Higher School of Economics, 119048 Moscow, Russia
description: Abstract In these notes we study integrable structures of conformal field theory with BCD symmetry. We realise these integrable structures as affine Yangian 𝔤 ​ 𝔩 ​ ( 1 ) \mathfrak{gl}(1) ”spin chains” with boundaries. We provide three solutions of Sklyanin KRKR equation compatible with affine Yangian R R -matrix and derive Bethe ansatz equations for the spectrum.

title: Aggregating From Multiple Target-Shifted Sources
creator: Changjian Shui, Zijian Li, Jiaqi Li, Christian Gagné, Charles X. Ling, Boyu Wang
description: Abstract Multi-source domain adaptation aims at leveraging the knowledge from multiple tasks for predicting a related target domain. A crucial aspect is to properly combine different sources based on their relations. In this paper, we analyzed the problem for aggregating source domains with different label distributions, where most recent source selection approaches fail.

title: On the logarithmic coarse structures of Lie groups and hyperbolic spaces Thanks: Author supported by the European Research Council, ERC Starting Grant 713998 GeoMeG ‘Geometry of Metric Groups’.
creator: Gabriel Pallier
description: Abstract . We characterize the Lie groups with finitely many connected components that are O ⁡ ( u ) O(u) -bilipschitz equivalent (almost quasiisometric in the sense that the sublinear function u u replaces the additive bounds of quasiisometry) to the real hyperbolic space, or to the complex hyperbolic plane.

title: AppealNet: An Efficient and Highly-Accurate Edge/Cloud Collaborative Architecture for DNN Inference
creator: Min Li 1 , Yu Li 1 , Ye Tian 1 , Li Jiang 2 and Qiang Xu 1
description: Abstract This paper presents AppealNet , a novel edge/cloud collaborative architecture that runs deep learning (DL) tasks more efficiently than state-of-the-art solutions. For a given input, AppealNet accurately predicts on-the-fly whether it can be successfully processed by the DL model deployed on the resource-constrained edge device, and if not, appeals to the more powerful DL model deployed at the cloud.

title: Homological mirror symmetry for the symmetric squares of punctured spheres
creator: Yankı Lekili, Alexander Polishchuk
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Yankı Lekili, Alexander Polishchuk. For an appropriate choice of a ℤ \mathbb{Z} -grading structure, we prove that the wrapped Fukaya category of the symmetric square of a ( k + 3 ) (k+3) -punctured sphere, i.e.

title: MuseMorphose: Full-Song and Fine-Grained Piano Music Style Transfer with One Transformer VAE
creator: Shih-Lun Wu, and Yi-Hsuan Yang
description: Abstract Transformers and variational autoencoders (VAE) have been extensively employed for symbolic (e.g., MIDI) domain music generation. While the former boast an impressive capability in modeling long sequences, the latter allow users to willingly exert control over different parts (e.g., bars) of the music to be generated.

title: Z-GCNETs: Time Zigzags at Graph Convolutional Networks for Time Series Forecasting
creator: Yuzhou Chen, Ignacio Segovia-Dominguez, Yulia R. Gel
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Yuzhou Chen, Ignacio Segovia-Dominguez, Yulia R. Gel. There recently has been a surge of interest in developing a new class of deep learning (DL) architectures that integrate an explicit time dimension as a fundamental building block of learning and representation mechanisms.

title: Toeplitz algebras over Fock and Bergman spaces
creator: Shengkun Wu 1, Xianfeng Zhao 2
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Shengkun Wu 1, Xianfeng Zhao 2. In this paper, we investigate Toeplitz subalgebras generated by certain class of Toeplitz operators on the p p -Fock space and the p p -Bergman space with 1 < p < ∞ 1<p<\infty . Let BUC( ℂ n \mathbb{C}^{n} ) and BUC( 𝔹 n \mathbb{B}_{n} ) denote the collections of bounded uniformly continuous functions on ℂ n \mathbb{C}^{n} and 𝔹 n \mathbb{B}_{n} (the unit ball in ℂ n \mathbb{C}^{n} ), respectively.

title: Wiki-Reliability: A Large Scale Dataset for Content Reliability on Wikipedia Conference: Proceedings of the 44th International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval; July 11–15, 2021; Virtual Event, Canada Proceedings of the 44th International ACM SIGIR Conference
creator: KayYen Wong, Miriam Redi, Diego Saez-Trumper
description: Abstract . Wikipedia is the largest online encyclopedia, used by algorithms and web users as a central hub of reliable information on the web. The quality and reliability of Wikipedia content is maintained by a community of volunteer editors. Machine learning and information retrieval algorithms could help scale up editors’ manual efforts around Wikipedia content reliability.

title: Spin reorientation in tetragonally distorted spinel oxide NiCo 2 O 4 epitaxial films
creator: Hiroki Koizumi, Ikumi Suzuki, Daisuke Kan, Jun-ichiro Inoue, Yusuke Wakabayashi, Yuichi Shimakawa, Hideto Yanagihara
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Hiroki Koizumi, Ikumi Suzuki, Daisuke Kan, Jun-ichiro Inoue, Yusuke Wakabayashi, Yuichi Shimakawa, Hideto Yanagihara. We experimentally investigated the magnetic properties of NiCo 2 O 4 epitaxial films known to be conductive oxides with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (PMA) at room temperature. Both magneto-torque and magnetization measurements at various temperatures provide clear experimental evidence of the spin reorientation transition at which the MA changes from PMA to easy-cone magnetic anisotropy (ECMA) at a certain temperature ( T SR T_{\rm{SR}} ).

title: Convergent Filaments Contracting Towards an Intermediate-mass Prestellar Core 2019 Convergent Filaments Contracting Towards an Intermediate-mass Prestellar Core –
creator: Zhiyuan Ren, Lei Zhu, Hui Shi, Nannan Yue, Di Li Qizhou Zhang, Diego Mardones, Jingwen Wu, Sihan Jiao, Shu Liu, Gan Luo, Jinjin Xie, Chao Zhang, Xuefang Xu
description: Abstract Filamentary structures are closely associated with star-forming cores, but their detailed physical connections are still not clear. We studied the dense gas in the region of OMC-3 MMS-7 in Orion A molecular cloud using the molecular lines observed with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) and the Submillimeter Array (SMA).

title: FAID Diversity via Neural Networks Thanks: The work is funded in part by the NSF under grants CIF-1855879, CCF 2106189, CCSS-2027844 and CCSS-2052751. Bane Vasić has disclosed an outside interest in Codelucida to the University of Arizona. Conflicts of interest resulting from this interest are being
creator: Xin Xiao 1 , Nithin Raveendran 1 , Bane Vasić 1 , Shu Lin 2 , and Ravi Tandon 1
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Xin Xiao 1 , Nithin Raveendran 1 , Bane Vasić 1 , Shu Lin 2 , and Ravi Tandon 1. Decoder diversity is a powerful error correction framework in which a collection of decoders collaboratively correct a set of error patterns otherwise uncorrectable by any individual decoder.

title: Nonlinear MHD simulation of core plasma collapse events in stellarators
creator: Yasuhiro Suzuki, Shimpei Futatani, Joachim Geiger
description: Abstract Three-dimensional nonlinear MHD simulations study the core collapse events observed in a stellarator experiment. In the low magnetic shear configuration like the Wendelstein 7-X, the rotational transform profile is very sensitive to the toroidal current density. The 3D equilibrium with localized toroidal current density is studied.

title: Measurements of branching fractions and direct CP -violating asymmetries in B + → K + ​ π 0 ​ and ​ π + ​ π 0 B^{+}\to K^{+}\pi^{0}~\mbox{and}~\pi^{+}\pi^{0} decays using 2019 and 2020 Belle II data
creator: F. Abudinén, I. Adachi, R. Adak, K. Adamczyk, P. Ahlburg, J. K. Ahn, H. Aihara, N. Akopov, A. Aloisio, F. Ameli, L. Andricek, N. Anh Ky, D. M. Asner, H. Atmacan, V. Aulchenko, T. Aushev, V. Aushev, T. Aziz, V. Babu, S. Bacher, S. Baehr, S. Bahinipati, A. M. Bakich, P. Bambade, Sw. Banerjee, S. Bansa
description: Abstract We report measurements of branching fractions ( ℬ \mathcal{B} ) and direct CP -violating asymmetries ( 𝒜 𝐶𝑃 \mathcal{A}_{\it CP} ) for the decays B + → K + ​ π 0 B^{+}\to K^{+}\pi^{0} and B + → π + ​ π 0 B^{+}\to\pi^{+}\pi^{0} reconstructed with the Belle II detector in a sample of asymmetric-energy electron-positron collisions at the

title: ExpMRC: Explainability Evaluation for Machine Reading Comprehension
creator: Yiming Cui, Ting Liu, Wanxiang Che, Zhigang Chen, Shijin Wang
description: Abstract Achieving human-level performance on some of Machine Reading Comprehension (MRC) datasets is no longer challenging with the help of powerful Pre-trained Language Models (PLMs). However, it is necessary to provide both answer prediction and its explanation to further improve the MRC system’s reliability, especially for real-life applications.

title: Low dimensional flow polytopes and their toric ideals Thanks: Partially supported by National Research, Development and Innovation Office, NKFIH K 119934, K 132002 and PD 121410.
creator: M. Domokos and D. Joó
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by M. Domokos and D. Joó. The toric ideal of a d d -dimensional flow polytope has an initial ideal generated by square-free monomials of degree at most d d . The toric ideal of a flow polytope of dimension at most four has an initial ideal generated by square-free monomials of degree at most two, with the only exception of the four-dimensional Birkhoff polytope, whose toric ideal has an initial ideal generated by a square-free cubic monomial.

title: On the Partial Transpose of a Haar Unitary Matrix Thanks: Research supported by a Discovery Grant from the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada (JM); The Simons Foundation grant No. 360242 (MP); and Narodowe Centrum Nauki grant 2016/23/D/ST1/01077 (KSz)
creator: James A. Mingo, Mihai Popa, Kamil Szpojankowski
description: Abstract . We consider the effect of a partial transpose on the limit ∗ * -distribution of a Haar distributed random unitary matrix. If we fix the number of blocks, b b , we show that the partial transpose can be decomposed along diagonals into a sum of b b matrices which are asymptotically free and identically distributed.

title: Neural Program Repair with Execution-based Backpropagation
creator: He Ye, Matias Martinez, Martin Monperrus
description: Abstract . Neural machine translation (NMT) architectures have achieved promising results for automatic program repair. Yet, they have the limitation of generating low-quality patches (e.g., not compilable patches). This is because the existing works only optimize a purely syntactic loss function based on characters and tokens without incorporating program-specific information during neural network weight optimization.

title: The global structure of magnetic fields and gas in simulated Milky Way-analogue galaxies 2021 The global structure of magnetic fields and gas in simulated Milky Way-analogue galaxies – A
creator: Benjamin D. Wibking, Mark R. Krumholz
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Benjamin D. Wibking, Mark R. Krumholz. We simulate an isolated, magnetised Milky Way-like disc galaxy using a self-consistent model of unresolved star formation and feedback, evolving the system until it reaches statistical steady state.

title: Spreading and Suppression of Infection Clusters on the Ginibre Continuum Percolation Clusters
creator: Machiko Katori, Makoto Katori
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Machiko Katori, Makoto Katori. Off-lattice SIR models are constructed on continuum percolation clusters defined on the Ginibre point process (GPP) and on the Poisson point process (PPP). The static percolation transitions in the continuum percolation models as well as the infection-spreading transitions in the SIR models, which are regarded as the dynamic percolation transitions, are enhanced in the GPP-based model compared with the PPP-based model. This enhancement is caused by hyperuniformity of the GPP.

title: Radial oscillations and gravitational wave echoes of strange stars with nonvanishing lambda
creator: Jyatsnasree Bora, Umananda Dev Goswami
description: Abstract We study the effect of the cosmological constant on radial oscillations and gravitational wave echoes (GWEs) of non-rotating strange stars. To depict strange star configurations we used two forms of equations of state (EoSs), viz., the MIT Bag model EoS and the linear EoS.

title: Skew-Oblivious Data Routing for Data Intensive Applications on FPGAs with HLS PubID: pubid: 978-1-6654-3274-0/21/$31.00 © 2021 IEEE
creator: Xinyu Chen, Hongshi Tan, Yao Chen, Bingsheng He, Weng-Fai Wong, Deming Chen
description: Abstract FPGAs have become emerging computing infrastructures for accelerating applications in datacenters. Meanwhile, high-level synthesis (HLS) tools have been proposed to ease the programming of FPGAs. Even with HLS, irregular data-intensive applications require explicit optimizations, among which multiple processing elements (PEs) with each owning a private BRAM-based buffer are usually adopted to process multiple data per cycle.

title: CREPO: An Open Repository to Benchmark Credal Network Algorithms
creator: Rafael Cabañas, Alessandro Antonucci
description: Abstract Credal networks are a popular class of imprecise probabilistic graphical models obtained as a Bayesian network generalization based on, so-called credal , sets of probability mass functions. A Java library called CREMA has been recently released to model, process and query credal networks.

title: Inter-GPS: Interpretable Geometry Problem Solving with Formal Language and Symbolic Reasoning
creator: Pan Lu, Ran Gong, Shibiao Jiang, Liang Qiu, Siyuan Huang, Xiaodan Liang, Song-Chun Zhu
description: Abstract Geometry problem solving has attracted much attention in the NLP community recently. The task is challenging as it requires abstract problem understanding and symbolic reasoning with axiomatic knowledge. However, current datasets are either small in scale or not publicly available. Thus, we construct a new large-scale benchmark, Geometry3K, consisting of 3,002 geometry problems with dense annotation in formal language.

title: COBALT: COnstrained Bayesian optimizAtion of computationaLly expensive grey-box models exploiting derivaTive information
creator: Joel A. Paulson, Congwen Lu
description: Abstract Many engineering problems involve the optimization of computationally expensive models for which derivative information is not readily available. The Bayesian optimization (BO) framework is a particularly promising approach for solving these problems, which uses Gaussian process (GP) models and an expected utility function to systematically tradeoff between exploitation and exploration of the design space.

title: Bagging cross-validated bandwidth selection in nonparametric regression estimation with applications to large-sized samples Thanks: Corresponding author: E-mail: mariofr@udc.es
creator: D. Barreiro-Ures
description: Abstract Cross-validation is a well-known and widely used bandwidth selection method in nonparametric regression estimation. However, this technique has two remarkable drawbacks: (i) the large variability of the selected bandwidths, and (ii) the inability to provide results in a reasonable time for very large sample sizes. To overcome these problems, bagging cross-validation bandwidths are analyzed in this paper.

title: Computer assisted proof of branches of stationary and periodic solution, and Hopf bifurcations, for dissipative PDEs Thanks: The author is partially supported by the PRIN project Equazioni alle derivate parziali di tipo ellittico e parabolico: aspetti geometrici, disuguaglianze collegate, e applicaz
creator: Gianni Arioli
description: Abstract . We discuss an approach to the computer assisted proof of the existence of branches of stationary and periodic solutions for dissipative PDEs, using the Brussellator system with diffusion and Dirichlet boundary conditions as an example, We also consider the case where the branch of periodic solutions emanates from a branch of stationary solutions through a Hopf bifurcation. 1.

title: On the Hardness of Opinion Dynamics Optimization with L 1 L_{1} -Budget on Varying Susceptibility to Persuasion
creator: T-H. Hubert Chan, Chui Shan Lee
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by T-H. Hubert Chan, Chui Shan Lee. Recently, Abebe et al. (KDD 2018) and Chan et al. (WWW 2019) have considered an opinion dynamics optimization problem that is based on a popular model for social opinion dynamics, in which each agent has some fixed innate opinion, and a resistance that measures the importance it places on its innate opinion; moreover, the agents influence one another’s opinions through an iterative process. Under certain conditions, this iterative process converges to some equilibrium opinion vector.

title: PeriPy - A High Performance OpenCL Peridynamics Package Journal: Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering
creator: B. Boys, T. J. Dodwell, M. Hobbs, M. Girolami
description: Abstract This paper presents a lightweight, open-source and high-performance python package for solving peridynamics problems in solid mechanics. The development of this solver is motivated by the need for fast analysis tools to achieve the large number of simulations required for ‘outer-loop’ applications, including sensitivity analysis, uncertainty quantification and optimisation.

title: Efficient Error-Correcting-Code Mechanism for High-Throughput Memristive Processing-in-Memory PubID: pubid: 978-1-6654-3274-0/21/$31.00 ©2021 IEEE. Personal use of this material is permitted. Permission from IEEE must be obtained for all other uses, in any current or future media, including reprinti
creator: Orian Leitersdorf 1 , Ben Perach, Ronny Ronen, and Shahar Kvatinsky
description: Abstract Inefficient data transfer between computation and memory inspired emerging processing-in-memory (PIM) technologies. Many PIM solutions enable storage and processing using memristors in a crossbar-array structure, with techniques such as memristor-aided logic (MAGIC) used for computation. This approach provides highly-paralleled logic computation with minimal data movement.

title: Resonant interaction in chiral, Eshelby-twisted van der Waals atomic layers
creator: Pilkyung Moon
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Pilkyung Moon. We study the electronic structures of chiral, Eshelby-twisted van der Waals atomic layers with a particular focus on a chiral twisted graphite (CTG), a graphene stack with a constant twist angle θ \theta between successive layers. We show that each CTG can host infinitely many resonant states which arise from the interaction between the degenerate monolayer states of the constituent layers.

title: M center in 4 H -SiC is a carbon self-interstitial
creator: J. Coutinho, J. D. Gouveia, T. Makino, T. Ohshima, Ž. Pastuović, L. Bakrač, T. Brodar, I. Capan
description: Abstract The list of semiconductor materials with spectroscopically fingerprinted self-interstitials is very short. M M center in 4 ​ H 4H -SiC, a bistable defect responsible for a family of electron traps, has been deprived of a model which could unveil its real importance for almost two decades.

title: Attraction rates for iterates of a superattracting skew product Thanks: This work was supported by the Research Institute for Mathematical Sciences, an International Joint Usage/Research Center located in Kyoto University.
creator: Kohei Ueno
description: Abstract . Let f ⁡ ( z , w ) = ( p ⁡ ( z ) , q ⁡ ( z , w ) ) f(z,w)=(p(z),q(z,w)) be a holomorphic skew product with a superattracting fixed point at the origin.

title: Norm rigidity for arithmetic and profinite groups
creator: Leonid Polterovich, Yehuda Shalom, Zvi Shem-Tov
description: Abstract Let A A be a commutative ring, and assume every non-trivial ideal of A A has finite-index. We show that if SL n ​ ( A ) {\rm{SL}}_{n}(A) has bounded elementary generation then every conjugation-invariant norm on it is either discrete or precompact.

title: The closeness of localised structures between the Ablowitz-Ladik lattice and Discrete Nonlinear Schrödinger equations II: Generalised AL and DNLS systems
creator: Dirk Hennig, Nikos I. Karachalios, Jesús Cuevas-Maraver
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Dirk Hennig, Nikos I. Karachalios, Jesús Cuevas-Maraver. The Ablowitz-Ladik system, being one of the few integrable nonlinear lattices, admits a wide class of analytical solutions, ranging from exact spatially localised solitons to rational solutions in the form of the spatiotemporally localised discrete Peregrine soliton.

title: On Linear Stochastic Flows Thanks: This work was partially supported by the ARC Discovery Grant DP200101866. Thanks: The work of Szymon Peszat was supported by Polish National Science Center grant 2017/25/B/ST1/02584.
creator: Beniamin Goldys, Szymon Peszat
description: Abstract . We study the existence of the stochastic flow associated to a linear stochastic evolution equation d ​ X = A ​ X ​ d ​ t + ∑ k B k ​ X ​ d ​ W k , {\rm d}X=AX{\rm d}t+\sum_{k}B_{k}X{\rm d}W_{k}, on a Hilbert space.

title: Long-term pulse period evolution of the ultra-luminous X-ray pulsar NGC 7793 P13
creator: F. Fürst, D. J. Walton, M. Heida, M. Bachetti, C. Pinto, M. J. Middleton, M. Brightman, H. P. Earnshaw, D. Barret, A. C. Fabian, P. Kretschmar, K. Pottschmidt, A. Ptak, T. Roberts, D. Stern, N. Webb, J. Wilms
description: Abstract Ultra-luminous X-ray pulsars (ULXPs) provide a unique opportunity to study persistent super-Eddington accretion. Here we present the results of a long-term monitoring campaign of ULXP NGC 7793 P13, focusing on the pulse period evolution and the determination of the orbital ephemeris.

title: Monte Carlo simulations of the electron short-range quantum ordering in Coulomb systems: Reducing the “fermionic sign problem”
creator: V. Filinov, P. Levashov, A. Larkin
description: Abstract To account for the interference effects of the Coulomb and exchange interactions of electrons a new path integral representation of the density matrix has been developed in the canonical ensemble at finite temperatures. The developed representation allows to reduce the notorious “fermionic sign problem” in the Monte Carlo simulations of fermionic systems.

title: AoI-Aware Resource Allocation for Platoon-Based C-V2X Networks via Multi-Agent Multi-Task Reinforcement Learning
creator: Mohammad Parvini, Student Member, IEEE , Mohammad Reza Javan, Senior Member, IEEE , Nader Mokari, Senior Member, IEEE , Bijan Abbasi, Senior Member, IEEE , and Eduard A. Jorswieck, Fellow, IEEE
description: Abstract This paper investigates the problem of age of information (AoI) aware radio resource management for a platooning system. Multiple autonomous platoons exploit the cellular wireless vehicle-to-everything (C-V2X) communication technology to disseminate the cooperative awareness messages (CAMs) to their followers while ensuring timely delivery of safety-critical messages to the Road-Side Unit (RSU).

title: In-Hindsight Quantization Range Estimation for Quantized Training
creator: Marios Fournarakis, Markus Nagel Qualcomm AI Research mfournar@qti.qualcomm.com, markusn@qti.qualcomm.com
description: Abstract Quantization techniques applied to the inference of deep neural networks have enabled fast and efficient execution on resource-constraint devices. The success of quantization during inference has motivated the academic community to explore fully quantized training, i.e. quantizing back-propagation as well. However, effective gradient quantization is still an open problem.

title: ReadTwice : Reading Very Large Documents with Memories
creator: Yury Zemlyanskiy, Joshua Ainslie, Michiel de Jong, Philip Pham, Ilya Eckstein, Fei Sha
description: Abstract Knowledge-intensive tasks such as question answering often require assimilating information from different sections of large inputs such as books or article collections. We propose ReadTwice 1 1 1 Source code and pre-trained checkpoints for ReadTwice can be found at https://goo.gle/research-readtwice .

title: An Analysis of Phenotypic Diversity in Multi-Solution Optimization Thanks: This work received funding from the German Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF) (grant agreement no. 03FH012PX5)
creator: Alexander Hagg (✉), Mike Preuss, Alexander Asteroth, Thomas Bäck
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Alexander Hagg (✉), Mike Preuss, Alexander Asteroth, Thomas Bäck. More and more, optimization methods are used to find diverse solution sets. We compare solution diversity in multi-objective optimization, multimodal optimization, and quality diversity in a simple domain. We show that multiobjective optimization does not always produce much diversity, multimodal optimization produces higher fitness solutions, and quality diversity is not sensitive to genetic neutrality and creates the most diverse set of solutions.

title: Expressivity of Parameterized and Data-driven Representations in Quality Diversity Search Conference: 2021 Genetic and Evolutionary Computation Conference; July 10–14, 2021; Lille, France 2021 Genetic and Evolutionary Computation Conference (GECCO ’21), July 10–14, 2021, Lille, France ISBN: 978-1-45
creator: Alexander Hagg, Sebastian Berns, Alexander Asteroth, Simon Colton, Thomas Bäck
description: Abstract . We consider multi-solution optimization and generative models for the generation of diverse artifacts and the discovery of novel solutions. In cases where the domain’s factors of variation are unknown or too complex to encode manually, generative models can provide a learned latent space to approximate these factors.

title: Age of Information Aware VNF Scheduling in Industrial IoT Using Deep Reinforcement Learning Thanks: Mohammad Akbari is with Communication Department, ICT Research Institute, Tehran, Iran (e-mail: m.akbari@itrc.ac.ir) Thanks: Mohammad Reza Abedi is with the Department of Electrical Engineering, Tarbi
creator: Mohammad Akbari, Mohammad Reza Abedi, Roghayeh Joda, Member, IEEE, Mohsen Pourghasemian, Nader Mokari, Senior Member, IEEE, Melike Erol-Kantarci, Senior Member, IEEE
description: Abstract In delay-sensitive industrial internet of things (IIoT) applications, the age of information (AoI) is employed to characterize the freshness of information. Meanwhile, the emerging network function virtualization provides flexibility and agility for service providers to deliver a given network service using a sequence of virtual network functions (VNFs).

title: Designing Air Flow with Surrogate-assisted Phenotypic Niching
creator: Alexander Hagg (✉), Dominik Wilde, Alexander Asteroth, Thomas Bäck
description: Abstract In complex, expensive optimization domains we often narrowly focus on finding high performing solutions, instead of expanding our understanding of the domain itself. But what if we could quickly understand the complex behaviors that can emerge in said domains instead?

title: An illustrated view of differential operators of a reduced quotient of an affine semigroup ring Thanks: CB was partially supported by NSF DMS 2001101. LFM was partially supported by the Simons Foundation.
creator: Christine Berkesch, C-Y. Jean Chan, Patricia Klein, Laura Felicia Matusevich, Janet Page, Janet Vassilev
description:
A 2021 arXiv research paper by Christine Berkesch, C-Y. Jean Chan, Patricia Klein, Laura Felicia Matusevich, Janet Page, Janet Vassilev. Through examples, we illustrate how to compute differential operators on a quotient of an affine semigroup ring by a radical monomial ideal, when working over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0. Introduction

In this paper, we provide illustrative examples and visualizations of some differential operators on the quotient of an affine semigroup ring by a radical monomial ideal. These examples motivate our work in
