title: Exclusive heavy vector meson electroproduction to NLO in collinear factorisation Preprint: . HIP-2021-18/TH . IPPP/20/100 . LTH 1260
creator: C. A. Flett, J. A. Gracey, S. P. Jones, and T. Teubner
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by C. A. Flett, J. A. Gracey, S. P. Jones, and T. Teubner. We compute the exclusive electroproduction, γ ∗ ​ p → V ​ p \gamma^{*}p\rightarrow Vp , of heavy quarkonia V V to NLO in the collinear factorisation scheme, which has been formally proven for this process. The inclusion of an off-shell virtuality Q 2 Q^{2} carried by the photon extends the photoproduction phase space of the exclusive heavy quarkonia observable to electroproduction kinematics.

title: Investigating global convective dynamos with mean-field models: full spectrum of turbulent effects required
creator: Jörn Warnecke, Matthias Rheinhardt, Mariangela Viviani, Frederick A. Gent, Simo Tuomisto, Maarit J. Käpylä
description: Abstract The role of turbulent effects for dynamos in the Sun and stars continues to be debated. Mean-field (MF) theory provides a broadly used framework to connect these effects to fundamental magnetohydrodynamics. While inaccessible observationally, turbulent effects can be directly studied using global convective dynamo (GCD) simulations.

title: On isolated singular solutions of semilinear
description: Abstract Our purpose of this paper is to study isolated singular solutions of semilinear Helmholtz equation − Δ ​ u − u = Q ​ | u | p − 1 ​ u in ℝ N ∖ { 0 } , lim | x | → 0 u ⁡ ( x ) = + ∞ , -\Delta u-u=Q|u|^{p-1}u\quad{\rm in}\ \

title: Generation of the special linear group by elementary matrices in some measure Banach algebras
creator: Amol Sasane
description: Abstract . For a commutative unital ring R R , and n ∈ ℕ n\in\mathbb{N} , let SL n ​ ( R ) {\textrm{SL}}_{n}(R) denote the special linear group over R R , and E n ​ ( R ) {\textrm{E}}_{n}(R) the subgroup of elementary matrices.

title: A sufficient condition for k k -contraction of the series connection of two systems
creator: Ron Ofir, Michael Margaliot, Yoash Levron, Jean-Jacques Slotine
description: Abstract The flow of contracting systems contracts 1-dimensional parallelotopes, i.e., line segments, at an exponential rate. One reason for the usefulness of contracting systems is that many interconnections of contracting sub-systems yield an overall contracting system. A generalization of contracting systems is k k -contracting systems, where k ∈ { 1 , … , n } k\in\{1,\dots,n\} .

title: Cryptanalysis of Semidirect Product Key Exchange Using Matrices Over Non-Commutative Rings
creator: Christopher Battarbee, Delaram Kahrobaei, and Siamak F. Shahandashti
description: Abstract It was recently demonstrated that the Matrix Action Key Exchange (MAKE) algorithm, a new type of key exchange protocol using the semidirect product of matrix groups, is vulnerable to a linear algebraic attack if the matrices are over a commutative ring.

title: Enhancement of the superconductivity and quantum metallic state in the thin film of superconducting Kagome metal KV 3 Sb 5
creator: Teng Wang, Aobo Yu, Han Zhang, Yixin Liu, Wei Li, Wei Peng, Zengfeng Di, Da Jiang, Gang Mu
description: Abstract Recently V-based Kagome metal attracted intense attention due to the emergence of superconductivity in the low temperature. Here we report the fabrication and physical investigations of the high quality single-crystalline thin films of the Kagome metal KV 3 Sb 5 .

title: On Properties of a Regular Simplex Inscribed into a Ball
creator: Mikhail Nevskii
description: Abstract Let B B be a Euclidean ball in ℝ n {\mathbb{R}}^{n} and let C ⁡ ( B ) C(B) be a space of continuous functions f : B → ℝ f:B\to{\mathbb{R}} with the uniform norm ‖ f ‖ C ⁡ ( B ) := max x ∈ B ⁡ | f ⁡ ( x ) | . \|f\|_{C(B)}:=\max_{x\in B}|f(x)|.

title: A galaxy cluster in the innermost Zone of Avoidance, close to the radio phoenix VLSS J2217.5+5943
creator: W. Kollatschny, H. Meusinger, M. Hoeft, G. J. Hill, M.W. Ochmann, G. Zeimann, D. Froebrich, and S. Bhagat
description: Abstract Context. Galaxy clusters grow by mergers with other clusters and groups. Extended regions of diffuse radio emission with a steep radio spectral index are thought to be indicators of such merger events. Extended radio sources with a significantly curved spectrum and complex morphology have been found in several galaxy clusters.

title: EXTENDED SCALAR SECTORS AT CURRENT AND FUTURE COLLIDERS
creator: T. ROBENS
description: Abstract We here give a brief overview on the current status of selected models that extend the scalar sector of the Standard Model with additional matter states. We comment on current bounds as well as possible discovery prospects at current and future colliders.

title: Incompressibility and Symmetry Energy of Neutron Star
creator: Ankit Kumar 1,2, H. C. Das 1,2, S. K. Patra 1,2
description: Abstract We trace a systematic and consistent method to precisely numerate the magnitude range for various structural and isospin compositional properties of the neutron star. Incompressibility, symmetry energy, slope parameter and curvature of a neutron star are investigated using the relativistic energy density functional within the framework of coherent density fluctuation model.

title: Approximate Novelty Search
description: Abstract Width-based search algorithms seek plans by prioritizing states according to a suitably defined measure of novelty, that maps states into a set of novelty categories. Space and time complexity to evaluate state novelty is known to be exponential on the cardinality of the set. We present novel methods to obtain polynomial approximations of novelty and width-based search.

title: Deep Learning Models in Software Requirements Engineering
creator: Maria Naumcheva
description: Abstract Requirements elicitation is an important phase of any software project: the errors in requirements are more expensive to fix than the errors introduced at later stages of software life cycle. Nevertheless many projects do not devote sufficient time to requirements. Automated requirements generation can improve the quality of software projects.

title: The drip lines of kaonic nuclei
creator: J. Guo, D. H. Chen, Xian-Rong Zhou, H.-J. Schulze, Q. B. Chen
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by J. Guo, D. H. Chen, Xian-Rong Zhou, H.-J. Schulze, Q. B. Chen. The effects of an additional K − K^{-} meson on the neutron and proton drip lines are investigated within Skyrme-Hartree-Fock approach combined with a Skyrme-type kaon-nucleon interaction. While an extension of the proton drip line is observed due to the strongly attractive K − ​ p K^{-}p interaction, contrasting effects (extension and reduction) on the neutron drip line of Be, O, and Ne isotopes are found.

title: A complete picture of the four-party linear inequalities in terms of the 0 0 -entropy
creator: Zhiwei Song, Lin Chen, Yize Sun, Mengyao Hu
description: Abstract Multipartite quantum system is complex. Characterizing the relations among the three bipartite reduced density operators ρ A ​ B \rho_{AB} , ρ A ​ C \rho_{AC} and ρ B ​ C \rho_{BC} of a tripartite state ρ A ​ B ​ C \rho_{ABC} has been an open problem in quantum information.

title: A Systematic Investigation of the Coupling between One-Dimensional Edge States of a Topological Crystalline Insulator
creator: Johannes Jung, Artem Odobesko, Robin Boshuis, Andrzej Szczerbakow, Tomasz Story, Matthias Bode
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Johannes Jung, Artem Odobesko, Robin Boshuis, Andrzej Szczerbakow, Tomasz Story, Matthias Bode. The interaction of spin-polarized one-dimensional (1D) topological edge modes localized along single-atomic steps of the topological crystalline insulator Pb 0.7 Sn 0.3 Se(001) has been studied systematically by scanning tunneling spectroscopy. Our results reveal that the coupling of adjacent edge modes sets in at a step–to–step distance d ss ≤ 25 d_{\rm ss}\leq 25 nm, resulting in a characteristic splitting of a single peak at the Dirac point in tunneling spectra.

title: IKT 16 a.k.a. PSR J0058–7218: Discovery of a 22 ms energetic rotation-powered pulsar in the Small Magellanic Cloud 2020 IKT 16 a.k.a. PSR J0058–7218: Discovery of a 22 ms energetic rotation-powered pulsar in the Small Magellanic Cloud – References
creator: C. Maitra, P. Esposito, A. Tiengo, J. Ballet, F. Haberl, S. Dai, M. D. Filipović, M. Pilia
description: Abstract We report here on the discovery with XMM-Newton of pulsations at 22 ms from the central compact source associated with IKT 16, a supernova remnant in the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC). The measured spin period and spin period derivative correspond to 21.7661076(2) ms and 2.9 ​ ( 3 ) × 10 − 14 2.

title: Connectivity of 1d random geometric graphs
creator: Alexander P. Kartun-Giles, Kostas Koufos, Nicolas Privault
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Alexander P. Kartun-Giles, Kostas Koufos, Nicolas Privault. A 1d random geometric graph (1d RGG) is built by joining a random sample of n n points from an interval of the real line with probability p p . We count the number of k k -hop paths between two vertices of the graph in the case where the space is the 1d interval [ 0 , 1 ] [0,1] .

title: Toward the Design of Fault-Tolerance- and Peak- Power-Aware Multi-Core Mixed-Criticality Systems
creator: Behnaz Ranjbar, Ali Hosseinghorban, Mohammad Salehi, Alireza Ejlali, and Akash Kumar
description: Abstract Mixed-Criticality (MC) systems have recently been devised to address the requirements of real-time systems in industrial applications, where the system runs tasks with different criticality levels on a single platform. In some workloads, a high-critically task might overrun and overload the system, or a fault can occur during the execution.

title: Insulator-to-Metal Crossover near the Edge of the Superconducting Dome in Nd 1-x Sr x NiO 2
creator: Yu-Te Hsu, Bai Yang Wang, Maarten Berben, Danfeng Li, Kyuho Lee, Caitlin Duffy, Thom Ottenbros, Woo Jin Kim, Motoki Osada, Steffen Wiedmann, Harold Y. Hwang, Nigel E. Hussey
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Yu-Te Hsu, Bai Yang Wang, Maarten Berben, Danfeng Li, Kyuho Lee, Caitlin Duffy, Thom Ottenbros, Woo Jin Kim, Motoki Osada, Steffen Wiedmann, Harold Y. Hwang, Nigel E. Hussey. We report a systematic magnetotransport study of superconducting infinite-layer nickelate thin films Nd 1-x Sr x NiO 2 with 0.15 ≤ x ≤ 0.225 0.15\leq x\leq 0.225 .

title: S ​ U ​ ( 𝟓 ) L × U ​ ( 𝟏 ) Y SU(5)_{L}\times U(1)_{Y} electroweak unification
creator: Adrian Palcu
description: Abstract We propose here - for the first time in the literature, to our best knowledge - an electroweak unification based on the S ​ U ​ ( 5 ) L × U ​ ( 1 ) Y SU(5)_{L}\times U(1)_{Y} gauge group.

title: Be Causal: De-biasing Social Network Confounding in Recommendation DOI: 10.1145/1122445.1122456 Conference: Woodstock ’18: ACM Symposium on Neural Gaze Detection; June 03–05, 2018; Woodstock, NY Woodstock ’18: ACM Symposium on Neural Gaze Detection, June 03–05, 2018, Woodstock, NY Price: 15.00 ISBN:
creator: Qian Li, Xiangmeng Wang, Guandong Xu
description: Abstract . In recommendation systems, the existence of the missing-not-at-random (MNAR) problem results in the selection bias issue, degrading the recommendation performance ultimately. A common practice to address MNAR is to treat missing entries from the so-called “exposure” perspective, i.e., modeling how an item is exposed (provided) to a user.

title: Temporal Prediction and Evaluation of Brassica Growth in the Field using Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks
creator: Lukas Drees 1 , Laura Verena Junker-Frohn 2 , Jana Kierdorf 1 , Ribana Roscher 1
description: Abstract Farmers frequently assess plant growth and performance as basis for making decisions when to take action in the field, such as fertilization, weed control, or harvesting. The prediction of plant growth is a major challenge, as it is affected by numerous and highly variable environmental factors.

title: Shell-model description for the first-forbidden β − \beta^{-} decay of 207 Hg into the one-proton-hole nucleus 207 Tl Journal: Journal of L a T e X Templates
creator: Anil Kumar, Praveen C. Srivastava
description: Abstract In this work, we have performed large-scale shell-model calculations for the first-forbidden β − \beta^{-} decay of 207 Hg into the one-proton-hole nucleus 207 Tl corresponding to the recently available experimental data from ISOLDE-CERN [T. A. Berry et al., Phys. Rev. C 101, 054311 (2020)].

title: Complex Frequency
creator: Federico Milano, IEEE Fellow
description: Abstract The paper introduces the concept of complex frequency . The imaginary part of the complex frequency is the variation with respect of a synchronous reference of the local bus frequency as commonly defined in power system studies. The real part is defined based on the variation of the voltage magnitude.

title: Deep regression for uncertainty-aware and interpretable analysis of large-scale body MRI
creator: \IEEEauthorblockN Taro Langner \IEEEauthorrefmark 1, Robin Strand \IEEEauthorrefmark 1 \IEEEauthorrefmark 2, Håkan Ahlström \IEEEauthorrefmark 1 \IEEEauthorrefmark 3 and Joel Kullberg \IEEEauthorrefmark 1 \IEEEauthorrefmark 3 \IEEEauthorblockA \IEEEauthorrefmark 1Department of Surgical Sciences, Upp
description: Abstract Large-scale medical studies such as the UK Biobank examine thousands of volunteer participants with medical imaging techniques. Combined with the vast amount of collected metadata, anatomical information from these images has the potential for medical analyses at unprecedented scale.

title: High repetition rate and coherent Free-Electron Laser in the tender X-rays based on the Echo-Enabled Harmonic Generation of an Ultra-Violet Oscillator pulse
creator: N. S. Mirian 1 , M. Opromolla 2,3 , G. Rossi 2 , L. Serafini 3 and V. Petrillo 2,3
description: Abstract Fine time-resolved analysis of matter - i.e. spectroscopy and photon scattering - in the linear response regime requires a fs-scale pulsed, high repetition rate, fully coherent X-ray source. A seeded Free-Electron Laser (FEL) driven by a Super-Conducting Linac, generating 10 8 10^{8} - 10 10 10^{10} coherent photons at 2-5 keV with about 0.

title: Jacob’s ladders, class of crossbreeding conserving certain cell of meta-functional equations and existence of cancerous growth of that cell
creator: Jan Moser
description: Abstract . In this paper a set of 48 crossbreedings on certain cell of meta-functional equations preserving the cell is obtained. In opposite direction we presente an example of very complicated meta-functional equation not obtained in basic cell though it is generated by sequence of internal crossbreedings. Such a formula is called as cancerous growth on the basic cell.

title: Multi-modal Visual Place Recognition in Dynamics-Invariant Perception Space
creator: Lin Wu, Teng Wang, Changyin Sun
description: Abstract Visual place recognition is one of the essential and challenging problems in the fields of robotics. In this letter, we for the first time explore the use of multi-modal fusion of semantic and visual modalities in dynamics-invariant space to improve place recognition in dynamic environments.

title: On the Interpretation of the Aharonov-Bohm Effect
creator: Jay Solanki
description: Abstract The Aharonov-Bohm (A-B) effect showed that the phase of electron wave pattern could be changed by the excluded electromagnetic field, the region where electromagnetic field is zero. This apparent non-local effect has been explained by mainly two salient interpretations called ”the interpretation of electromagnetic potentials” and ”the interpretation of interaction energy”.

title: JDAM - Jump Diffusion by Analytic Models
creator: Yaqing Xy Wang, Jack Kelsall, Nadav Avidor
description: Abstract Nanoscopic diffusion at surfaces normally takes place when an adsorbate jumps from one adsorption site to the other. Jump diffusion can be measured via quasi-elastic scattering experiments, and the results can often be interpreted in terms of analytic models.

title: Summing Up Smart Transitions
creator: Neta Elad, Sophie Rain, Neil Immerman, Laura Kovács, Mooly Sagiv
description: Abstract Some of the most significant high-level properties of currencies are the sums of certain account balances. Properties of such sums can ensure the integrity of currencies and transactions. For example, the sum of balances should not be changed by a transfer operation.

title: Statistical study of electron density turbulence and ion-cyclotron waves in the inner heliosphere: Solar Orbiter observations
creator: F. Carbone, L. Sorriso-Valvo ,, Yu. V. Khotyaintsev, K. Steinvall, A. Vecchio, D. Telloni, E. Yordanova, D. B. Graham, N. J. T. Edberg, A. I. Eriksson, E. P. G. Johansson, C. L. Vásconez, M. Maksimovic, R. Bruno, R. D’Amicis, S. D. Bale, T. Chust, V. Krasnoselskikh, M. Kretzschmar, E. Lorfèvre, D. P
description: Abstract Context. The recently released spacecraft potential measured by the RPW instrument on-board Solar Orbiter has been used to estimate the solar wind electron density in the inner heliosphere. Aims. Solar-wind electron density measured during June 2020 has been analysed to obtain a thorough characterization of the turbulence and intermittency properties of the fluctuations.

title: Lüscher-corrections for 1-particle form-factors in non-diagonally scattering integrable quantum field theories
creator: Árpád Hegedűs
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Árpád Hegedűs. In this paper we derive from field theory a Lüscher-formula, which gives the leading exponentially small in volume corrections to the 1-particle form-factors in non-diagonally scattering integrable quantum field theories. Our final formula is expressed in terms of appropriate expressions of 1- and 3-particle form-factors, and can be considered as the generalization of previous results obtained for diagonally scattering bosonic integrable quantum field theories.

title: TopicsRanksDC: Distance-based Topic Ranking applied on Two-Class Data Thanks: This work has been partially supported by the ”Wachstumskern Qurator – Corporate Smart Insights” project (03WKDA1F) funded by the German Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF)
creator: Malik Yousef, Jamal Al Qundus, Silvio Peikert, Adrian Paschke
description: Abstract In this paper, we introduce a novel approach named TopicsRanksDC for topics ranking based on the distance between two clusters that are generated by each topic. We assume that our data consists of text documents that are associated with two-classes. Our approach ranks each topic contained in these text documents by its significance for separating the two-classes.

title: A deterministic Kaczmarz algorithm for solving linear systems
creator: Changpeng Shao
description: Abstract We propose a new deterministic Kaczmarz algorithm for solving consistent linear systems A ​ 𝐱 = 𝐛 A{\bf x}={\bf b} . Basically, the algorithm replaces orthogonal projections with reflections in the original scheme of Stefan Kaczmarz. Building on this, we give a geometric description of solutions of linear systems.

title: Activation function design for deep networks: linearity and effective initialisation
creator: † ⁣ ‡ \dagger{\ddagger} M. Murray, † \dagger V. Abrol, † ⁣ ‡ \dagger{\ddagger} J. Tanner
description: Abstract The activation function deployed in a deep neural network has great influence on the performance of the network at initialisation, which in turn has implications for training. In this paper we study how to avoid two problems at initialisation identified in prior works: rapid convergence of pairwise input correlations, and vanishing and exploding gradients.

title: Tidal deformability of neutron stars with exotic particles within a density dependent relativistic mean field model in R-squared gravity
creator: K Nobleson, Tuhin Malik, Sarmistha Banik
description: Abstract There is a growing interest in investigating modified theories of gravity, primarily, with the aim of explaining the universe’s accelerated expansion, which has been confirmed by several independent observations. Compact objects, like neutron stars, exhibit strong gravity effects and therefore are used to study modified gravity theories.

title: Generic versions of a result in the theory of Hardy spaces
creator: V. Nestoridis, E. Thirios
description: Abstract We show generic existence of functions f f in the Handy space H p ​ ( 0 < p < 1 ) H^{p}(0<p<1) on the open unit disc whose primitive F ⁡ ( f ) F(f) satisfies the following.

title: How to Explain Neural Networks: an Approximation Perspective
creator: Hangcheng Dong, Bingguo Liu, Fupeng Wei, Fengdong Chen, Dong Ye, Guodong Liu
description: Abstract The lack of interpretability has hindered the large-scale adoption of AI technologies. However, the fundamental idea of interpretability, as well as how to put it into practice, remains unclear. We provide notions of interpretability based on approximation theory in this study.

title: Induction and Skolemization in saturation theorem proving
creator: Stefan Hetzl, Jannik Vierling
description: Abstract We consider a typical integration of induction in saturation-based theorem provers and investigate the effects of Skolem symbols occurring in the induction formulas. In a practically relevant setting we establish a Skolem-free characterization of refutation in saturation-based proof systems with induction. Finally, we use this characterization to obtain unprovability results for a concrete saturation-based induction prover.

title: Are renewable energies on a sustained path? Analysis of selected case-studies from the pre-pandemic-era
creator: Alessandro Bessi, Mariangela Guidolin, Piero Manfredi
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Alessandro Bessi, Mariangela Guidolin, Piero Manfredi. Provided widespread vaccination will bring the COVID-19 pandemic under full control worldwide, the contrast to climate change and the energy transition as one of its main actions will return at the top of national and international policy agendas. This paper employs multivariate diffusion models to investigate and quantitatively assess the competitive power of renewable energy technologies and their perspectives along the invoked energy transition.

title: Islands and current singularities in quasisymmetric toroidal plasmas.
creator: E. Rodríguez, A. Bhattacharjee
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by E. Rodríguez, A. Bhattacharjee. The presence of current singularities in a quasisymmetric magnetic field is explored. Quasisymmetry is shown effective in isolating Pfirsch-Schlüter singularities, to leading order, to a single magnetic surface resonant with the helicity of the symmetry. The effects of pressure driven currents are analysed, indicating that exclusion of this surface from the plasma volume reduces the potential opening of islands, but does not generally eliminate them completely due to higher order asymmetric geometric effects.

title: Learning to Relate Depth and Semantics for Unsupervised Domain Adaptation
creator: Suman Saha* ETH Zurich, Anton Obukhov* ETH Zurich, Danda Pani Paudel ETH Zurich, Menelaos Kanakis ETH Zurich, Yuhua Chen ETH Zurich, Stamatios Georgoulis ETH Zurich, Luc Van Gool ETH Zurich, KU Leuven
description: Abstract We present an approach for encoding visual task relationships to improve model performance in an Unsupervised Domain Adaptation (UDA) setting. Semantic segmentation and monocular depth estimation are shown to be complementary tasks; in a multi-task learning setting, a proper encoding of their relationships can further improve performance on both tasks.

title: Crofton formulas in pseudo-Riemannian space forms Thanks: MSC classification : 53C65, 53B30, 53C50, 52A22, 52A39 A.B. was supported by DFG grant BE 2484/5-2 D.F. was supported by ISF Grant 1750/20. G.S. was supported by FEDER/MICINN grant PGC2018-095998-B-I00 and the Serra Húnter Programme
creator: Andreas Bernig, Dmitry Faifman, Gil Solanes
description: Abstract . Crofton formulas on simply-connected Riemannian space forms allow to compute the volumes, or more generally the Lipschitz-Killing curvature integrals of a submanifold with corners, by integrating the Euler characteristic of its intersection with all geodesic submanifolds. We develop a framework of Crofton formulas with distributions replacing measures, which has in its core Alesker’s Radon transform on valuations.

title: Local fractional metric dimension of rotationally symmetric planar graphs arisen from planar chorded cycles
creator: Shahbaz Ali, Raúl M. Falcón, Muhammad Khalid Mahmood
description: Abstract . In this paper, a new family of rotationally symmetric planar graphs is described based on an edge coalescence of planar chorded cycles. Their local fractional metric dimension is established for those ones arisen from chorded cycles of order up to six.

title: Exact Anti-Self-Dual four-manifolds with a Killing symmetry by similarity transformations
creator: Andronikos Paliathanasis
description: Abstract We study the group properties and the similarity solutions for the constraint conditions of anti-self-dual null Kähler four-dimensional manifolds with at least a Killing symmetry vector. Specifically we apply the theory of Lie symmetries to determine all the infinitesimal generators of the one-parameter point transformations which leave the system invariant.

title: The Flipped Classroom model for teaching Conditional Random Fields in an NLP course
creator: Manex Agirrezabal
description: Abstract In this article, we show and discuss our experience in applying the flipped classroom method for teaching Conditional Random Fields in a Natural Language Processing course. We present the activities that we developed together with their relationship to a cognitive complexity model (Bloom’s taxonomy). After this, we provide our own reflections and expectations of the model itself.

title: Quantization-based approximation of reflected BSDEs with extended upper bounds for recursive quantization
creator: Rancy El Nmeir & Gilles Pagès
description: Abstract We establish upper bounds for the L p L^{p} -quantization error, p ∈ ( 1 , 2 + d ) p\in(1,2+d) , induced by the recursive Markovian quantization of a d d -dimensional diffusion discretized via the Euler scheme.

title: “Hey Alexa, What do You Know About the COVID-19 Vaccine?” - (Mis)perceptions of Mass Immunization Among Voice Assistant Users
creator: Filipo Sharevski, Anna Slowinski, Peter Jachim, Emma Pieroni
description: Abstract In this paper, we analyzed the perceived accuracy of COVID-19 vaccine information spoken back by Amazon Alexa. Unlike social media, Amazon Alexa doesn’t apply soft moderation to unverified content, allowing for use of third-party malicious skills to arbitrarily phrase COVID-19 vaccine information.

title: The Online Pivot: Lessons Learned from Teaching a Text and Data Mining Course in Lockdown, Enhancing online Teaching with Pair Programming and Digital Badges
creator: Beatrice Alex, Clare Llewellyn, Pawel Michal Orzechowski Maria Boutchkova
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Beatrice Alex, Clare Llewellyn, Pawel Michal Orzechowski Maria Boutchkova. In this paper we provide an account of how we ported a text and data mining course online in summer 2020 as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic and how we improved it in a second pilot run. We describe the course, how we adapted it over the two pilot runs and what teaching techniques we used to improve students’ learning and community building online.

title: Contractions of hyper-Kähler fourfolds and the Brauer group Thanks: G.K. is supported by the project Narodowe Centrum Nauki 2018/30/E/ST1/00530, B.v.G. was supported by the PRIN 2015 project Geometry of Algebraic Varieties
creator: Bert van Geemen, Grzegorz Kapustka
description: Abstract . We study the geometry of exceptional loci of birational contractions of hyper-Kähler fourfolds that are of K3 [2] -type. These loci are conic bundles over K3 surfaces and we determine their classes in the Brauer group. For this we use the results on twisted sheaves on K3 surfaces, on contractions and on the corresponding Heegner divisors.

title: Optimal Group Formulation Using Machine Learning
creator: Mahbub Hasan, Md. Al-Emran
description: Abstract Group formation itself a perplexing process. Over the decade of time education and others disciple has improved imminently but optimal group formation in educational system is still struggling. Our research focus on to create optimal group in a class of any institute.

title: Super jeu de taquin and combinatorics
creator: of super tableaux of type A
description: Abstract 1. Introduction The structure of plactic monoids has its origins in the works of Schensted [ 26 ] and Knuth [ 17 ] in the combinatorial study of Young tableaux [ 30 ] , and it has became a ubiquitous tool in algebraic combinatorics, representation theory and probabilistic combinatorics, [ 24 , 10 , 8 ] .

title: Bayesian inference-driven model parameterization and model selection for 2CLJQ fluid models
creator: Owen C. Madin, Simon Boothroyd, Richard A. Messerly, John D. Chodera, Josh Fass, Michael R. Shirts
description: Abstract A high level of physical detail in a molecular model improves its ability to perform high accuracy simulations, but can also significantly affect its complexity and computational cost. In some situations, it is worthwhile to add additional complexity to a model to capture properties of interest; in others, additional complexity is unnecessary and can make simulations computationally infeasible.

title: Silicon rich nitride-lithium niobate on insulator platform for photonics integrated circuits Journal: osajournal Publication type: Research Article
creator: Yang Liu, \authormark 1,2, † \dagger Xingrui Huang, \authormark 1,2, † \dagger Zezheng Li, \authormark 1,2 Huan Guan, \authormark 1 Zhongchao Fan, \authormark 3,4 Weihua Han, \authormark 3,4 and Zhiyong Li \authormark 1,*
description: Abstract In this paper, a silicon rich nitride-lithium niobate on insulator (SRN-LNOI) hybrid platform with waveguides and several key components is proposed. The propagation loss of the silicon rich nitride-lithium niobate rib-loaded waveguide (1 μ ​ m \mu m × \times 300 nm) is 2.6 dB/cm at 1550 nm.

title: Quantum correlations on quantum spaces
creator: Arkadiusz Bochniak, Paweł Kasprzak, Piotr M. Sołtan
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Arkadiusz Bochniak, Paweł Kasprzak, Piotr M. Sołtan. For given quantum (non-commutative) spaces ℙ \mathbb{P} and 𝕆 \mathbb{O} we study the quantum space of maps 𝕄 ℙ , 𝕆 \mathbb{M}_{\mathbb{P},\mathbb{O}} from ℙ \mathbb{P} to 𝕆 \mathbb{O} . In case of finite quantum spaces these objects turn out to be behind a large class of maps which generalize the classical qc \mathrm{qc} -correlations known from quantum information theory to the setting of quantum input and output sets.

title: Quantum Uncertainty in Decision Theory
description: Abstract An approach is presented treating decision theory as a probabilistic theory based on quantum techniques. Accurate definitions are given and thorough analysis is accomplished for the quantum probabilities describing the choice between separate alternatives, sequential alternatives characterizing conditional quantum probabilities, and behavioral quantum probabilities taking into account rational-irrational duality of decision making.

title: BigEarthNet-MM: A Large Scale Multi-Modal Multi-Label Benchmark Archive for Remote Sensing Image Classification and Retrieval
creator: Gencer Sumbul, Arne de Wall, Tristan Kreuziger, Filipe Marcelino, Hugo Costa, Pedro Benevides, Mário Caetano, Begüm Demir, Volker Markl
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Gencer Sumbul, Arne de Wall, Tristan Kreuziger, Filipe Marcelino, Hugo Costa, Pedro Benevides, Mário Caetano, Begüm Demir, Volker Markl. This paper presents the multi-modal BigEarthNet (BigEarthNet-MM) benchmark archive made up of 590,326 pairs of Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 image patches to support the deep learning (DL) studies in multi-modal multi-label remote sensing (RS) image retrieval and classification.

title: Nanometre-scale emittance beams from a continuous-wave RF gun
creator: Anatoliy Opanasenko, Zoltán Tibai, Kévin Pepitone, Georgii Shamuilov, Vitaliy Goryashko
description: Abstract The operation of Ultrafast Electron Diffractometers (UEDs) and Free-Electron Lasers (FELs) relies on high-brightness electron beams produced by radio-frequency (RF) photocathode guns. The next generation of high-repetition rate UEDs and FELs requires electron beams with a high average brightness. To this end, we introduce a continuous wave RF photocathode gun at 325 MHz with an APEX-like geometry.

title: Large-Scale Unsupervised Person Re-Identification with Contrastive Learning
creator: Weiquan Huang, Yan Bai, Qiuyu Ren, Xinbo Zhao, Ming Feng, Yin WangTongji UniversityShanghai, China {weiquanh,yan.bai,qiuyu.ren,1930792,1810865,yinw}@tongji.edu.cn
description: Abstract Existing public person Re-Identification (ReID) datasets are small in modern terms because of labeling difficulty. Although unlabeled surveillance video is abundant and relatively easy to obtain, it is unclear how to leverage these footage to learn meaningful ReID representations.

title: Strong constraints on Lorentz violation using new γ \gamma -ray observations around PeV
creator: Liang Chen 1,2,3, Zheng Xiong 1,2,3, Cong Li 1,3, SongZhan Chen 1,3, HuiHai He 1,2,3
description: Abstract The tiny modification of dispersion relation induced by Lorentz violation (LV) is an essential issue in quantum gravity (QG) theories, which can be magnified into significant effects when dealing with astrophysical observations at high energy and long propagation distance.

title: Kim-independence in positive logic Thanks: The first author was supported by DFG project BA 6785/2-1. He also acknowledges the financial support of his visit to UEA by EPSRC grant EP/S017313/1. The second author was supported by a studentship from the UEA
creator: Jan Dobrowolski and Mark Kamsma
description: Abstract . An important dividing line in the class of unstable theories is being NSOP 1 , which is more general than being simple. In NSOP 1 theories forking independence may not be as well-behaved as in stable or simple theories, so it is replaced by another independence notion, called Kim-independence.

title: A family of weighted Erdős-Mordell inequality and applications
creator: Tran Quang Hung
description: Abstract . We establish some new generalizations of Erdős-Mordell inequality by adding weights to its terms. Using these generalizations, we derived strengthened versions of the original Erdős-Mordell inequality. We also found two other variations of Erdős-Mordell inequality to be generalizable in the same way. 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification 51M04, 51M16 1.

title: Mean Field Games Flock! The Reinforcement Learning Way
creator: Sarah Perrin, Mathieu Laurière, Julien Pérolat, Matthieu Geist, Romuald Élie, Olivier Pietquin
description: Abstract We present a method enabling a large number of agents to learn how to flock, which is a natural behavior observed in large populations of animals. This problem has drawn a lot of interest but requires many structural assumptions and is tractable only in small dimensions.

title: Spin Flavor Spectral Splits of Supernova Neutrino Flavor Conversions
description: Abstract The supernova neutrino flavor evolution in the presence of the non-trivial neutrino magnetic moment and strong magnetic field is numerically derived using the two-flavor and single-angle approximation. The novel properties of collective neutrino oscillations are studied and distinct patterns of flavor and spin-flavor spectral splits are presented.

title: Universality of Abelian and non-Abelian Wannier functions in one dimension
creator: Kiryl Piasotski, Mikhail Pletyukhov, Clara S. Weber, Jelena Klinovaja, Dante M. Kennes, Herbert Schoeller
description: Abstract Within a Dirac model in 1 + 1 1+1 dimensions, a prototypical model to describe low-energy physics for a wide class of lattice models, we propose a field-theoretical version for the representation of Wannier functions, the Zak-Berry connection, and the geometric tensor.

title: RoSmEEry: Robotic Simulated Environment for Evaluation and Benchmarking of Semantic Mapping Algorithms
creator: Sara Kaszuba, Sandeep Reddy Sabbella, Vincenzo Suriani, Francesco Riccio, Daniele Nardi
description: Abstract Human-robot interaction requires a common understanding of the operational environment, which can be provided by a representation that blends geometric and symbolic knowledge: a semantic map . Through a semantic map the robot can interpret user commands by grounding them to its sensory observations. Semantic mapping is the process that builds such a representation.

title: Current-Conserving Relativistic Linear Response for Collisional Plasmas
creator: Martin Formanek, Christopher Grayson, Johann Rafelski, Berndt Müller
description: Abstract We investigate the response of a relativistic plasma to electromagnetic fields in the framework of the Boltzmann equation incorporating a collision term in the relaxation rate approximation selected in a form assuring current conservation. We obtain an explicit solution for the linearized perturbation of the Fermi-Dirac equilibrium distribution in terms of the average relaxation rate κ \kappa .

title: Adaptive Finite-time and Fixed-time Control Design using Output Stability Conditions*
creator: Konstantin Zimenko, Denis Efimov, and Andrey Polyakov
description: Abstract The present paper provides a sufficient condition to ensure output finite-time and fixed-time stability. Comparing with analogous researches the proposed result is less restrictive and obtained for a wider class of systems. The presented output stability condition is used for adaptive control design, where the state vector of a plant is extended by adjustable control parameters.

title: QED radiative corrections for accelerator neutrinos Preprint: FERMILAB-PUB-21-232-T, LA-UR-21-27844, USTC-ICTS/PCFT-21-32
creator: Oleksandr Tomalak, Qing Chen, Richard J. Hill, Kevin S. McFarland
description:
Abstract ABSTRACT Neutrino oscillation experiments at accelerator energies aim to establish charge-parity violation in the neutrino sector by measuring the energy-dependent rate of 
u_{e} appearance and 
u_{\mu} disappearance in a 
u_{\mu} beam. These experiments can precisely measure 
u_{\mu} cross sections at near detectors, but 
u_{e} cross sections are poorly constrained and require theoretical inputs.

title: Modeling of emergent memory and voltage spiking in ionic transport through angström-scale slits
creator: Paul Robin, Nikita Kavokine, Lydéric Bocquet
description: Abstract Recent advances in nanofluidics have enabled the confinement of water down to a single molecular layer. Such monolayer electrolytes show promise in achieving bio-inspired functionalities through molecular control of ion transport. However, the understanding of ion dynamics in these systems is still scarce.

title: A block theoretic proof of Thompson’s A × B A\times B -Lemma
creator: Radha Kessar and Markus Linckelmann
description: Abstract . We show that Thompson’s A × B A\times B -Lemma can be obtained as a consequence of the Brauer pair version of Brauer’s Third Main Theorem. Let k be an algebraically closed field of prime characteristic p . Brauer’s Third Main Theorem [ 2 , Theorem 3] , rephrased using Brauer pairs (cf. [ 1 , Theorem 3.

title: Using Transformers to Provide Teachers with Personalized Feedback on their Classroom Discourse: The TalkMoves Application
creator: Abhijit Suresh, Jennifer Jacobs, Vivian Lai, Chenhao Tan
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Abhijit Suresh, Jennifer Jacobs, Vivian Lai, Chenhao Tan. TalkMoves is an innovative application designed to support K-12 mathematics teachers to reflect on, and continuously improve their instructional practices. This application combines state-of-the-art natural language processing capabilities with automated speech recognition to automatically analyze classroom recordings and provide teachers with personalized feedback on their use of specific types of discourse aimed at broadening and deepening classroom conversations about mathematics.

title: Group-wise shrinkage estimation in penalized model-based clustering
creator: Alessandro Casa, Andrea Cappozzo ∗, Michael Fop
description: Abstract Finite Gaussian mixture models provide a powerful and widely employed probabilistic approach for clustering multivariate continuous data. However, the practical usefulness of these models is jeopardized in high-dimensional spaces, where they tend to be over-parameterized. As a consequence, different solutions have been proposed, often relying on matrix decompositions or variable selection strategies.

title: Quasinormal frequencies for a black hole in a bumblebee gravity
creator: R. Oliveira a, D. M. Dantas a, C. A. S. Almeida a
description: Abstract After recent observational events like the LIGO-Virgo detections of gravitational waves and the shadow image of M87* supermassive black hole by Event Horizon Telescope (EHT), the theoretical study of black holes was significantly improved. Quantities as quasinormal frequencies, shadows, and light deflection become more important to analyze black hole models.

title: Joint Optimization of Hadamard Sensing and Reconstruction in Compressed Sensing Fluorescence Microscopy
creator: Alan Q. Wang*, Aaron K. LaViolette*, Leo Moon, Chris Xu, Mert R. Sabuncu
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Alan Q. Wang*, Aaron K. LaViolette*, Leo Moon, Chris Xu, Mert R. Sabuncu. Compressed sensing fluorescence microscopy (CS-FM) proposes a scheme whereby less measurements are collected during sensing and reconstruction is performed to recover the image. Much work has gone into optimizing the sensing and reconstruction portions separately. We propose a method of jointly optimizing both sensing and reconstruction end-to-end under a total measurement constraint, enabling learning of the optimal sensing scheme concurrently with the parameters of a neural network-based reconstruction network.

title: TCL: Transformer-based Dynamic Graph Modelling via Contrastive Learning DOI: 10.1145/1122445.1122456 Conference: Woodstock ’18: ACM Symposium on Neural Gaze Detection; June 03–05, 2018; Woodstock, NY Woodstock ’18: ACM Symposium on Neural Gaze Detection, June 03–05, 2018, Woodstock, NY Price: 15.00
creator: Lu Wang, Xiaofu Chang, Shuang Li, Yunfei Chu, Hui Li, Wei Zhang, Xiaofeng He, Le Song, Jingren Zhou, Hongxia Yang
description: Abstract . Dynamic graph modeling has recently attracted much attention due to its extensive applications in many real-world scenarios, such as recommendation systems, financial transactions, and social networks. Although many works have been proposed for dynamic graph modeling in recent years, effective and scalable models are yet to be developed.

title: Distributionally Robust Chance-Constrained Flexibility Planning for Integrated Energy System
creator: Sen Zhan, Peng Hou, Guangya Yang
description: Abstract Inflexible combined heat and power (CHP) plants and uncertain wind power production result in excess power in distribution networks, which leads to inverse power flow challenging grid operations. Power-to-X facilities such as electrolysers and electric boilers can offer extra flexibility to the integrated energy system.

title: Ultrahigh-energy photons from LHAASO as probes of Lorentz symmetry violations
creator: Chengyi Li a \,{}^{a}, Bo-Qiang Ma a , b , c \,{}^{a,b,c}
description: Abstract The Large High Altitude Air Shower Observatory (LHAASO) is one of the most sensitive gamma-ray detector arrays currently operating at TeV and PeV energies. Recently the LHAASO experiment detected ultra-high-energy (UHE; E γ ≳ 100 ​ TeV E_{\gamma}\gtrsim 100~\mathrm{TeV} ) photon emissions up to 1.4 ​ PeV 1.4~\mathrm{PeV} from twelve astrophysical gamma-ray sources.

title: Learn to Intervene: An Adaptive Learning Policy for Restless Bandits in Application to Preventive Healthcare
creator: Arpita Biswas, Gaurav Aggarwal, Pradeep Varakantham, Milind Tambe
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Arpita Biswas, Gaurav Aggarwal, Pradeep Varakantham, Milind Tambe. In many public health settings, it is important for patients to adhere to health programs, such as taking medications and periodic health checks. Unfortunately, beneficiaries may gradually disengage from such programs, which is detrimental to their health. A concrete example of gradual disengagement has been observed by an organization that carries out a free automated call-based program for spreading preventive care information among pregnant women.

title: A New Vertex Connectivity Metric
creator: David L. Rhodes, Breanna N. Johnson
description: Abstract A new metric for quantifying pairwise vertex connectivity in graphs is defined and an implementation presented. While general in nature, it features a combination of input features well-suited for social networks, including applicability to directed or undirected graphs, weighted edges, and computes using the impact from all-paths between the vertices.

title: Anomaly detection with Convolutional Graph Neural Networks
creator: Oliver Atkinson, Akanksha Bhardwaj, Christoph Englert, Vishal S. Ngairangbam, and Michael Spannowsky
description: Abstract We devise an autoencoder based strategy to facilitate anomaly detection for boosted jets, employing Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to do so. To overcome known limitations of GNN autoencoders, we design a symmetric decoder capable of simultaneously reconstructing edge features and node features.

title: On log-concave approximations of high-dimensional posterior measures and stability properties in non-linear inverse problems
creator: Jan Bohr Richard Nickl University of Cambridge August 7, 2026
description: Abstract . The problem of efficiently generating random samples from high-dimensional and non-log-concave posterior measures arising in nonlinear regression problems is considered. Extending investigations from [ 48 ] , local and global stability properties of the model are identified under which such posterior distributions can be approximated in Wasserstein distance by suitable log-concave measures.

title: Explicit representation of discrete fractional resolvent families in Banach spaces.
creator: Jorge González-Camus, Rodrigo Ponce
description: Abstract . In this paper we introduce a discrete fractional resolvent family { S α , β n } n ∈ ℕ 0 \{S_{\alpha,\beta}^{n}\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}} generated by a closed linear operator in a Banach space X X for a given α , β > 0 . \alpha,\beta>0.

title: The 3-dimensional Lyness map and a self-mirror log Calabi–Yau 3-fold
creator: Tom Ducat
description: Abstract The 2-dimensional Lyness map is a 5-periodic birational map of the plane which may famously be resolved to give an automorphism of a log Calabi–Yau surface, given by the complement of an anticanonical pentagon of ( − 1 ) (-1) -curves in a del Pezzo surface of degree 5.

title: Permutations designs, projective planes, and transitive sets of permutations Thanks: This research is supported by National Natural Science Foundation of China (12071001, 61672036), Excellent Youth Foundation of Natural Science Foundation of Anhui Province (1808085J20), the Academic Fund for Outstan
creator: Minjia Shi, XiaoXiao Li, Patrick Solé
description: Abstract A notion of t t -designs in the symmetric group on n n letters, called permutation designs in this paper, was introduced by Godsil in 1988. In particular t t -transitive sets of permutations form a t t -design in that sense.

title: Distinguishing Dark Energy Models with Neutrino Oscillations
creator: Ali Rida Khalifeh, Raul Jimenez
description: Abstract Dark Energy models are numerous and distinguishing between them is becoming difficult. However, using distinct observational probes can ease this quest and gives better assessment to the nature of Dark energy. To this end, the plausibility of neutrino oscillations to be a probe of Dark Energy models is investigated.

title: A Two-Sided Matching Model for Data Stream Processing in the Cloud – Fog Continuum
creator: Narges Mehran, Dragi Kimovski, Radu Prodan, Institute of Information Technology, Alpen-Adria-Universität Klagenfurt, Austria Email: {name}.{surname}@aau.at
description: Abstract Latency-sensitive and bandwidth-intensive stream processing applications are dominant traffic generators over the Internet network. A stream consists of a continuous sequence of data elements, which require processing in nearly real-time. To improve communication latency and reduce the network congestion, Fog computing complements the Cloud services by moving the computation towards the edge of the network.

title: INCLUSIVE DETERMINATION OF | V c ​ b | |V_{cb}| AT BELLE
creator: RAYNETTE VAN TONDER for the Belle Collaboration
description: Abstract We present the measurement of the f irst to fourth order moments of the four-momentum transfer squared, q 2 q^{2} , of inclusive B → X c ​ ℓ ​ ν B\rightarrow X_{c}\ell\nu decays using the full Belle data set consisting of 711 ​ fb − 1 711\,\mathrm{fb^{-1}} of integrated luminosity at the Υ ⁡ ( 4 ​ S

title: Compacting Squares: Input-Sensitive In-Place Reconfiguration of Sliding Squares
creator: Hugo A. Akitaya, Erik D. Demaine, Matias Korman, Irina Kostitsyna, Irene Parada, Willem Sonke, Bettina Speckmann, Ryuhei Uehara, Jules Wulms
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Hugo A. Akitaya, Erik D. Demaine, Matias Korman, Irina Kostitsyna, Irene Parada, Willem Sonke, Bettina Speckmann, Ryuhei Uehara, Jules Wulms. A well-established theoretical model for modular robots in two dimensions are edge-connected configurations of square modules, which can reconfigure through so-called sliding moves.

title: Gradient Masking and the Underestimated Robustness Threats of Differential Privacy in Deep Learning
creator: Franziska Boenisch, Philip Sperl, and Konstantin Böttinger
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Franziska Boenisch, Philip Sperl, and Konstantin Böttinger. An important problem in deep learning is the privacy and security of neural networks (NNs). Both aspects have long been considered separately. To date, it is still poorly understood how privacy enhancing training affects the robustness of NNs. This paper experimentally evaluates the impact of training with Differential Privacy (DP), a standard method for privacy preservation, on model vulnerability against a broad range of adversarial attacks.

title: Full operator preconditioning and the accuracy of solving linear systems
creator: Stephan Mohr, Yuji Nakatsukasa, Carolina Urzúa-Torres
description: Abstract Unless special conditions apply, the attempt to solve ill-conditioned systems of linear equations with standard numerical methods leads to uncontrollably high numerical error. Often, such systems arise from the discretization of operator equations with a large number of discrete variables.

title: The Gołąb-Schinzel and Goldie functional equations in Banach
creator: algebras
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by algebras. We are concerned below with the characterization in a unital commutative real Banach algebra \mathbb{A} of continuous solutions of the Gołąb-Schinzel functional equation (below), the general Popa groups they generate and the associated Goldie functional equation.

title: Controlling an Inverted Pendulum with Policy Gradient Methods - A Tutorial
creator: Swagat Kumar
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Swagat Kumar. This paper provides details of implementing two important policy gradient methods to solve the OpenAI/Gym’s pendulum problem. These are called Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) and the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithms respectively. The problem is solved by using an actor-critic model where an actor network is used to learn the policy function and, a critic network to evaluates the action taken by the actor by learning to estimate the value or Q function.

title: Binary Sequences Derived from Differences of Consecutive Primitive Roots
creator: Arne Winterhof, Zibi Xiao
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Arne Winterhof, Zibi Xiao. Let 1 < g 1 < … < g φ ⁡ ( p − 1 ) < p − 1 1<g_{1}<\ldots<g_{\varphi(p-1)}<p-1 be the ordered primitive roots modulo p p . We study the pseudorandomness of the binary sequence ( s n ) (s_{n}) defined by s n ≡ g n + 1 + g n + 2 mod 2 s_{n}\equiv g_{n+1}+g_{n+2}\bmod 2 , n = 0 , 1 , … n=0,1,\ldots .

title: Decimations for Two-dimensional Ising and Rotator Models I
creator: Matteo D’Achille, Aernout C.D. van Enter, Arnaud Le Ny
description: Abstract Abstract: We extend proofs of non-Gibbsianness of decimated Gibbs measures at low temperatures to include long-range, as well as vector-spin interactions. Our main tools consist in a two-dimensional use of “Equivalence of boundary conditions” in the long-range case and an extension of Global specifications for two-dimensional vector spins. AMS 2000 subject classification : Primary- 60K35 ; secondary- 82B20.

title: Spatiotemporal wildfire modeling through point processes with moderate and extreme marks
creator: Jonathan Koh, François Pimont, Jean-Luc Dupuy, Thomas Opitz
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jonathan Koh, François Pimont, Jean-Luc Dupuy, Thomas Opitz. Accurate spatiotemporal modeling of conditions leading to moderate and large wildfires provides better understanding of mechanisms driving fire-prone ecosystems and improves risk management. We here develop a joint model for the occurrence intensity and the wildfire size distribution by combining extreme-value theory and point processes within a novel Bayesian hierarchical model, and use it to study daily summer wildfire data for the French Mediterranean basin during 1995–2018.

title: One-dimensional topological theories with defects and linear generating functions
creator: Mee Seong Im, Paul Zimmer
description:
A 2021 arXiv research paper by Mee Seong Im, Paul Zimmer. We study the Gram determinant and construct bases of hom spaces for the one-dimensional topological theory of decorated unoriented one-dimensional cobordisms, as recently defined by Khovanov, when the pair of generating functions is linear.
