description: Abstract We identify an effective proxy for the analytically unknown second integral of motion ( I 2 I_{2} ) for rotating barred or tri-axial potentials. Planar orbits of a given energy follow a tight sequence in the space of the time-averaged angular momentum and its amplitude of fluctuation.

title: The Social Responsibility of Game AI Thanks: Funded by a Royal Academy of Engineering Research Fellowship
creator: Michael Cook
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Michael Cook. Over the last decade we have watched as artificial intelligence has been transformed into one of the most important issues of our time, and games have grown into the biggest entertainment industry. As a result, game AI research as a field has enjoyed increased access to funding, exposure in the press, and influence with governments and some of the largest technology firms in the world.

title: An Epidemiological Model for contact tracing with the Dutch CoronaMelder App
creator: Peter Boncz
description: Abstract 1 Introduction CoronaMelder is the digital contact tracing app based on exposure notification support in the mobile operating systems of Google and Apple. It was introduced in September 2021 and has been active during the second wave of COVID-19 infections in The Netherlands.

title: Semi-Anchored Multi-Step Gradient Descent Ascent Method for Structured Nonconvex-Nonconcave Composite Minimax Problems Thanks: Submitted to the editors DATE. Funding: This work was supported in part by the National Research Foundation of Korea (NRF) grant funded by the Korea government (MSIT) (No. 2
creator: Sucheol Lee, Donghwan Kim
description: Abstract Minimax problems, such as generative adversarial network, adversarial training, and fair training, are widely solved by a multi-step gradient descent ascent (MGDA) method in practice. However, its convergence guarantee is limited. In this paper, inspired by the primal-dual hybrid gradient method, we propose a new semi-anchoring (SA) technique for the MGDA method.

title: Enhanced anomalous Nernst effects in ferromagnetic materials driven by Weyl nodes
creator: Ilias Samathrakis, Teng Long, Zeying Zhang, Harish K. Singh, Hongbin Zhang
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Ilias Samathrakis, Teng Long, Zeying Zhang, Harish K. Singh, Hongbin Zhang. Based on high-throughput first-principles calculations, we evaluated the anomalous Hall and anomalous Nernst conductivities of 266 transition-metal-based ferromagnetic compounds. Detailed analysis based on the symmetries and Berry curvatures reveals that the origin of singular-like behaviour of anomalous Hall/Nernst conductivities can be mostly attributed to the appearance of Weyl nodes or nodal lines located in the proximity of the Fermi energy, which can be further tailored by external stimuli such as biaxial strains and

title: Weak Harnack inequality for a mixed local and nonlocal parabolic equation
creator: Prashanta Garain and Juha Kinnunen
description: Abstract . This article proves a weak Harnack inequality with a tail term for sign changing supersolutions of a mixed local and nonlocal parabolic equation. Our argument is purely analytic. It is based on energy estimates and the Moser iteration technique.

title: Towards an Integrated Conceptual Modelling Kernel for Business Transaction Workflows Part of this work has been supported by CITEC, a business unit of the Queensland Government’s Department of Public Works and Housing (formerly the Administrative Services Department).
creator: A.P. Barros 1 , A.H.M. ter Hofstede 2 , H.A. Proper 2 1 School of Information Technology 2 Faculty of Information Technology The University of Queensland Queensland University of Technology Brisbane, Qld 4072 GPO Box 2434, Brisbane 4001 Australia Australia e-mail: E.Proper@acm.org
description: Abstract Keywords: Conceptual Modelling, Business Process, Workflow, Object-Oriented Analysis Published as: A.P. Barros, A.H.M. ter Hofstede, and H.A. (Erik) Proper. Towards an Integrated Conceptual Modelling Kernel for Business Transaction Workflows. Technical report, Department of Computer Science, University of Queensland, Brisbane, Queensland, Australia, November 1996.

title: Asteroseismic analysis of variable hot subdwarf stars observed with TESS Thanks: Based on observations at the La Silla Observatory of the European Southern Observatory for programs number 0103.D-0511 and 0104.D-0514. Based on observations obtained at Las Campanas Observatory under the run code 0KJ21
creator: Murat Uzundag, Maja Vučković, Péter Németh, M. Miller Bertolami, Roberto Silvotti, Andrzej S. Baran, John H. Telting, Mike Reed, K. A. Shoaf, Roy H. Østensen, and Sumanta K. Sahoo
description: Abstract Context. We present photometric and spectroscopic analyses of gravity (g-mode) long-period pulsating hot subdwarf B (sdB) stars, also called V1093 Her stars, observed by the TESS space telescope in both 120 s short-cadence and 20 s ultra-short-cadence mode during the survey observation and the extended mission of the southern ecliptic hemisphere. Aims.

title: Revealing Chern number from quantum metric
creator: Anwei Zhang
description: Abstract Chern number is usually characterized by Berry curvature. Here, by investigating the Dirac model of even-dimensional Chern insulator, we give the general relation between Berry curvature and quantum metric, which indicates that the Chern number can be encoded in quantum metric as well as the surface area of the Brillouin zone on the hypersphere embedded in Euclidean parameter space.

title: Multimodal Detection of Information Disorder from Social Media
creator: Kirchknopf Armin, Slijepčević Djordje, Zeppelzauer Matthias
description: Abstract Social media is accompanied by an increasing proportion of content that provides fake information or misleading content, known as information disorder. In this paper, we study the problem of multimodal fake news detection on a large-scale multimodal dataset. We propose a multimodal network architecture that enables different levels and types of information fusion.

title: HOW MANY STRUCTURE CONSTANTS DO EXIST IN RIEMANNIAN GEOMETRY
creator: J.-F. POMMARET
description: Abstract ABSTRACT After reading such a question, any mathematician will say that, according to a well known result of L.P. Eisenhart found in 1926, the answer is ” One ” of course, namely the only constant allowing to describe the so-called ” constant riemannian curvature ” condition.

title: Policies for the Dynamic Traveling Maintainer Problem with Alerts Journal: European Journal of Operations Research
creator: Paulo da Costa, Peter Verleijsdonk, Simon Voorberg, Alp Akcay, Stella Kapodistria, Willem van Jaarsveld, Yingqian Zhang
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Paulo da Costa, Peter Verleijsdonk, Simon Voorberg, Alp Akcay, Stella Kapodistria, Willem van Jaarsveld, Yingqian Zhang. Downtime of industrial assets such as wind turbines and medical imaging devices comes at a sharp cost. To avoid such downtime costs, companies seek to initiate maintenance just before failure. Unfortunately, this is challenging for the following two reasons: On the one hand, because asset failures are notoriously difficult to predict, even in the presence of real-time monitoring devices which signal early degradation.

title: Diophantine Equation with Balancing-like Sequences Associated to the Pillai-Tijdeman-type Problem
creator: Bijan Kumar Patel, Prashant Tiwari
description: Abstract Let { x n } n ≥ 0 \{x_{n}\}_{n\geq 0} be the balancing-like sequence defined by x n + 1 = A ​ x n − x n − 1 x_{n+1}=Ax_{n}-x_{n-1} , for A > 2 A>2 , where x 0 = 0 x_{0}=0 and x 1 = 1 x_{1}=1 .

title: Learning from Perturbations: Diverse and Informative Dialogue Generation with Inverse Adversarial Training
creator: Wangchunshu Zhou Qifei Li Chenle LiBeihang University, Beijing, China zhouwangchunshu@buaa.edu.cn
description: Abstract In this paper, we propose I nverse A dversarial T raining (IAT) algorithm for training neural dialogue systems to avoid generic responses and model dialogue history better. In contrast to standard adversarial training algorithms, IAT encourages the model to be sensitive to the perturbation in the dialogue history and therefore learning from perturbations.

title: Uniformity of quadratic points Thanks: Work supported in part by funds from NSF grant DMS-2100548 and DMS-1759514
creator: Tangli Ge
description: Abstract . In this paper, we extend a uniformity result of Dimitrov–Gao–Habegger [ 6 ] to dimension two and use it to get a uniform bound on the cardinality of the set of all quadratic points for non-hyperelliptic non-bielliptic curves which only depends on the Mordell–Weil rank, the genus of the curve and the degree of the number field. 1.

title: Superharmonic instability for regularized long-wave models
creator: Jared C. Bronski, Vera Mikyoung Hur, Samuel Lee Wester
description: Abstract We examine the spectral stability and instability of periodic traveling waves for regularized long-wave models. Examples include the regularized Boussinesq, Benney–Luke, and Benjamin–Bona–Mahony equations. Of particular interest is a striking new instability phenomenon—spectrum off the imaginary axis extending into infinity.

title: Comment on ‘Local available quantum correlations for Bell Diagonal states and markovian decoherence’
creator: David M. Bellorin R, Hermann L. Albrecht Q
description: Abstract In this brief paper, we complete the analysis presented previously in [RMF 64 (2018) 662–670] regarding the quantifiers of the classical correlations and the so-called local available quantum correlations for Bell Diagonal states. A correction is introduced in their previous expressions once two cases within the optimizations are included. pacs 03.65.Ud, 03.67.-a, 03.67.Mn.

title: Assessing disinformation through the dynamics of supply and demand in the news ecosystem
creator: Pietro Gravino*, Giulio Prevedello, Martina Galletti, Vittorio Loreto
description: Abstract Social dialogue, the foundation of our democracies, is currently threatened by disinformation and partisanship, with their disrupting role on individual and collective awareness and detrimental effects on decision-making processes. Despite a great deal of attention to the news sphere itself, little is known about the subtle interplay between the offer and the demand for information.

title: Critical transition to a non-chaotic regime in isotropic turbulence
creator: Daniel Clark 1, Andres Armua 1, Richard D. J. G. Ho 2, Arjun Berera 1
description: Abstract We study the properties of homogeneous and isotropic turbulence in higher spatial dimensions through the lens of chaos and predictability using numerical simulations. We employ both direct numerical simulations (DNS) and numerical calculations of the Eddy Damped Quasi Normal Markovian (EDQNM) closure approximation.

title: Institute of Theoretical Physics and Astronomy, Vilnius University,
creator: Saulėtekio 3, Vilnius LT-10257, Lithuania
description: Abstract Optical lattice with spin-dependent sub-wavelength barriers E. Gvozdiovas, P. Račkauskas, G. Juzeliūnas * August 7, 2026 Abstract We analyze a tripod atom light coupling scheme characterized by two dark states playing the role of quasi-spin states. It is demonstrated that by properly configuring the coupling laser fields, one can create a lattice with spin-dependent sub-wavelength barriers.

title: Regression-Adjusted Estimation of Quantile Treatment Effects under Covariate-Adaptive Randomizations
creator: Liang Jiang, Peter C. B. Phillips, Yubo Tao, Yichong Zhang
description: Abstract Datasets from field experiments with covariate-adaptive randomizations (CARs) usually contain extra covariates in addition to the strata indicators. We propose to incorporate these additional covariates via auxiliary regressions in the estimation and inference of unconditional quantile treatment effects (QTEs) under CARs.

title: A polynomial composites and monoid domains as algebraic structures and their applications
creator: Magdalena Jankowska
description: Abstract This paper contains the results collected so far on polynomial composites in terms of many basic algebraic properties. Since it is a polynomial structure, results for monoid domains come in here and there. The second part of the paper contains the results of the relationship between the theory of polynomial composites, the Galois theory and the theory of nilpotents.

title: Unifying Distillation with Personalization in Federated Learning
creator: Siddharth Divi, Habiba Farrukh, Z Berkay Celik
description: Abstract . Federated learning (FL) is a decentralized privacy-preserving learning technique in which clients learn a joint collaborative model through a central aggregator without sharing their data. In this setting, all clients learn a single common predictor ( FedAvg ), which does not generalize well on each client’s local data due to the statistical data heterogeneity among clients.

title: Theory of defect-mediated morphogenesis
creator: Ludwig A. Hoffmann 1, Livio Nicola Carenza 1, Julia Eckert 2, Luca Giomi 1
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Ludwig A. Hoffmann 1, Livio Nicola Carenza 1, Julia Eckert 2, Luca Giomi 1. Growing experimental evidence indicates that topological defects could serve as organizing centers in the morphogenesis of tissues. Here, we provide a quantitative explanation for this phenomenon, rooted in the buckling theory of deformable active polar liquid crystals. Using a combination of linear stability analysis and computational fluid dynamics, we demonstrate that active layers, such as confined cell monolayers, are unstable to the formation of protrusions in the presence of disclinations.

title: Constraining effective equation of state in f ⁡ ( Q , T ) f(Q,T) gravity Journal: Eur. Phys. J. C
creator: Simran Arora e1,addr1, Abhishek Parida e2,addr2, P.K. Sahoo e3,addr1
description: Abstract New high-precision observations are now possible to constrain different gravity theories. To examine the accelerated expansion of the Universe, we used the newly proposed f ⁡ ( Q , T ) f(Q,T) gravity, where Q Q is the non-metricity, and T T is the trace of the energy-momentum tensor.

title: Dilute magnetic moments in an exactly solvable interacting host
creator: Chandan Setty
description: Abstract Despite concerted efforts, the problem of dilute local moments embedded in a correlated conduction electron host such as Nd 1-x Ce x CuO 2 persists due to lack of analytically controllable models. Here, we address the question: how do local moments couple to correlated but integrable hosts?

title: A novel second-order nonstandard finite difference method for solving one-dimensional autonomous dynamical systems Journal: Elsevier
creator: Manh Tuan Hoang
description: Abstract In this work, a novel second-order nonstandard finite difference (NSFD) method that preserves simultaneously the positivity and local asymptotic stability of one-dimensional autonomous dynamical systems is introduced and analyzed. This method is based on novel non-local approximations for right-hand side functions of differential equations in combination with nonstandard denominator functions.

title: Evidence of TeV Halos Around Millisecond Pulsars
creator: Dan Hooper, Tim Linden
description: Abstract Using data from the HAWC gamma-ray Telescope, we have studied a sample of 37 millisecond pulsars (MSPs), selected for their spindown power and proximity. From among these MSP, we have identified four which favor the presence of very high-energy gamma-ray emission at a level of ( 2 ​ Δ ​ ln ⁡ ℒ ) 1 / 2 ≥ 2.

title: Electron correlations and T T -breaking density wave order in a ℤ 2 \mathbb{Z}_{2} kagome metal
creator: Chandan Setty ⊕,†, Haoyu Hu ⊕, Lei Chen, Qimiao Si
description: Abstract There have been extensive recent developments on kagome metals, such as T m X n (T= Fe, Co and X= Sn, Ge) and A A V 3 Sb 5 ( A = A= Cs, K, Rb). An emerging issue is the nature of correlated phases when topologically non-trivial bands cross the Fermi level.

title: Future searches for light sterile neutrinos at nuclear reactors
creator: Jeffrey M. Berryman, Luis A. Delgadillo, Patrick Huber
description: Abstract We study the optimization of a green-field, two-baseline reactor experiment with respect to the sensitivity for electron antineutrino disappearance in search of a light sterile neutrino. We consider both commercial and research reactors and identify as key factors the distance of closest approach and detector energy resolution.

title: Leptoquarks facing flavour tests and b → s ​ ℓ ​ ℓ \boldsymbol{b\to s\ell\ell} after Moriond 2021
description: Abstract In view of the emerging hints for the violation of lepton flavour universality in several B B -meson decays, we conduct a model-independent study (effective field theory approach) of several well-motivated new physics scenarios. Taking into account the most recent LHCb data, we provide updates to Wilson coefficient fits for numerous popular new physics hypotheses.

title: Dynamics of superconducting qubit relaxation times
creator: M. Carroll *, S. Rosenblatt *, P. Jurcevic, I. Lauer, A. Kandala
description: Abstract Superconducting qubits are a leading candidate for quantum computing but display temporal fluctuations in their energy relaxation times T 1 T_{1} . This introduces instabilities in multi-qubit device performance. Furthermore, autocorrelation in these time fluctuations introduces challenges for obtaining representative measures of T 1 T_{1} for process optimization and device screening.

title: Locally Private k k -Means Clustering with Constant Multiplicative Approximation and Near-Optimal Additive Error
creator: Anamay Chaturvedi, Matthew Jones, Huy L. Nguyễn
description: Abstract Given a data set of size n n in d ′ d^{\prime} -dimensional Euclidean space, the k k -means problem asks for a set of k k points (called centers) so that the sum of the ℓ 2 2 \ell_{2}^{2} -distances between points of a given data set of size n n and the set of k k centers

title: Calculating a function of a matrix with a real spectrum
creator: P. Kubelík, V. G. Kurbatov, I. V. Kurbatova
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by P. Kubelík, V. G. Kurbatov, I. V. Kurbatova. Let T T be a square matrix with a real spectrum, and let f f be an analytic function. The problem of approximate calculation of f ⁡ ( T ) f(T) is discussed. Applying the Schur triangular decomposition and the reordering, one can assume that T T is triangular and its diagonal entries t i ​ i t_{ii} are arranged in increasing order.

title: Quantifying dynamical coherence with coherence measures
creator: Sunho Kim, Chunhe Xiong, Asutosh Kumar, Guijun Zhang, Junde Wu
description: Abstract Quantum coherence, like entanglement, is a fundamental resource in quantum information. In recent years, remarkable progress has been made in formulating resource theory of coherence from a broader perspective. The notions of block-coherence and POVM-based coherence have been established. Certain challenges, however, remain to be addressed.

title: Bi-Hamiltonian recursion, Liu–Pandharipande relations, and vanishing terms of the second Dubrovin–Zhang bracket
creator: Francisco Hernández Iglesias, Sergey Shadrin
description: Abstract . The Dubrovin–Zhang hierarchy is a Hamiltonian infinite-dimensional integrable system associated to a semi-simple cohomological field theory or, alternatively, to a semi-simple Dubrovin–Frobenius manifold. Under an extra assumption of homogeneity, Dubrovin and Zhang conjectured that there exists a second Poisson bracket that endows their hierarchy with a bi-Hamiltonian structure.

title: Deep Learning Assessment of galaxy morphology in S-PLUS Data Release 1
creator: C. R. Bom, A. Cortesi, G. Lucatelli, L. O. Dias, P. Schubert, G.B. Oliveira Schwarz, N. M. Cardoso, E. V. R. Lima, C. Mendes de Oliveira, L. Sodre Jr, A.V. Smith Castelli, F. Ferrari, G. Damke, R. Overzier, A. Kanaan, T. Ribeiro, W. Schoenell
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by C. R. Bom, A. Cortesi, G. Lucatelli, L. O. Dias, P. Schubert, G.B. Oliveira Schwarz, N. M. Cardoso, E. V. R. Lima, C. Mendes de Oliveira, L. Sodre Jr, A.V. Smith Castelli, F. Ferrari, G. Damke, R. Overzier, A. Kanaan, T. Ribeiro, W. Schoenell. The morphological diversity of galaxies is a relevant probe of galaxy evolution and cosmological structure formation, but the classification of galaxies in large sky surveys is becoming a significant challenge.

title: Col-OSSOS: The Distinct Colour Distribution of Single and Binary Cold Classical KBOs
creator: Wesley C. Fraser, Susan D. Benecchi, JJ Kavelaars, Michaël Marsset, Rosemary E. Pike, Michele T. Bannister, Megan E. Schwamb, Kathryn Volk, David Nesvorny, Mike Alexandersen, Ying-Tung Chen, Stephen Gwyn, Matthew J. Lehner, Shiang-Yu Wang
description: Abstract The cold classical Kuiper Belt Objects (KBOs) possess a high, ≳ 30 % \gtrsim 30\% binary fraction. Widely separated and dynamically fragile, these binary systems have been useful in tracing the origins of KBOs. A new class of binaries was recently identified by their colours.

title: Boosted dark matter from diffuse supernova neutrinos Preprint: SLAC-PUB-17591, N3AS-21-005
creator: Anirban Das, Manibrata Sen
description: Abstract The XENON collaboration recently reported an excess of electron recoil events in the low energy region with a significance of around 3.3 ​ σ 3.3\sigma . An explanation of this excess in terms of thermal dark matter seems challenging.

title: Dynamical Friction Modeling of Massive Black Holes in Cosmological Simulations and Effects on Merger Rate Predictions 2021 Dynamical Friction Modeling of Massive Black Holes in Cosmological Simulations and Effects on Merger Rate Predictions – C
creator: Nianyi Chen, Yueying Ni, Michael Tremmel, Tiziana Di Matteo, Simeon Bird, Colin DeGraf, Yu Feng
description: Abstract In this work we establish and test methods for implementing dynamical friction for massive black hole pairs that form in large volume cosmological hydrodynamical simulations which include galaxy formation and black hole growth. We verify our models and parameters both for individual black hole dynamics and for the black hole population in cosmological volumes.

title: A Quasipolynomial ( 2 + ε ) (2+\varepsilon) -Approximation for Planar Sparsest Cut
creator: Vincent Cohen-AddadAnupam GuptaPhilip N. Klein, Jason Li
description: Abstract The (non-uniform) sparsest cut problem is the following graph-partitioning problem: given a “supply” graph, and demands on pairs of vertices, delete some subset of supply edges to minimize the ratio of the supply edges cut to the total demand of the pairs separated by this deletion.

title: Towards the continuum limit of a ( 1 + 1 ) (1+1) d quantum link Schwinger model
creator: Torsten V. Zache, Maarten Van Damme, Jad C. Halimeh, Philipp Hauke, Debasish Banerjee
description: Abstract The solution of gauge theories is one of the most promising applications of quantum technologies. Here, we discuss the approach to the continuum limit for U ⁡ ( 1 ) U(1) gauge theories regularized via finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces of quantum spin- S S operators, known as quantum link models.

title: Force-and-moment-based Model Predictive Control for Achieving Highly Dynamic Locomotion on Bipedal Robots
creator: Junheng Li, Quan Nguyen
description: Abstract In this paper, we propose a novel framework on force-and-moment-based Model Predictive Control (MPC) for dynamic legged robots. Specifically, we present a formulation of MPC designed for 10 degree-of-freedom (DoF) bipedal robots using simplified rigid body dynamics with input forces and moments.

title: Crystal Growth and Anisotropic Magnetic Properties of Quasi-2D (Fe 1-x Ni x ) 2 P 2 S 6
creator: S. Selter, Y. Shemerliuk, M.-I. Sturza, A. U. B. Wolter, B. Büchner, S. Aswartham
description: Abstract We report the crystal growth by chemical vapor transport together with a thorough structural and magnetic characterization of the quasi-2D magnets (Fe 1-x Ni x ) 2 P 2 S 6 with x Ni = 0, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9 & 1 x_{\textrm{Ni}}=\textrm{0, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9 \& 1} .

title: Harmonic persistent homology
creator: Saugata Basu, Nathanael Cox
description: Abstract We introduce harmonic persistent homology spaces for filtrations of finite simplicial complexes. As a result we can associate concrete subspaces of cycles to each bar of the barcode of the filtration. We prove stability of the harmonic persistent homology subspaces, as well as the subspaces associated to the bars of the barcodes, under small perturbations of functions defining them.

title: Extended scalar sectors at future colliders Thanks: Presented by Tania Robens at XXVII Cracow EPIPHANY Conference of Future of particle physics
creator: Tania Robens Jan Kalinowski, Aleksander Filip Żarnecki Andreas Papaefstathiou
description: Abstract After the discovery of the Higgs boson in 2012, particle physics has entered an exciting era. An important question is whether the Standard Model of particle physics correctly describes the scalar sector realized by nature, or whether it is part of a more extended model, featuring additional particle content.

title: Universal statistics of waves in a random time-varying medium
creator: R. Carminati, H. Chen, R. Pierrat, B. Shapiro
description: Abstract We study the propagation of waves in a medium in which the wave velocity fluctuates randomly in time. We prove that at long times, the statistical distribution of the wave energy is log-normal, with the average energy growing exponentially.

title: Iterated Mapping Cones for Strongly Koszul Algebras
creator: Keller VandeBogert
description: Abstract . In this paper we extend the well-known iterated mapping cone procedure to monomial ideals in strongly Koszul algebras. We study properties of ideals generated by monomials in commutative Koszul algebras and show that the linear strand of ideals generated by linear forms is obtained as a subcomplex of the Priddy complex.

title: Eventually, geometric ( n k ) (n_{k}) configurations exist for all n n
creator: Leah Wrenn Berman, Gábor Gévay, Tomaž Pisanski
description: Abstract . In a series of papers and in his 2009 book on configurations Branko Grünbaum described a sequence of operations to produce new ( n 4 ) (n_{4}) configurations from various input configurations. These operations were later called the “Grünbaum Incidence Calculus”. We generalize two of these operations to produce operations on arbitrary ( n k ) (n_{k}) configurations.

title: A magnetic domain wall Mackey-Glass oscillator
creator: Jérôme Williame, Joo-Von Kim
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jérôme Williame, Joo-Von Kim. We propose a time-delay oscillator with Mackey-Glass nonlinearity based on a pinned magnetic domain wall in a thin film nanostrip. Through spin transfer torques, electric currents applied along the strip cause the domain wall to deform and displace away from a geometrical pinning site, which can be converted into a nonlinear transfer function through a suitable choice of a readout. This readout serves as a delay signal, which is subsequently fed back into the applied current with amplification.

title: FAPIS: A Few-shot Anchor-free Part-based Instance Segmenter
creator: Khoi Nguyen and Sinisa Todorovic Oregon State University Corvallis, OR 97330, USA {nguyenkh,sinisa}@oregonstate.edu
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Khoi Nguyen and Sinisa Todorovic Oregon State University Corvallis, OR 97330, USA {nguyenkh,sinisa}@oregonstate.edu. This paper is about few-shot instance segmentation, where training and test image sets do not share the same object classes. We specify and evaluate a new few-shot anchor-free part-based instance segmenter (FAPIS). Our key novelty is in explicit modeling of latent object parts shared across training object classes, which is expected to facilitate our few-shot learning on new classes in testing.

title: A comparative evaluation of learned feature descriptors on hybrid monocular visual SLAM methods
creator: Hudson M. S. Bruno, Esther L. Colombini
description: Abstract Classical Visual Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (VSLAM) algorithms can be easily induced to fail when either the robot’s motion or the environment is too challenging. The use of Deep Neural Networks to enhance VSLAM algorithms has recently achieved promising results, which we call hybrid methods.

title: Super-Linear Growth Reveals the Allee Effect in Tumors
creator: Youness Azimzade, Abbas Ali Saberi, Robert A. Gatenby
description: Abstract Abstract: Integrating experimental data into ecological models plays a central role in understanding biological mechanisms that drive tumor progression where such knowledge can be used to develop new therapeutic strategies. While the current studies emphasize the role of competition among tumor cells, they fail to explain recently observed super-linear growth dynamics across human tumors.

title: Extending Higher Bruhat Orders to non-longest words in S n S_{n}
creator: Daniel Hothem
description: Abstract . In this paper, we extend Manin and Schechtman’s higher Bruhat orders for S n S_{n} to higher Bruhat orders for non-longest words w w in S n S_{n} . We prove that the higher Bruhat orders of non-longest words are ranked posets with unique minimal and maximal elements.

title: Charge Condensation and Lattice Coupling Drives Stripe Formation in Nickelates
creator: Y. Shen, G. Fabbris, H. Miao, Y. Cao, D. Meyers, D. G. Mazzone, T. Assefa, X. M. Chen, K. Kisslinger, D. Prabhakaran, A. T. Boothroyd, J. M. Tranquada, W. Hu, A. M. Barbour, S. B. Wilkins, C. Mazzoli, I. K. Robinson, M. P. M. Dean
description: Abstract Revealing the predominant driving force behind symmetry breaking in correlated materials is sometimes a formidable task due to the intertwined nature of different degrees of freedom. This is the case for La 2-x Sr x NiO 4+δ in which coupled incommensurate charge and spin stripes form at low temperatures.

title: Quantum battery based on quantum discord at room temperature
creator: C. Cruz, M. F. Anka, M. S. Reis, R. Bachelard, Alan C. Santos
description: Abstract The study of advanced quantum devices for energy storage has attracted the attention of the scientific community in the past few years. Although several theoretical progresses have been achieved recently, experimental proposals of platforms operating as quantum batteries under ambient conditions are still lacking.

title: Towards the 0 0 -statement of the Kohayakawa-Kreuter Conjecture Thanks: J.H. was supported by UKRI Future Leaders Fellowship grant MR/S016325/1 and ERC Advanced Grant 101020255.
creator: Joseph Hyde
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Joseph Hyde. In this paper, we study asymmetric Ramsey properties of the random graph G n , p G_{n,p} . Let r ∈ ℕ r\in\mathbb{N} and H 1 , … , H r H_{1},\ldots,H_{r} be graphs.

title: Islands in the Stream of Hawking Radiation
creator: Timothy J. Hollowood, S. Prem Kumar, Andrea Legramandi and Neil Talwar
description: Abstract We consider the island formula for the entropy of subsets of the Hawking radiation in the adiabatic limit where the black hole evaporation is very slow. We find a simple concrete ‘on-shell’ formula for the generalized entropy which involves the image of the island out in the stream of radiation, the ‘island in the stream’.

title: Ultra-Reliable Indoor Millimeter Wave Communications using Multiple Artificial Intelligence-Powered Intelligent Surfaces
creator: Mehdi Naderi Soorki 1 , Walid Saad 2,4 , Mehdi Bennis 3 , and Choong Seon Hong 4 1 Engineering Faculty, Shahid Chamran University of Ahvaz, Iran. 2 Wireless@VT, Bradley Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Virginia Tech, Blacksburg, VA, USA. 3 Centre for Wireless Communications, Univer
description: Abstract In this paper, a novel framework for guaranteeing ultra-reliable millimeter wave (mmW) communications using multiple artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) is proposed. The use of multiple AI-powered RISs allows changing the propagation direction of the signals transmitted from a mmW access point (AP) thereby improving coverage particularly for non-line-of-sight (NLoS) areas.

title: Nonperturbative quasiclassical theory of graphene photoconductivity
creator: S. A. Mikhailov
description: Abstract We present a nonperturbative quasi-classical theory of graphene photoconductivity. We consider the influence of low-frequency (microwave, terahertz, mid-infrared) radiation on the static conductivity of a uniform graphene layer and calculate its photoconductivity as a function of frequency, polarization and strength of the external ac electric field, as well as on the material properties (electron density, scattering time) and temperature.

title: 𝐇 𝜶 \boldsymbol{\mathrm{H^{\alpha}}} -flow of mean convex, complete graphical hypersurfaces
creator: Wolfgang Maurer
description: Abstract We consider the evolution of hypersurfaces in ℝ n + 1 \mathbb{R}^{n+1} with normal velocity given by a positive power of the mean curvature. The hypersurfaces under consideration are assumed to be strictly mean convex (positive mean curvature), complete, and given as the graph of a function.

title: Ringdown of Charged Compact Objects using Membrane Paradigm
creator: Mostafizur Rahman, Arpan Bhattacharyya
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Mostafizur Rahman, Arpan Bhattacharyya. Although black holes are an integral part of the standard model of astrophysics and cosmology, their existence poses some serious fundamental problems. In recent years, several horizonless compact object models were proposed to address those issues. As the gravitational wave detectors started to observe more and more merger events with a large signal-to-noise ratio, gravitational wave spectroscopy could hold the key to uncover the existence of these objects.

title: A Simple and General Debiased Machine Learning Theorem with Finite Sample Guarantees
creator: Victor Chernozhukov, Whitney K. Newey, Rahul Singh
description: Abstract Debiased machine learning is a meta algorithm based on bias correction and sample splitting to calculate confidence intervals for functionals, i.e. scalar summaries, of machine learning algorithms. For example, an analyst may desire the confidence interval for a treatment effect estimated with a neural network.

title: Zero-Shot Language Transfer vs Iterative Back Translation for Unsupervised Machine Translation
creator: Aviral Joshi, Chengzhi Huang, Har Simrat Singh
description: Abstract This work focuses on comparing different solutions for machine translation on low resource language pairs, namely, with zero-shot transfer learning and unsupervised machine translation. We discuss how the data size affects the performance of both unsupervised MT and transfer learning. Additionally we also look at how the domain of the data affects the result of unsupervised MT.

title: Analysis on Image Set Visual Question Answering
creator: Abhinav Khattar, Aviral Joshi, Har Simrat Singh, Pulkit Goel, Rohit Prakash Barnwal
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Abhinav Khattar, Aviral Joshi, Har Simrat Singh, Pulkit Goel, Rohit Prakash Barnwal. We tackle the challenge of Visual Question Answering in multi-image setting for the ISVQA dataset. Traditional VQA tasks have focused on a single-image setting where the target answer is generated from a single image. Image set VQA, however, comprises of a set of images and requires finding connection between images, relate the objects across images based on these connections and generate a unified answer.

title: Smooth convergence to the enveloping cylinder for mean curvature flow of complete graphical hypersurfaces
creator: Wolfgang Maurer
description: Abstract For a mean curvature flow of complete graphical hypersurfaces M t = graph u ⁡ ( ⋅ , t ) M_{t}=\mathop{\mathrm{graph}}u(\cdot,t) defined over domains Ω t \Omega_{t} , the enveloping cylinder is ∂ Ω t × ℝ \partial\Omega_{t}\times\mathbb{R} .

title: LIFT-SLAM: a deep-learning feature-based monocular visual SLAM method Journal: Neurocomputing
creator: Hudson Martins Silva Bruno, Esther Luna Colombini
description: Abstract The Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) problem addresses the possibility of a robot to localize itself in an unknown environment and simultaneously build a consistent map of this environment. Recently, cameras have been successfully used to get the environment’s features to perform SLAM, which is referred to as visual SLAM (VSLAM).

title: Approximation Schemes for Multiperiod Binary Knapsack Problems
creator: Zuguang Gao, John R. Birge, Varun Gupta
description: Abstract An instance of the multiperiod binary knapsack problem (MPBKP) is given by a horizon length T T , a non-decreasing vector of knapsack sizes ( c 1 , … , c T ) (c_{1},\ldots,c_{T}) where c t c_{t} denotes the cumulative size for periods 1 , … , t 1,\ldots,t , and a list of n n items.

title: High Power Backward Wave Oscillator using Folded Waveguide with Distributed Power Extraction Operating at an Exceptional Point
creator: Tarek Mealy, Ahmed F. Abdelshafy and Filippo Capolino
description: Abstract The concept of exceptional point of degeneracy (EPD) is used to conceive a degenerate synchronization regime that is able to enhance the level of output power and power conversion efficiency for backward wave oscillators (BWOs) operating at millimeter-wave and Terahertz frequencies.

title: Simulation of semiconductor detectors in 3D with SolidStateDetectors.jl
creator: and A.J. Zsigmond \note Corresponding author
description: Abstract The open-source software package SolidStateDetectors.jl to calculate the fields and simulate the drifts of charge carriers in solid state detectors, especially in large volume high-purity germanium detectors, together with the corresponding pulses, is introduced. The package can perform all calculations in full 3D while it can also make use of detector symmetries.

title: Misinformation detection in Luganda-English code-mixed social media text
creator: Peter Nabende, David Kabiito, Claire Babirye, Hewitt Tusiime, Joyce Nakatumba-Nabende
description: Abstract The increasing occurrence, forms, and negative effects of misinformation on social media platforms has necessitated more misinformation detection tools. Currently, work is being done addressing COVID-19 misinformation however, there are no misinformation detection tools for any of the 40 distinct indigenous Ugandan languages.

title: Adaptive Quantum Heat Engines
creator: M. Khanahmadi, A. T. Rezakhani
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by M. Khanahmadi, A. T. Rezakhani. For heat engines working between two heat baths, functionality is often conditioned on a set of fixed constraints such as given internal structure of the engine and given temperatures for the baths. It is, however, important to devise heat engines which can function adaptively, in particular when the engine is a quantum system and the baths are subject to fluctuations. Here we study a model for an adaptive quantum heat engine whose heat baths can have variable temperatures.

title: Universal information of critical quantum spin chains from wavefunction overlaps
creator: Yijian Zou
description: Abstract Given a critical quantum spin chain, we show how universal information about its quantum critical point can be extracted from wavefunction overlaps. More specifically, we consider overlap between low-energy eigenstates of the spin chain Hamiltonian with different boundary conditions, namely periodic boundary conditions and open boundary conditions.

title: Field-tunable interactions and frustration in underlayer-mediated artificial spin ice
creator: Susan Kempinger, Yu-Sheng Huang, Paul Lammert, Michael Vogel, Axel Hoffmann, Vincent H. Crespi, Peter Schiffer, Nitin Samarth
description: Abstract Artificial spin ice systems have opened experimental windows into a range of model magnetic systems through the control of interactions among nanomagnet moments. This control has previously been enabled by altering the nanomagnet size and the geometry of their placement.

title: A nonintrusive hybrid neural-physics modeling of incomplete dynamical systems: Lorenz equations
creator: Suraj Pawar, Omer San, Adil Rasheed, Ionel M. Navon
description: Abstract This work presents a hybrid modeling approach to data-driven learning and representation of unknown physical processes and closure parameterizations. These hybrid models are suitable for situations where the mechanistic description of dynamics of some variables is unknown, but reasonably accurate observational data can be obtained for the evolution of the state of the system.

title: Adversarial Heart Attack: Neural Networks Fooled to Segment Heart Symbols in Chest X-Ray Images
creator: Gerda Bortsova, Florian Dubost, Laurens Hogeweg, Ioannis Katramados, Marleen de Bruijne
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Gerda Bortsova, Florian Dubost, Laurens Hogeweg, Ioannis Katramados, Marleen de Bruijne. Adversarial attacks consist in maliciously changing the input data to mislead the predictions of automated decision systems and are potentially a serious threat for automated medical image analysis. Previous studies have shown that it is possible to adversarially manipulate automated segmentations produced by neural networks in a targeted manner in the white-box attack setting (assuming the full access to the target model).

title: Balancing Fairness and Efficiency in Traffic Routing via Interpolated Traffic Assignment
creator: Devansh Jalota, Kiril Solovey, Matthew Tsao, Stephen Zoepf, Marco Pavone
description: Abstract System optimum (SO) routing, wherein the total travel time of all users is minimized, is a holy grail for transportation authorities. However, SO routing may discriminate against users who incur much larger travel times than others to achieve high system efficiency, i.e., low total travel times.

title: High-order Barrier Functions: Robustness, Safety and Performance-Critical Control
creator: Xiao Tan, Wenceslao Shaw Cortez, Dimos V. Dimarogonas
description: Abstract In this paper, we propose a notion of high-order (zeroing) barrier functions that generalizes the concept of zeroing barrier functions and guarantees set forward invariance by checking their higher order derivatives. The proposed formulation guarantees asymptotic stability of the forward invariant set, which is highly favorable for robustness with respect to model perturbations.

title: The Atmospheric Ghost Correction
creator: Mariannne Cowherd, Isaaac Malsky
description: Abstract While the presence of ghosts has been known for decades, the impact of these apparitions on remote sensing observations has gone unquantified, leaving atmospheric corrections susceptible to ghosting. In this work, we present the first spectral characterization of three common ghost types and provide a framework for incorporating these properties into atmospheric correction algorithms.

title: Experimental verification of arcsine laws in mesoscopic non-equilibrium systems
creator: Raunak Dey, Avijit Kundu, Biswajit Das, Ayan Banerjee
description: Abstract A large number of processes in the mesoscopic world occur out of equilibrium, where the time course of a system evolution becomes immensely important since it is driven principally by dissipative effects. Non-equilibrium steady states (NESS) represent a crucial category in such systems, where relaxation timescales are comparable to the operational timescales.

title: Plasmonic enhancement of molecular hydrogen dissociation on metallic magnesium nanoclusters
creator: Oscar A. Douglas-Gallardo, Connor L. Box, Reinhard J. Maurer
description: Abstract Light-driven plasmonic enhancement of chemical reactions on metal catalysts is a promising strategy to achieve highly selective and efficient chemical transformations. The study of plasmonic catalyst materials has traditionally focused on late transition metals such as Au, Ag, and Cu.

title: Abstract
description: Abstract On the completeness of generalized eigenfunctions of the Hamiltonian of reggeon field theory in Bargmann space Abdelkader Intissar (1,2) (1) Equipe d’Analyse spectrale, UMR-CNRS n : 6134, Université de Corse, Quartier Grossetti, 20 250 Corté-France. E.mail : abdelkader.intissar@orange.fr (2) Le Prador,129, rue du commandant Rolland, 13008 Marseille-France.

title: One-point distribution of the geodesic in directed last passage percolation
creator: Zhipeng Liu
description: Abstract We consider the geodesic of the directed last passage percolation with iid exponential weights. We find the explicit one-point distribution of the geodesic location joint with the last passage times, and its limit as the parameters go to infinity under the KPZ scaling.

title: Hilbert transforms and the equidistribution of zeros of polynomials
creator: Emanuel Carneiro, Mithun Kumar Das, Alexandra Florea, Angel V. Kumchev, Amita Malik, Micah B. Milinovich, Caroline Turnage-Butterbaugh, and Jiuya Wang
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Emanuel Carneiro, Mithun Kumar Das, Alexandra Florea, Angel V. Kumchev, Amita Malik, Micah B. Milinovich, Caroline Turnage-Butterbaugh, and Jiuya Wang. We improve the current bounds for an inequality of Erdős and Turán from 1950 related to the discrepancy of angular equidistribution of the zeros of a given polynomial. Building upon a recent work of Soundararajan, we establish a novel connection between this inequality and an extremal problem in Fourier analysis involving the maxima of Hilbert transforms, for which we provide a complete solution.

title: Static spherically symmetric black holes in weak f ⁡ ( T ) f(\mdmathbb{T}) -gravity
creator: Christian Pfeifer 1 ID, Sebastian Schuster 2 ID
description: Abstract With the advent of gravitational wave astronomy and first pictures of the “shadow” of the central black hole of our milky way, theoretical analyses of black holes (and compact objects mimicking them sufficiently closely) have become more important than ever. The near future promises more and more detailed information about the observable black holes and black hole candidates.

title: Holographic Path-Integral Optimization
creator: Jan Boruch
description: Abstract In this work we elaborate on holographic description of the path-integral optimization in conformal field theories (CFT) using Hartle-Hawking wave functions in Anti-de Sitter spacetimes. We argue that the maximization of the Hartle-Hawking wave function is equivalent to the path-integral optimization procedure in CFT.

title: Cubic rational expressions over a finite field
creator: Sandro Mattarei, Marco Pizzato
description:
A 2021 arXiv research paper by Sandro Mattarei, Marco Pizzato. We study and partially classify cubic rational expressions g ⁡ ( x ) / h ⁡ ( x ) g(x)/h(x) over a finite field 𝔽 q \mathbb{F}_{q} , up to pre- and post-composition with independent Möbius transformations. In particular, we obtain a full classification when q q is even, and prove an upper bound of 4 ​ q 4q for the number of equivalence classes when q q is odd. 2000 Mathematics Subject Classification

title: Effects of Causes and Causes of Effects Journal: Xxxx. Xxx. Xxx. Xxx. DOI: 10.1146/((please add article doi))
creator: A. Philip Dawid 1 and Monica Musio 2
description: Abstract We describe and contrast two distinct problem areas for statistical causality: studying the likely effects of an intervention (“effects of causes”), and studying whether there is a causal link between the observed exposure and outcome in an individual case (“causes of effects”).

title: IMPLICATIONS OF DYNAMICAL DARK ENERGY IN THE EXPANSION OF THE UNIVERSE AND THE STRUCTURE FORMATION
creator: Javier de Cruz Pérez
description: Abstract Implications of Dynamical Dark Energy in the expansion of the Universe and the Structure Formation by Javier de Cruz Pérez A dissertation submitted in fulfillment of the requirements for the degree of Doctor per la Universitat de Barcelona . PhD program in Physics. Line of research: Particle Physics and Gravitation.

title: Showing Academic Performance Predictions during Term Planning: Effects on Students’ Decisions, Behaviors, and Preferences Conference: CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems; May 8–13, 2021; Yokohama, Japan CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI ’21), May 8–13, 2021,
creator: Gonzalo Gabriel Méndez, Luis Galárraga, Katherine Chiluiza
description: Abstract . Course selection is a crucial activity for students as it directly impacts their workload and performance. It is also time-consuming, prone to subjectivity, and often carried out based on incomplete information. This task can, nevertheless, be assisted with computational tools, for instance, by predicting performance based on historical data.

title: Dynamics and Statistical Mechanics of Closed Composite Multi-Level University and Scientific Hierarchical Systems Pertaining to the Undergraduate and Graduate Student Phenomena
creator: Jason Garver
description: Abstract Content: Qualitative and ad-hoc descriptions of observations of the “undergraduate” and “graduate” effects. Comparisons between the classical models of both undergraduate and graduate systems separately lead to the conclusion that a quantized model is inevitably required to explain certain effects such as “Spooky Action At A Seminar” and the FTR (Food Travel Ratio) among other select observed phenomena.

title: Asymptotic factorization of n-particle 𝑺 ​ 𝑼 ​ ( 𝑵 ) SU(N) form factors
creator: Hrachya M. Babujian, Angela Foerster, and Michael Karowski
description: Abstract We investigate the high energy behavior of the S ​ U ​ ( N ) SU(N) chiral Gross-Neveu model in 1 + 1 1+1 dimensions. The model is integrable and matrix elements of several local operators (form factors) are known exactly.

title: Scalable Visual Attribute Extraction through Hidden Layers of a Residual ConvNet
creator: Andres Baloian DCC-University of Chile Av. Beauchef 851, Santiago, Chile abaloian@dcc.uchile.cl, Nils Murrugarra-Llerena Snap Research 2772 D. Douglas L. N, S. Monica, CA, US nmurrugarraller@snap.com, Jose M. Saavedra Impresee Inc. 600 California, San Francisco, US jose.saavedra@impresee.com
description: Abstract Visual attributes play an essential role in real applications based on image retrieval. For instance, the extraction of attributes from images allows an eCommerce search engine to produce retrieval results with higher precision. The traditional manner to build an attribute extractor is by training a convnet-based classifier with a fixed number of classes.

title: Preliminary Analysis of Planetary Characteristics, Dynamics, and Climates from the Systems Alliance Planetary Survey Catalogue numpy ( Harris et al. 2020 ) , Forecaster ( Chen & Kipping 2017 ) , SPOCK ( Tamayo et al. 2020 ) Rebound ( Rein & Liu 2012 ) astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ; As
creator: Alysa Obertas, Adiv Paradise
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Alysa Obertas, Adiv Paradise. Just a few decades after the discovery of the Charon Relay, and the ensuing First Contact War, relatively little is known about the population of planets linked by the Prothean mass relays. Understanding the nature of these systems and how they may differ from the broader population of planetary systems in our galaxy is key to both continued human habitation across the broader Galaxy, as well as to our understanding of the Prothean civilization.

title: Adaptive Configuration of In Situ Lossy Compression for Cosmology Simulations via Fine-Grained Rate-Quality Modeling Conference: Proceedings of the 30th International Symposium on High-Performance Parallel and Distributed Computing; June 21–25, 2021; Virtual Event, Sweden Proceedings of the 30th Int
creator: Sian Jin, Jesus Pulido, Pascal Grosset, Jiannan Tian, Dingwen Tao, James Ahrens
description: Abstract . Extreme-scale cosmological simulations have been widely used by today’s researchers and scientists on leadership supercomputers. A new generation of error-bounded lossy compressors has been used in workflows to reduce storage requirements and minimize the impact of throughput limitations while saving large snapshots of high-fidelity data for post-hoc analysis.

title: Visual Attention in Imaginative Agents
creator: Samrudhdhi B. Rangrej, James J. Clark
description: Abstract We present a recurrent agent who perceives surroundings through a series of discrete fixations. At each timestep, the agent imagines a variety of plausible scenes consistent with the fixation history. The next fixation is planned using uncertainty in the content of the imagined scenes.

title: Studying Ad Library Integration Strategies of Top Free-to-Download Apps
creator: Md Ahasanuzzaman, Member, IEEE, Safwat Hassan, Member, IEEE, Ahmed E. Hassan, Fellow, IEEE
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Md Ahasanuzzaman, Member, IEEE, Safwat Hassan, Member, IEEE, Ahmed E. Hassan, Fellow, IEEE. In-app advertisements have become a major revenue source for app developers in the mobile app ecosystem. Ad libraries play an integral part in this ecosystem as app developers integrate these libraries into their apps to display ads. In this paper, we study ad library integration strategies by analyzing 35,459 updates of 1,837 top free-to-download apps of the Google Play Store.

title: Online Learning Probabilistic Event Calculus Theories in Answer Set Programming
creator: NIKOS KATZOURIS 1, ALEXANDER ARTIKIS 2,1 and GEORGIOS PALIOURAS 1, 1 Institute of Informatics & Telecommunications, National Center for Scientific Research (NCSR) “Demokritos”, Athens, Greece 2 Department of Maritime Studies, University of Piraeus, Piraeus, Greece
description: Abstract Complex Event Recognition (CER) systems detect event occurrences in streaming time-stamped input using predefined event patterns. Logic-based approaches are of special interest in CER, since, via Statistical Relational AI, they combine uncertainty-resilient reasoning with time and change, with machine learning, thus alleviating the cost of manual event pattern authoring.

title: Training Multi-bit Quantized and Binarized Networks withA Learnable Symmetric Quantizer
creator: Phuoc Pham, Jacob A. Abraham, Jaeyong Chung
description: Abstract Quantizing weights and activations of deep neural networks is essential for deploying them in resource-constrained devices, or cloud platforms for at-scale services. While binarization is a special case of quantization, this extreme case often leads to several training difficulties, and necessitates specialized models and training methods.

title: TransMOT: Spatial-Temporal Graph Transformer for Multiple Object Tracking
creator: Peng Chu, Jiang Wang, Quanzeng You, Haibin Ling, Zicheng Liu
description: Abstract Tracking multiple objects in videos relies on modeling the spatial-temporal interactions of the objects. In this paper, we propose a solution named TransMOT , which leverages powerful graph transformers to efficiently model the spatial and temporal interactions among the objects.

title: Are Bias Mitigation Techniques for Deep Learning Effective?
creator: Robik Shrestha, Kushal Kafle, Christopher Kanan, Rochester Institute of Technology, Adobe Research, Cornell Tech {rss9369, kk6055, kanan}@rit.edu
description: Abstract A critical problem in deep learning is that systems learn inappropriate biases, resulting in their inability to perform well on minority groups. This has led to the creation of multiple algorithms that endeavor to mitigate bias. However, it is not clear how effective these methods are.

title: Modular Tree Network for Source Code Representation Learning DOI: 10.1145/1122445.1122456 Journal: JACM Volume: 37 4 111 8 CCS: Software and its engineering Software creation and management
creator: Wenhan Wang, Ge Li, Sijie Shen, Xin Xia, Zhi Jin
description: Abstract . Learning representation for source code is a foundation of many program analysis tasks. In recent years, neural networks have already shown success in this area, but most existing models did not make full use of the unique structural information of programs.

title: Packed words and quotient rings
creator: Daniël Kroes and Brendon Rhoades
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Daniël Kroes and Brendon Rhoades. The coinvariant algebra is a quotient of the polynomial ring ℚ ⁡ [ x 1 , … , x n ] \mathbb{Q}[x_{1},\ldots,x_{n}] whose algebraic properties are governed by the combinatorics of permutations of length n n . A word w = w 1 ​ … ​ w n w=w_{1}\dots w_{n} over the positive integers is packed if whenever i > 2 i>2 appears as a letter of w w , so does i − 1 i-1 .

title: Unsupervised Person Re-identification via Simultaneous Clustering and Consistency Learning
creator: Junhui Yin, Jiayan Qiu, Siqing Zhang, Jiyang Xie, Zhanyu Ma, Jun Guo
description: Abstract Unsupervised person re-identification (re-ID) has become an important topic due to its potential to resolve the scalability problem of supervised re-ID models. However, existing methods simply utilize pseudo labels from clustering for supervision and thus have not yet fully explored the semantic information in data itself, which limits representation capabilities of learned models.

title: Radar Human Motion Classification Using Multi-Antenna System
creator: Patrick A Schooley, Syed A. Hamza
description: Abstract This paper considers human activity classification for an indoor radar system. Human motions generate nonstationary radar returns which represent Doppler and micro-Doppler signals. The time-frequency (TF) analysis of micro-Doppler signals can discern subtle variations on the motion by precisely revealing velocity components of various moving body parts.

title: Active plasmon interference control on ultrafast time scales by free electrons
creator: Rong Huang, Weiwei Luo, Wei Wu, Mengxin Ren, Xinzheng Zhang, Wei Cai, Jingjun Xu
description: Abstract Interference between light waves is one of the widely known phenomena in physics, which is widely used in modern optics, ranging from precise detection at the nanoscale to gravitational-wave observation. Akin to light, both classical and quantum interferences between surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) have been demonstrated.

title: The k k -Colorable Unit Disk Cover Problem Journal: DAM
creator: Monith S. Reyunuru, Kriti Jethlia, Manjanna Basappa
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Monith S. Reyunuru, Kriti Jethlia, Manjanna Basappa. In this article, we consider colorable variations of the Unit Disk Cover ( UDC ) problem as follows. k k -Colorable Discrete Unit Disk Cover ( k k -CDUDC) : Given a set P P of n n points, and a set D D of m m unit disks (of radius=1), both lying in the plane, and a parameter k k , the objective is to compute a set D ′ ⊆ D D^{\prime}\subseteq D such that

title: The Effect of Thermal Pressure on Collisionless Magnetic Reconnection Rate Journal: ApJ
creator: Xiaocan Li, Yi-Hsin Liu
description: Abstract Modeling collisionless magnetic reconnection rate is an outstanding challenge in basic plasma physics research. While the seemingly universal rate of an order 𝒪 ⁡ ( 0.1 ) \mathcal{O}(0.1) is often reported in the low- β \beta regime, it is not clear how reconnection rate scales with a higher plasma β \beta .

title: Describing traveler choice behavior using the free utility model
creator: Hao Wang, Xiao-Yong Yan
description: Abstract Travel demand forecasting is an essential part of transportation planning and management. The four-step travel model is the traditional and most-common procedure utilized for travel demand forecasting, and many models have been proposed in the literature to describe each step separately.

title: The topological order of the space Essay written for the Gravity Research Foundation 2021 Awards for Essays on Gravitation.
creator: Jingbo Wang
description: Abstract Topological order is a new type order that beyond Landau’s symmetry breaking theory. The topological entanglement entropy provides a universal quantum number to characterize the topological order in a system. The topological entanglement entropy of the BTZ black hole was calculated and found that it coincides with that for fractional quantum Hall state.

title: DF 2 AM: Dual-level Feature Fusion and Affinity Modeling for RGB-Infrared Cross-modality Person Re-identification
creator: Junhui Yin, Zhanyu Ma, Jiyang Xie, Shibo Nie, Kongming Liang, Jun Guo
description: Abstract RGB-infrared person re-identification is a challenging task due to the intra-class variations and cross-modality discrepancy. Existing works mainly focus on learning modality-shared global representations by aligning image styles or feature distributions across modalities, while local feature from body part and relationships between person images are largely neglected. In this paper, we propose a Dual-level (i.e.

title: Multilingual and code-switching ASR challenges for low resource Indian languages
creator: Anuj Diwan, Rakesh Vaideeswaran, Sanket Shah, Ankita Singh, Srinivasa Raghavan, Shreya Khare, Vinit Unni, Saurabh Vyas, Akash Rajpuria, Chiranjeevi Yarra, Ashish Mittal, Prasanta Kumar Ghosh, Preethi Jyothi, Kalika Bali, Vivek Seshadri, Sunayana Sitaram, Samarth Bharadwaj, Jai Nanavati, Raoul Nanava
description: Abstract Recently, there is increasing interest in multilingual automatic speech recognition (ASR) where a speech recognition system caters to multiple low resource languages by taking advantage of low amounts of labeled corpora in multiple languages. With multilingualism becoming common in today’s world, there has been increasing interest in code-switching ASR as well.

title: Multiparameter quantum metrology using strongly interacting spin systems
creator: Min Jiang, Yunlan Ji, Qing Li, Ran Liu, Dieter Suter, Xinhua Peng
description: Abstract Interacting quantum systems are attracting increasing interest for developing precise metrology. In particular, the realisation that quantum-correlated states and the dynamics of interacting systems can lead to entirely new and unexpected phenomena have initiated an intense research effort to explore interaction-based metrology both theoretically and experimentally.

title: Evaporation of black holes in flat space entangled with an auxiliary universe Preprint: UT-Komaba/21-3, YITP-21-27
creator: ​ Akihiro Miyata, ​ Tomonori Ugajin
description: Abstract We study a thermofield double type entangled state on two disjoint universes A A and B B , where one of the universes is asymptotically flat containing a black hole. As we increase the entanglement temperature, this black hole receives back-reaction from the stress energy tensor of the state.

title: Temperature of superconducting transition for very strong coupling in antiadiabatic limit of Eliashberg equations
creator: M. V. Sadovskii
description: Abstract It is shown that the famous Allen – Dynes asymtotic limit for superconducting transition temperature in very strong coupling region T c > 1 2 ​ π ​ λ ​ Ω 0 T_{c}>\frac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\lambda}\Omega_{0} (where λ ≫ 1 \lambda\gg 1 – is Eliashberg – McMillan electron – phonon coupling constant and Ω 0 \Omega_{0} – the characteristic frequency of phonons)

title: Pinpointing the Memory Behaviors of DNN Training Thanks: This work is supported by the National Key R&D Program of China (under Grant No. 2017YFB1003103) and the Science Fund for Creative Research Groups of the National Natural Science Foundation of China (under Grant No. 61521092).
creator: Jiansong Li †‡ , Xiao Dong ∗ , Guangli Li †‡ , Peng Zhao ¶ , Xueying Wang †‡ , Xiaobing Chen †‡ , Xianzhi Yu ¶ , Yongxin Yang †‡ , Zihan Jiang †‡ , Wei Cao † , Lei Liu † , Xiaobing Feng †‡
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jiansong Li †‡ , Xiao Dong ∗ , Guangli Li †‡ , Peng Zhao ¶ , Xueying Wang †‡ , Xiaobing Chen †‡ , Xianzhi Yu ¶ , Yongxin Yang †‡ , Zihan Jiang †‡ , Wei Cao † , Lei Liu † , Xiaobing Feng †‡. The training of deep neural networks (DNNs) is usually memory-hungry due to the limited device memory capacity of DNN accelerators. Characterizing the memory behaviors of DNN training is critical to optimize the device memory pressures.

title: Intrusive and non-intrusive reduced order modeling of the rotating thermal shallow water equation
creator: Süleyman Yıldız, Bülent Karasözen, Murat Uzunca
description: Abstract In this paper, we investigate projection-based intrusive and data-driven non-intrusive model order reduction methods in numerical simulation of rotating thermal shallow water equation (RTSWE) in parametric and non-parametric form. Discretization of the RTSWE in space with centered finite differences leads to Hamiltonian system of ordinary differential equations with linear and quadratic terms.

title: Dive into Ambiguity: Latent Distribution Mining and Pairwise Uncertainty Estimation for Facial Expression Recognition
creator: Jiahui She ∗1,2 Yibo Hu ∗2 Hailin Shi 2 Jun Wang 2 Qiu Shen †1 Tao Mei 2 1 Nanjing University 2 JD AI Research jh.she@foxmail.com, huyibo871079699@gmail.com, {wangjun492, shihailin}@jd.com shenqiu@nju.edu.cn, tmei@live.com
description: Abstract Due to the subjective annotation and the inherent inter-class similarity of facial expressions, one of key challenges in Facial Expression Recognition (FER) is the annotation ambiguity. In this paper, we proposes a solution, named DMUE, to address the problem of annotation ambiguity from two perspectives: the latent D istribution M ining and the pairwise U ncertainty E stimation.

title: Deep Contrastive Patch-Based Subspace Learning for Camera Image Signal Processing
creator: Yunhao Yang, Yi Wang, Chandrajit Bajaj
description: Abstract Camera Image Signal Processing(ISP) pipelines can get appealing results in different image signal processing tasks. Nonetheless, the majority of these methods, including those employing an encoder-decoder deep architecture for the task, typically utilize a uniform filter applied consistently across the entire image.

title: Hydrogel sphere impact cratering, spreading and bouncing on granular media
creator: Xiaoyan Ye 1 and Devaraj van der Meer 2
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Xiaoyan Ye 1 and Devaraj van der Meer 2. The impact of a hydrogel sphere onto a granular target results in both the deformation of the sphere and the formation of a prominent topographic feature known as impact crater on the granular surface.

title: Speedup of nuclear-spin diffusion in hyperpolarized solids
creator: Yu Wang, Kazuyuki Takeda
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Yu Wang, Kazuyuki Takeda. We propose a correction to the coefficient of nuclear-spin diffusion by a factor 1 / 1 − p ¯ 2 1/\sqrt{1-\overline{p}^{2}} , where p ¯ \overline{p} is the average nuclear-spin polarization. The correction, derived by extending the Lowe-Gade theory to low-temperature cases, implies that transportation of nuclear magnetization through nuclear-spin diffusion accelerates when the system is hyperpolarized, whereas for low-polarization the correction factor approaches unity and the diffusion coefficient coincides with the conventional diffusion coefficient valid in the high-temperature limit.

title: Optimal driving strategies for a fleet of trains on level track with prescribed intermediate signal times and safe separation
creator: Phil Howlett, Peter Pudney, Amie Albrecht
description: Abstract We propose an analytic solution to the problem of finding optimal driving strategies that minimize total tractive energy consumption for a fleet of trains travelling on the same track in the same direction subject to clearance-time equality constraints that ensure safe separation and compress the line-occupancy timespan.

title: On the difference between a D. H. Lehmer number and its inverse over short interval 0 0 footnotetext: 1.nyn0902@mail.nwpu.edu.cn 2.marong@nwpu.edu.cn 3.2805256907@qq.com
creator: Yana Niu, Rong Ma, Haodong Wang School of Mathematics and Statistics, Northwestern Polytechnical University Xi’an, Shaanxi, 710072, People’s Republic of China
description: Abstract Abstract Let q>2 be an odd integer. For each integer x with 0<x<q and (q,x)=1 , we know that there exists one and only one \bar{x} with 0<\bar{x}<q such that x\bar{x}\equiv 1(\bmod q) . A Lehmer number is defined to be any integer a with 2{\dagger}(a+\bar{a}) . For any nonnegative integer k , Let M(x,q,k)=\displaystyle\mathop{\displaystyle\mathop{\sum{{}^{\prime}}}_{a=1}^{q}\displaystyle\mathop{\sum{{}^{\prime}}}_{b\leq xq}}_{\mbox{\tiny$\begin{array}[]{c}2|a+b+1\\ ab\equiv 1(\bmod q)\end{array}$}}(a-b)^{2k}.

title: Detecting over/under-translation errors for determining adequacy in human translations
creator: Prabhakar Gupta, Ridha Juneja, Anil Nelakanti, Tamojit Chatterjee
description: Abstract We present a novel approach to detecting over and under translations (OT/UT) as part of adequacy error checks in translation evaluation. We do not restrict ourselves to machine translation (MT) outputs and specifically target applications with human generated translation pipeline. The goal of our system is to identify OT/UT errors from human translated video subtitles with high error recall.

title: Point-free Construction of Real Exponentiation
creator: Ming Ng ORCID:0000-0002-2170-0247, Steven Vickers ORCID:0000-0003-1907-9014
description: Abstract . We define a point-free construction of real exponentiation and logarithms, i.e. we construct the maps exp : ( 0 , ∞ ) × ℝ → ( 0 , ∞ ) , ( x , ζ ) ↦ x ζ \exp\colon(0,\infty)\times\mathbb{R}\rightarrow\!

title: Fast Jacobian-Vector Product for Deep Networks
creator: Randall Balestriero, Richard G. Baraniuk
description: Abstract Jacobian-vector products (JVPs) form the backbone of many recent developments in Deep Networks (DNs), with applications including faster constrained optimization, regularization with generalization guarantees, and adversarial example sensitivity assessments. Unfortunately, JVPs are computationally expensive for real world DN architectures and require the use of automatic differentiation to avoid manually adapting the JVP program when changing the DN architecture.

title: Bench-top Cooling of a Microwave Mode using an Optically Pumped Spin Refrigerator
creator: Hao Wu, Shamil Mirkhanov, Wern Ng, Mark Oxborrow
description: Abstract We experimentally demonstrate the temporary removal of thermal photons from a microwave mode at 1.45 GHz through its interaction with the spin-polarized triplet states of photo-excited pentacene molecules doped within a p -terphenyl crystal at room temperature. The crystal functions electromagnetically as a narrow-band cryogenic load, removing photons from the otherwise room-temperature mode via stimulated absorption.

title: Full-Duplex mmWave Massive MIMO Systems: A Joint Hybrid Precoding/Combining and Self-Interference Cancellation Design
creator: Asil Koc, Tho Le-Ngoc
description: Abstract Millimeter-wave (mmWave) massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems have been considered as one of the primary candidates for the fifth generation (5G) and beyond 5G wireless communication networks to satisfy the ever-increasing capacity demands. Full-duplex technology can further enhance the advantages of mmWave massive MIMO systems. However, the strong self-interference (SI) is the major limiting factor in the full-duplex technology.

title: Unsupervised Domain Expansion for Visual Categorization Journal: TOMM CCS: Computing methodologies Scene understanding CCS: Computing methodologies Object detection CCS: Computing methodologies Transfer learning
creator: Jie Wang, Kaibin Tian, Dayong Ding, Gang Yang, Xirong Li
description: Abstract . Expanding visual categorization into a novel domain without the need of extra annotation has been a long-term interest for multimedia intelligence. Previously, this challenge has been approached by unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA). Given labeled data from a source domain and unlabeled data from a target domain, UDA seeks for a deep representation that is both discriminative and domain-invariant.

title: Convergence of group actions in metric measure geometry Thanks: This work was supported by JSPS KAKENHI Grant Number 19K03459 and 19J10866.
creator: Hiroki Nakajima, Takashi Shioya
description: Abstract . We generalize the box and observable distances to those between metric measure spaces with group actions, and prove some fundamental properties. As an application, we obtain an example of a sequence of lens spaces with unbounded dimension converging to the cone of the infinite-dimensional complex projective space. Our idea is to use the theory of mass-transport.

title: Statistical Significance Revisited
creator: Maike Tormählen, Galiya Klinkova, Michael Grabinski *
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Maike Tormählen, Galiya Klinkova, Michael Grabinski *. Statistical significance measures the reliability of a result obtained from a random experiment. We investigate the number of repetitions needed for a statistical result to have a certain significance. In the first step, we consider binomially distributed variables in the example of medication testing with fixed placebo efficacy, asking how many experiments are needed in order to achieve a significance of 95%.

title: Many-to-English Machine Translation Tools, Data, and Pretrained Models
creator: Thamme Gowda, Zhao Zhang, Chris A Mattmann, Jonathan May
description: Abstract While there are more than 7000 languages in the world, most translation research efforts have targeted a few high resource languages. Commercial translation systems support only one hundred languages or fewer, and do not make these models available for transfer to low resource languages.

title: Retrofitting Effect Handlers onto OCaml DOI: 10.1145/3453483.3454039 pldi21main-p82-p ISBN: 978-1-4503-8391-2/21/06 Conference: Proceedings of the 42nd ACM SIGPLAN International Conference on Programming Language Design and Implementation; June 20–25, 2021; Virtual, Canada Proceedings of the 42nd AC
creator: KC Sivaramakrishnan, Stephen Dolan, Leo White, Tom Kelly, Sadiq Jaffer, Anil Madhavapeddy
description: Abstract . Effect handlers have been gathering momentum as a mechanism for modular programming with user-defined effects. Effect handlers allow for non-local control flow mechanisms such as generators, async/await, lightweight threads and coroutines to be composably expressed. We present a design and evaluate a full-fledged efficient implementation of effect handlers for OCaml, an industrial-strength multi-paradigm programming language.

title: Evaluating Neural Word Embeddings for Sanskrit
creator: Jivnesh Sandhan 1, Om Adideva 2 , Digumarthi Komal 1 ,
description: Abstract Recently, the supervised learning paradigm’s surprisingly remarkable performance has garnered considerable attention from Sanskrit Computational Linguists. As a result, the Sanskrit community has put laudable efforts to build task-specific labeled data for various downstream Natural Language Processing (NLP) tasks. The primary component of these approaches comes from representations of word embeddings.

title: New Constraints on Lorentz Invariance Violation from Combined Linear and Circular Optical Polarimetry of Extragalactic Sources
creator: Roman Gerasimov *, Praneet Bhoj *, Fabian Kislat *
description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Roman Gerasimov *, Praneet Bhoj *, Fabian Kislat *. Expanding on our prior efforts to search for Lorentz invariance violation (LIV) using the linear optical polarimetry of extragalactic objects, we propose a new method that combines linear and circular polarization measurements. While existing work has focused on the tendency of LIV to reduce the linear polarization degree, this new method additionally takes into account the coupling between photon helicities induced by some models.

title: The Compact Support Neural Network
creator: Adrian Barbu *, Hongyu Mou
description: Abstract Neural networks are popular and useful in many fields, but they have the problem of giving high confidence responses for examples that are away from the training data. This makes the neural networks very confident in their prediction while making gross mistakes, thus limiting their reliability for safety-critical applications such as autonomous driving, space exploration, etc.

title: A unified approach to hypergraph stability Thanks: The first and second author’s research is partially supported by NSF awards DMS-1763317 and DMS-1952767.
creator: Xizhi Liu, Dhruv Mubayi, Christian Reiher
description: Abstract . We present a method which provides a unified framework for most stability theorems that have been proved in graph and hypergraph theory. Our main result reduces stability for a large class of hypergraph problems to the simpler question of checking that a hypergraph ℋ \mathcal{H} with large minimum degree that omits the forbidden structures is vertex-extendable.

title: Modeling High-order Interactions across Multi-interests for Micro-video Recommendation (Student Abstract)
creator: Dong Yao, Shengyu Zhang, Zhou Zhao, Wenyan Fan, Jieming Zhu, Xiuqiang He, Fei Wu
description: Abstract Personalized recommendation system has become pervasive in various video platform. Many effective methods have been proposed, but most of them didn’t capture the user’s multi-level interest trait and dependencies between their viewed micro-videos well. To solve these problems, we propose a Self-over-Co Attention module to enhance user’s interest representation.

title: Two dimensional interacting Bose-Bose droplet in random repulsive potential
creator: Saswata Sahu, Dwipesh Majumder
description: Abstract We have studied the effect of time-independent repulsive random impurity potential on the quantum droplets of Bose-Einstein condensation of two different species of Bose atoms in two dimensions. We have solved the Gross-Pitaevskii equation to get the density profile and the energy of the condensate.

title: Measuring Masses and Radii of Neutron Stars in Low-Mass X-ray Binaries: Effects of Atmospheric Composition and Touchdown Radius
creator: Myungkuk Kim, Young-Min Kim, Kwang Hyun Sung, Chang-Hwan Lee, Kyujin Kwak
description: Abstract Context. X-ray bursts (XRBs) are energetic explosive events which have been observed in low-mass X-ray binaries (LMXBs). Some Type-I XRBs show photospheric radius expansion (PRE) and these PRE XRBs are used to simultaneously estimate the mass and the radius of a neutron star in LMXB. Aims.

title: Linear polarization–direction correlations in γ \gamma -ray scattering experiments
creator: Christian Iliadis, Udo Friman-Gayer
description: Abstract Scattering measurements with incident linearly polarized γ \gamma rays provide information on spins, parities, and γ \gamma -ray multipolarity mixing coefficients, and, therefore, on the nuclear matrix elements involved in the transitions. We present the general formalism for analyzing the observed angular correlations.

title: Training Medical Communication Skills with Virtual Patients: Literature Review and Directions for Future Research
creator: Edoardo Battegazzorre, Andrea Bottino, Fabrizio Lamberti
description: Abstract Effective communication is a crucial skill for healthcare provi-ders since it leads to better patient health, satisfaction and avoids malpractice claims. In standard medical education, students’ communication skills are trained with role-playing and Standardized Patients (SPs), i.e., actors. However, SPs are difficult to standardize, and are very resource consuming.
